body.text: Muktā-caritram
body.translated_text: <s>Muktā-caritram</s> (The Story of Pearls)

body.text: namaḥ śrī-gāndharvikā-giridharābhyām
body.translated_text: Obeisance to <s>Śrī Gāndharvikā</s> and <s>Giridhara</s> (the divine couple <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>).

children.translated_text: Charming as ten million <s>Kandarpas</s> (Cupids), with the splendor of a radiant blue lotus,
whose pastime is the enchantment of the world — obeisance to the son of the chief of cowherds (<s>Gopendra-sūnu</s>).
In the ocean of the sport of buying and selling pearls, where both are immersed,
each seeking victory over the other — I worship the pair, <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Mādhava</s>.
To bestow upon the earth the nectar of his own radiant <s>bhakti</s> (devotion),

children.text: uditaṃ taṃ śacī-garbha-vyomni pūrṇaṃ vidhuṃ bhaje ||
children.translated_text: risen in the sky of <s>Śacī</s>'s womb, a full moon — him I worship.

children.text: nāma-śreṣṭhaṃ manum api śacīputram atra svarūpaṃ
children.translated_text: The supreme holy name, the <s>mantra</s>, the son of <s>Śacī</s> — his own form,
<s>Śrī Rūpa</s>, his elder brother (<s>Sanātana</s>), the great city of <s>Mathurā</s>, the pasture-lands,
<s>Rādhā-kuṇḍa</s>, the great mountain (<s>Govardhana</s>), and the hope of [meeting] <s>Rādhikā</s> and <s>Mādhava</s> —

children.text: prāpto yasya prathita-kṛpayā śrī-guruṃ taṃ nato'smi ||
children.translated_text: all that I have obtained by the renowned mercy of my <s>Śrī Guru</s> — to him I bow.
The waves of the nectar of <s>Hari</s>'s pastimes, which have become the ocean of the waters of the <s>Vṛndā</s> forest —
may we expand them, full of <s>rasa</s>, for the supreme bliss of the assembly of the divine ones.

body.text: ekadā kiñcin-mātra-śruta-pūrva-vṛttāntayā satyabhāmayā kṛṣṇaḥ sākūtaṃ pṛṣṭaḥ |
body.translated_text: Once, <s>Satyabhāmā</s>, who had heard only slightly of the previous events, pointedly asked <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>:

children.text: latās tā madhurāḥ kasmin jāyante dhanyanivṛti |
children.translated_text: 'In what [garden] do those sweet creepers grow, O blessed one of fulfilled joy,
O Lord, whose fruit is the pearl-fruit placed upon my bracelets?'

body.text:
* This verse is quoted in UN 11.66 as an example of maugdhya. There the first line
reads:
kās tā latāḥ kva vā santi kena vā kila ropitāḥ
body.translated_text: * This verse is quoted in UN 11.66 as an example of <s>maugdhya</s> (charming naivety). There the first line reads: 'What are those creepers? Where do they grow? And by whom were they planted?'

body.text: tatas tad-vṛttānta-smaraṇāt kṛṣṇaḥ svāntar-glānir bahir vihasyāha |
body.translated_text: Then <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, feeling internal distress from the recollection of those events, but outwardly laughing, said:

children.text: gataḥ sa kālo yatrāsīt muktānāṃ janma valliṣu |
children.translated_text: 'Gone is that time when pearls were born on creepers;
now their causes are the caskets of oyster-shells.'

body.text:
tatas tad apūrvaṃ śrutvā sa-viśeṣa-śravaṇotkaṇṭhitayā tayā bāḍham āmreḍitaḥ
kṛṣṇaḥ punar āha | ekadā kārttike māsi gokule govardhana-girau
dīpa-mālikā-mahotsava āsīt | tatra sarvo jano vicitra-nepathya-sāmagrīṇāṃ
saṃskārāya sādhanāya ca paramāśakto babhūva | gopās tu svaṃ svaṃ bhūṣayanto'pi
viśeṣataḥ gavādi-paśūnāṃ prasādhanārtham udyuktā āsan | gopyaḥ kila
prasādhita-sadanā ātmanāṃ bhūṣaṇārthaṃ nānālaṅkāra-saṃskāra-sādhana-parā
babhūvuḥ | rādhā tu mālya-haraṇākhya-saras-tīropānta-mādhavī-catuḥ-śālikāyāṃ
sva-sakhī-samudayena paramottama-muktābhir vividha-bhūṣaṇāni racayitum
ārebhe |
body.translated_text: Then, hearing that unprecedented [account], with eagerness to hear more in detail, she repeatedly pressed him, and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> again spoke: 'Once, in the month of <s>Kārttika</s>, in <s>Gokula</s>, on <s>Govardhana</s> hill, there was the great festival of the row of lamps (<s>Dīpamālikā</s>). There, all the people were supremely engaged in the preparation and procurement of various costume materials. The cowherds, while adorning themselves, were especially busy in decorating their cows and other cattle. The <s>gopīs</s>, having beautified their homes, were wholly devoted to the preparation of various ornamental crafts for adorning themselves. <s>Rādhā</s>, however, in a bower of four <s>mādhavī</s> creepers on the bank of the lake called <s>Mālya-haraṇa</s>, began, with her company of friends, to fashion various ornaments from the finest pearls.'

children.text: mayā ca vicakṣaṇa iti yathārtha-nāma-kīra-kumāra-mukhatas tan niśamya
children.translated_text: 'And I, having heard about that through the mouth of the young parrot named <s>Vicakṣaṇa</s> (Clever) — a name most fitting —

children.text: sa-kautukaṃ tatra gatvātipremāspadasya haṃsī-hariṇīti nāmno dhenu-yugalasya
children.translated_text: went there with curiosity, and out of eagerness to adorn a pair of cows named <s>Haṃsī</s> and <s>Hariṇī</s> (Swan and Doe), supremely dear [to me],

children.text: bhūṣaṇautsukyena tāsāṃ sakāśe mauktikāni prārthitāni || tataḥ
children.translated_text: I requested pearls from them.' Then —

body.text:
suvividha-vaidagdhya-parimala-parilasita-sāmi-nimilita-vāma-nayana-nīlotpala-dal
āñcalena sāvahelanam iva manāg eva mām avalokya
muni-vrata-jatu-mudrita-hasita-hīrakānarghya-mahā-ratna-bahiḥ-prakāśaṃ
nirbharāveśa-viśeṣeṇa hārādi-gumphana-vilāsam eva vitanvatīs tāḥ prati sasmitam
idam aham ābhāṣitavān |
abhinava-yauvanā-mūlya-cintāmaṇi-labdhi-vivardhitottuṅga-garva-mahā-parvatā
vaguṇṭhita-karṇyaḥ! priya-vayasyasya mama prārthite kṣaṇam api karṇān
udghāṭayantu bhavatyaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'With the tip of the blue lotus petal of her half-closed left eye, glinting with the fragrance of manifold cleverness, glancing at me as if with disdain, barely — while extending the sport of stringing necklaces and the like with the special intensity of an unrestrained impulse, [her lips sealed in] a sage's vow sealing away the priceless great jewel of diamond-like laughter — to them I spoke with a smile: "O you whose ears are veiled, whose great mountains of pride have grown towering from the acquisition of the wish-fulfilling gem — the price of fresh youth! For my dear friend's request, please open your ears for a moment!"'

body.text:
tatas tāsām īṣat smitvānyonyam ālokayantīnāṃ madhye pragalbhā lalitā vihasya
saroṣam iva vyājahāra | aye nāgara! etāni bahu-mūlyāni mauktikāni
rāja-mahiṣī-yogyāni | tava mahiṣīnām evālaṅkriyāyai satyam abhirūpāṇi kathaṃ
na dāsyāmaḥ ?
body.translated_text: 'Then, while they slightly smiled and glanced at each other, the bold <s>Lalitā</s> from their midst laughed and spoke as if angrily: "O gallant one! These pearls are of great value, fit for royal queens. Truly they are suitable for adorning your queens — how shall we not give them?"'

body.text:
tatas tad-vacaḥ śrutvā mayā kautukenāviṣṭena sāmnā punaḥ punar idam evoktam |
bhoḥ priya-bhūṣaṇāḥ! sarvāṇi yadi na deyāni tadā
mad-atyanta-priya-dhenu-yugala-śṛṅga-paryāptāny evāvaśyaṃ dīyantām |
body.translated_text: 'Then, hearing her words, I, filled with curiosity, again and again said conciliatingly: "O dear ornaments! If all cannot be given, then at least give enough for the horns of my most beloved pair of cows — that much must certainly be given."'

body.text:
tato lalitā sarvāsāṃ mauktikāni punaḥ punaś cālayantī bhūyaḥ prāha | he kṛṣṇa!
kiṃ kartavyam ? tava dhenu-yogyam ekam api nāsti |
body.translated_text: 'Then <s>Lalitā</s>, shaking all their pearls again and again, said further: "O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>! What is to be done? There is not even one [pearl] here suitable for your cows."'

body.text:
tadāham uktavān | ayi parama-cature lalite! tiṣṭha tiṣṭha | ahaṃ kārpaṇya-bhāk
paścāt tvayā vaktuṃ na śakya ity upālabhya satvaram ambāṃ vrajeśvarīm āgatya
mātar dehi me mauktikāni | ahaṃ tu tāni kṛṣṭa-kedārikāyām eva vapsyāmīti
punaḥ punar avocam | tato mātrā vihasyoktaṃ | vatsa na mauktikāny uptāni
prarohanti |
body.translated_text: 'Then I said: "O supremely clever <s>Lalitā</s>! Stop, stop! I am a recipient of pity — afterward you shall not be able to say [otherwise]." Having reproached her thus, I swiftly went to mother <s>Vrajeśvarī</s> (Yaśodā) and said: "Mother, give me pearls! I shall sow them in a tilled field." I said this again and again. Then mother laughed and said: "Child, pearls do not sprout when sown."'

body.text:
tadā mayoktaṃ | mātar avaśyam eva dīyantāṃ dina-trayābhyantare prarūḍhāni
bhavaty eva sākṣāt kartavyānīty asman-nirbandha-parihārāsamarthayā tayā dattāni
bahūni mauktikāni | mayā gokula-jalāharaṇa-ghaṭṭa-samīpa-vartini
yamunopakaṇṭhe pauruṣa-trayam avagāḍhāṃ kedarikāṃ niṣpādya sahāsaṃ
paśyantīṣu kāsucid gopikāsu tany uptvā sā punar apūri | parito vṛtiś ca kāṣṭhair
niviḍā kṛtā |
body.translated_text: 'Then I said: "Mother, they must certainly be given. Within three days, having sprouted, it can be verified directly." Unable to resist my insistence, she gave many pearls. I prepared a field three puruṣa-measures deep near the <s>Yamunā</s> riverbank by the water-drawing landing-place of <s>Gokula</s>, and while some <s>gopīs</s> watched laughing, I sowed them and filled [the field] again. And a thick hedge of sticks was made all around.'

body.text:
tatas tāsāṃ mauktikaprārthanvacanāsvaranirāsārthaṃ kedārikāsekāya vayasadvārā
gavyeṣu prārthyamāneṣu solluṇṭhaṃ vihasya tāḥ procuḥ |
tanmauktikakedārikāseko'smākaṃ gavyena kathamucitaḥ | yatpriyagobhūṣaṇārthaṃ
kṛtamauktikakedārikāsekastāsāṃ gavāṃ dugdhenaiva kriyatām |
tatkedārikotpadyamāne phale nāsmābhirabhilāṣaḥ kartavyaḥ | iti śrutvā mayā
svagṛhāṇāṃ gavāṃ bahubhiḥ payobhireva tā darśayatā pratyahaṃ sekaḥ kriyate sma |
body.translated_text: 'Then, in order to refute their words of refusal regarding the pearl-request, when through the cowherd-boys I was requesting milk from the cows for watering the pearl-field, they laughingly said with playful insolence: "How is it appropriate for our milk to water that pearl-field? Since the pearl-field was made for adorning your beloved cows, let the watering be done with the milk of those very cows. We have no claim on the fruit produced from that field." Hearing this, I performed the daily watering with abundant milk from my own household cows, demonstrating to them.'

body.text:
tataścaturthadivasa eva mauktikāni praūḍhāni | taddarśanenollasitena mayā
māturañcalaṃ gṛhītvānīya tadaṅkurā darśitāḥ | tān dṛṣṭvā tu mātā kimetaditi
manasi vicārayantī sandigdhā satī vrajaṃ jagāma | gopyas tu tacchrutvā hiṃsrā
latāḥ prarūḍhā iti parasparaṃ sahāsamūcire |
body.translated_text: 'Then, on the very fourth day, the pearls sprouted! Delighted by seeing that, I took mother by her garment-edge, brought her, and showed her the sprouts. Seeing them, mother, wondering "what is this?" in her mind, remained doubtful and went to <s>Vraja</s>. The <s>gopīs</s>, hearing of it, said to each other laughingly: "Harmful creepers have sprouted!"'

body.text:
tato nātivilambena mūrvākāriṇyastā mauktikalatā vistāriṇyaḥ samālocya
samīpavartināṃ kadambānāmupariṣṭhāt krameṇāvarohitāḥ | tataḥ
katipayairdivasaistāḥ saurabhonmāditamadhuvrataiḥ kusumanicayairgopīnāṃ
camatkāramātanvānāḥ sakalaṃ gokulamevādhyavasāyan |
body.translated_text: 'Then, before long, those pearl-creepers, growing thick like <s>mūrvā</s> vines, having spread widely, were gradually draped down from the tops of the nearby <s>kadamba</s> trees. Then, within a few days, with clusters of flowers whose fragrance maddened the bees, causing wonder among the <s>gopīs</s>, they pervaded all of <s>Gokula</s>.'

body.text:
tato'ṣṭa-vidha-yonija-mauktikebhyo vilakṣaṇāṃ śriyaṃ dadhati muktāphalāni tāsu
jātāni tāni dṛṣṭvā vraja-vāsināṃ vismayo'tyarthaṃ jātaḥ | viśeṣataś ca gopīnām |
tataḥ praty aham eva tad-darśanena jāta-lobhās tāḥ mantrayāñcakrire | bhoḥ
sakhyaḥ bhadrena jñātam asmabhyaḥ kṛṣṇo mauktikāni sarvathaiva na dāsyatyeva |
bhavatu | tat-kṛta-mauktika-kṛṣi-prakriyāsmābhir na dṛṣṭāstīti na syāt |
tatrānadhyavasāyaṃ tyaktvā tad-dviguṇikāyāḥ kedārikāyayā ārambhaḥ kathaṃ na
kriyate ?
body.translated_text: 'Then, pearl-fruits appeared on them, possessing a beauty quite different from the eight types of naturally-born pearls — and seeing them, the wonder of the residents of <s>Vraja</s> became exceedingly great. Especially [that] of the <s>gopīs</s>. Then, each day, greed arising from seeing them, they deliberated among themselves: "O friends! It is well known to us — <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> will absolutely never give us pearls. So be it. Let it not be said that we have not observed his method of pearl-cultivation. Abandoning hesitation in this matter, why should we not begin [our own field] of twice the size?"'

body.text:
iti śrutvāticaturā lalitā prāha -- bhoḥ pavana-vyādhi-vyāpṛtā gopyaḥ!
govardhanoddharaṇādi-bhūmi-mauktikotpādanādikaṃ lokottaraṇām api duṣkaraṃ
karma | tena yad añjasā kriyate tat kila mahā-siddhato
labdha-siddhauṣadhi-mantrādi-prabhāvād eveti samasta-vraja-janair niścitam eva |
anyathāsmad-vrajendra-gṛhiṇī garbha-sarovarotpanna-sukomala-nīlotpalasya
jñāta-sva-gopa-jāti-kriyā-kalāpa-mātrasya gopālakasya tasya tat-tat-karaṇe katham
etāvatī śaktiḥ svataḥ sambhaved iti jānantyo'pi bhavatyaḥ
siddhauṣadhi-mantrādy-antareṇa yat-tat-karmaṇi pravartitum abhilaṣanti | tat khalu
pariṇatāvagādha-lajjā-parihāsa-sāgarāntaḥ-svapatanāyaiveti satyam avadhāryatām |
body.translated_text: 'Hearing this, the supremely clever <s>Lalitā</s> said: "O <s>gopīs</s> afflicted with the wind-disease [of folly]! The raising of <s>Govardhana</s> and other [miracles], producing pearls from the earth and the like — this is a deed difficult even for those beyond the world. Therefore, whatever he does so easily is certainly from the power of accomplished herbs, mantras, and the like obtained from a great <s>siddha</s> — this is firmly established by all the people of <s>Vraja</s>. Otherwise, how could such power naturally belong to that cowherd boy, born from the lotus-lake womb of our <s>Vrajendra</s>'s wife, known only for his own cowherd-caste activities? Knowing this, yet you ladies wish to undertake that task without accomplished herbs, mantras, and the like — that is truly [a plunge] into the ocean of deeply-matured, unfathomable ridicule-laughter. Let this be understood truly!"'

body.text:
tatas tuṅgavidyā prāha -- asmābhir api
śrī-bhagavatī-pāda-padma-siddha-mantra-śiṣyā-nāndīmukhī-sakāśāt
siddha-mantram ekam ādāya kathaṃ na tathodyamaḥ kriyate ?
body.translated_text: 'Then <s>Tuṅgavidyā</s> said: "By us also, having obtained one accomplished <s>mantra</s> from <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>, the disciple of the blessed <s>Bhagavatī</s>'s lotus-feet-accomplished-mantra — why should such an effort not be made?"'

body.text:
sarvāḥ -- bhadraṃ vadati tuṅgavidyeti nirṇīya tat-pārśvam upetya sa-vinayam
ātmābhilāṣaṃ nivedayāmāsuḥ |
body.translated_text: 'All [declared]: "<s>Tuṅgavidyā</s> speaks well!" — having determined thus, they went to her side and respectfully communicated their desire.'

body.text:
tato nāndīmukhī svagatamāha -- aye nija-nayana-yugma-dṛṣṭi-sāphalyāya
cira-dinam asmad-vidhābhilaṣyamāṇa-kraya-vikraya-krīḍā-kutūhala-kalpataror
bāḍham akasmād asmād dṛśāṃ bhāgyātiśaya-vaśāt sākṣād bīja-rūpo'yam avasaraḥ
pratyāsanno babhūva | tad-vidagdhānāṃ śiromaṇīr apy etās tathā
yukti-sauṣṭhavātiśayena kṛtye'tra pravartayāmi | yathā sa tarus tvaritam eva
praūḍhaḥ phalavān bhaved iti manasi vicintya sāntarānandaṃ nāndī prāha -- bhoḥ
sakhyaḥ | satyaṃ mukundasya na mantra-kṛteyaṃ mṛdi mauktikā sṛṣṭiḥ |
body.translated_text: Then <s>Nāndīmukhī</s> spoke a welcome: 'Ah! For the fulfillment of our own pair of eyes' vision, the seed-form opportunity for the trade-and-barter play — that wish-fulfilling tree long desired by ones such as ourselves — has indeed suddenly drawn near through the surplus of our eyes' fortune. Now I shall set even the crest-jewel among clever women to this task with such surplus excellence of reasoning that that tree shall quickly become fully grown and fruitful.' Thinking thus in her mind, <s>Nāndī</s> spoke with inner delight: 'O friends! Truly, this creation of pearls in the soil is not the magic of <s>Mukunda</s>.'

body.text:
sarvāḥ - tan nija-janena kāraṇa-śuktyādi-mātram antareṇa kathaṃ mṛttikāyām
asambhaveyaṃ tad-utpattiḥ pratīyate |
body.translated_text: All replied: 'Then how can this production of them in the soil, which is impossible without causal factors such as an oyster shell and the like, be perceived by one's own people?'

body.text:
nāndī -- asyā bhuvaḥ svābhāvikedṛk-prabhāvād eva | yad vividha-ratna-jananīyaṃ
vraja-vana-bhūr iti śrī-bhagavatī-pāda-padmaiḥ punaḥ punar nivarṇyate | ṛtam apy
anubhūyante tathā | yataḥ
pravāla-nava-pallava-marakata-chada-vajra-mauktika-prakara-koraka-kamala-rāga
-nānā-phalādimanto hiraṇmaya-mahīruhāḥ sphuṭam atra jātā jāyamānāś ca
dṛśyante | ato'syām upta-muktāphalāni janiṣyante phaliṣyanti ceti kiṃ citram ? tad
bhavatībhir api surabhitara-navanītādi-seka-pūrvakam atiprayatnena tathā tat-kṛṣiḥ
kriyatāṃ yathā tato'py adhikatamāni paramottama-phalāni labhyante |
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndī</s> replied: 'By the natural and wondrous power of this earth itself! For "this land of <s>Vraja</s> forests is a mother of various jewels" — this is described again and again by the lotus feet of <s>Śrī Bhagavatī</s>. And it is truly experienced as such. For golden trees bearing coral-like new sprouts, emerald leaves, clusters of buds like diamonds and pearls, and various ruby-like fruits are clearly seen growing here, both already born and being born. So what wonder that pearl-seeds sown in this earth will sprout and bear fruit? Therefore, let you also cultivate them with the utmost effort, watering them with the most fragrant butter and the like, so that from them even more excellent, supremely fine fruits may be obtained.'

body.text:
iti tad-vacana-mādhurīm āpīya sa-santoṣaṃ sa-ślāghaṃ pratyayantyaḥ sarvās tām
āliṅgya nijāṃ sthalīm āgatya spardhayā maj-jayāya samucita-vetanato
dviguṇa-triguṇa-gorasa-pradānena karma-kārānānāyya sthāne sthāne kedārikāḥ
kṛtvā peṭikāyām agrathitāni grathitāny aṅga-bhūṣaṇa-rūpāṇi ca yāvanti sthitāni
tāvanti yathā-yuktam alpāny eva saṃrakṣyāṅgataḥ samuttāritāni ca mauktikāni
niravaśeṣam uptvā pratyaham eva tri-sandhyaṃ go-dugdha-navanīta-suvāsita-ghṛtair
eva sekaṃ kartum ārabdhavatyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Having savored the sweetness of her words, all of them, with satisfaction and praise, embraced her, came to their own plots, and out of rivalry — to defeat me — brought laborers by paying double and triple the usual wages in dairy products. Having made garden beds in place after place, they removed from their boxes whatever pearls were stored — both strung and unstrung, and those in the form of bodily ornaments — keeping only a suitable few for themselves, and sowed all the remaining pearls without exception. They then began watering them daily at the three junctions of the day with cow's milk, butter, and fragrant ghee alone.

body.text:
tatastāsāṃ muktākṛṣikaraṇaśravaṇānmātsaryato lobhataśca candrāvalīprabhṛtayo'pi
sarvā vallabyastato'pyadhikakedārikāḥ sthāne sthāne kṛtvā
dehagehayorekamapyasaṃrakṣya samastamauktikānyuptavatyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Then, hearing about their pearl-farming, all the beloved <s>gopīs</s> led by <s>Candrāvalī</s>, out of jealousy and greed, also made even more garden beds in place after place, and without saving even a single pearl for their bodies or homes, sowed all their pearls.

body.text:
tataḥ katipayadināntare svasvakedārikāsu jātān hiṃsralatāṅkurān dṛṣṭvā
antargarbhitagarvābhirvallabhībhistābhiḥ sarvābhiśchalato matpriyavayasyāḥ
parihasyante sma |
body.translated_text: Then, after some days, seeing thorny vine-shoots that had sprouted in their respective garden beds, those rival <s>gopīs</s>, whose pride was concealed within, mocked my dear friends under false pretenses.

body.text:
ekasmin dine gorasānāmatīvavyayaṃ svasvagṛhasya ca nimauktikatāṃ vīkṣya gopāḥ
sasaṃrambhaṃ kāraṇaṃ papracchuḥ |
body.translated_text: One day, seeing the excessive expenditure of dairy products and the pearl-less state of their own houses, the cowherds angrily asked the reason.

body.text:
tacchrutvā vṛddhā ūcuḥ | bho āyuṣmantaḥ | nānuyogaviṣayo'yamābhirbālābhiḥ
kṛto mauktikakedārikānāṃ nimittaṃ bahulo vyayo'cirādeva bahutaralābho
bhaviṣyati | yatkṛṣṇakedārikāyāṃ rājadārāṇāmapi durlabhāni muktāphalāni kila
dṛṣṭāni santīti |
body.translated_text: Hearing this, the elder women said: 'O long-lived ones! This is not a matter for inquiry. The great expenditure made by us young women on account of the pearl garden beds will soon yield abundant profit. For in <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s garden bed, pearls rarely obtainable even by queens have indeed been seen!'

body.text:
athaikadā viśākhayā svadekārikāsu tānaṅkurānnirīkṣya kāsāñcit karṇe
nibhṛtamidamuktam | bhoḥ sakhyaḥ | kṛṣṇakedārikāmadhye mayā yādṛśā aṅkurā
dṛṣṭā ete tu tādṛśā na dṛśyante | na jāne paścāt kiṃ bhavet |
kṛṣṇavayasyadṛṣṭinivāraṇārthaṃ chalataḥ suṣṭhu veṣṭyantām |
body.translated_text: Then one day, <s>Viśākhā</s>, having examined those shoots in her own garden beds, quietly whispered in the ears of some friends: 'O friends! The shoots I saw in <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s garden bed do not look like these. I do not know what will happen later. To prevent <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s companion from seeing, let them be well concealed under some pretext.'

body.text:
atha katipayadivasaistāsāṃ rādhādīnāmanyāsāṃ ca kedārikāsu kaṇṭakādicihnena
latābhirnijarūpe prakāśyamāne gopīkedārikāsu hiṃsrā latā jātā iti sakalagokula
eva khyātam |
body.translated_text: Then, after some days, when the vines in the garden beds of <s>Rādhā</s> and the others revealed their true nature through signs of thorns and the like, it became known throughout the entire <s>Gokula</s> that thorny vines had sprouted in the <s>gopīs</s>' garden beds.

body.text:
etad ākarṇya vayasya-dvārā gāndharvā-goṣṭhyāṃ mayedaṃ sotprāsaṃ vijñāpitaṃ
śrutaṃ bhavatīnāṃ kedārikāsu bahūni muktā-phalāni jātāni santi | ahaṃ tāvat
snigdhas tat sa-vayasyāya mahyaṃ prathama-phalāni dīyantām |
body.translated_text: Hearing this, through a companion, at a musical gathering, I said with mockery: 'I have heard that many pearl-fruits have been produced in your garden beds. I, for one, am an intimate friend — so give me the first fruits, along with my companions.'

body.text:
tatas tābhir uktaṃ | yadi vayaṃ kṛṣim akariṣyāmas tadā sakala-goṣṭhaṃ
mauktikamayam abhaviṣyat | paśupālya-svadharmam apahāya sa iva kaḥ
kīlāsa-vṛttim [*NOTE: Karṣaka-vṛttiḥ pakṣe kārpaṇyam] āśrayet ||
body.translated_text: Then they replied: 'If we had done farming, then the entire cow-settlement would have become entirely made of pearls. Abandoning the proper duty of cattle-tending, who would resort to the occupation of a farmer like him?' [Note: <s>kīlāsa-vṛtti</s> — farming occupation, with a pun on miserliness]

body.text:
tad ākarṇya mayā nikhila-vayasyāḥ savatsā gāvaḥ śakaṭa-vahā mahiṣyaḥ,
savarkarā ajā, vṛndāvana-vartinyaś ca mauktika-mayair mālādy-alaṅkārair
maṇḍitāḥ |
body.translated_text: Hearing that, I decorated all my companions, cows with their calves, cart-pulling buffaloes, goats with their enclosures, and those dwelling in <s>Vṛndāvana</s> with garlands and other ornaments made of pearls.

body.text:
tataś ca gopyo lajjayā sva-bhūṣaṇa-vyatirekeṇa bahu-dhana-vināśena gopa-bhiyā ca
kim atra yuktam iti mantrayitum ārebhire | aye gṛhīta-kṛṣṇa-pakṣayā
dhūrta-nāndīmukhyā'bhadreṇa pratāritāḥ sma ity ābhāṣya sarps.aṃ tan-nikaṭam
āgatya tat-kathana-pūrvakaṃ bahuśas tābhir bhartsitā nāndīmukhī prāha | bhoḥ
tapobhyaḥ śape na mayā sarvathaiva pratāritāḥ stha, kintu yuṣmābhir eva tat sarvaṃ
vināśitam |
body.translated_text: Then the <s>gopīs</s>, out of shame at the loss beyond their own ornaments, at the great destruction of wealth, and out of fear of the cowherds, began to deliberate on what would be proper. Saying 'Alas! We have been deceived through evil means by the wicked <s>Nāndīmukhī</s> who took <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s side!' — all of them came near her, and having narrated the events, thoroughly scolded her. <s>Nāndīmukhī</s> said: 'O ascetic ones! I swear — I did not deceive you in any way at all; rather, you yourselves ruined everything.' Then, among them, <s>Rādhā</s> said: 'O friends! Whether <s>Nāndīmukhī</s> deceives or that rogue does as he pleases — what profit is there now in deliberating about that? At present, other sorrows are not to be counted; it is only the fear from elders that distresses us. We would be relieved only when pearls are shown to them. Such pearls are truly extremely rare here, but let it be so arranged that they may be obtained from <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> himself for a price. Let a plan for that be devised.'

body.text: sarvāḥ | kapaṭini kathaṃ kāram |
body.translated_text: All: 'O deceitful one! How so?'

body.text:
nāndī | yato garvitābhir yuṣmābhir ḍhakkā-vādyavat kolāhala-prapañcena
savayasya-gaṇasya tasya śravaṇa-kuhare suṣṭhu-gocarīkṛtya kedārikāsu muktāḥ
sphuṭam uptāḥ tathā ko'py ekaḥ prahariko'pi tatra na rakṣitaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndī</s>: 'Because, puffed up with pride, you publicized through a great commotion — like drum-beating — to the ears of his companion-group that pearls were clearly sown in the garden beds, and yet not even a single guard was placed there to protect them.'

body.text: sarvāḥ -- etāvatā kiṃ na jātam ?
body.translated_text: All: 'Was that not enough for them to grow?'

body.text:
nāndī saroṣam | yaj jātaṃ tac caturaṃmanyābhiḥ śrūyatām | yuṣmān vijetum
abhīṣṭam iṣṭānna-pradānena suṣṭhu pralobhya dhūrta-guruṇā yuṣman-nāgareṇa
tena prerita-lolupa-bhaṇḍa-madhumaṅgalenāti-nirbaddhato vicitya kiñcij
jātāṅkurāḥ sarvā muktā niravaśeṣaṃ samādāya tatra tatra hiṃsrāvallī-kadambān
samāropya kayatyaḥ pṛthak svakṛta ekasmin kedāre pratnataḥ saṃropitāḥ |
tathānyāsāṃ tu tathaivānīya kālindī-gabhīra-nīrāntaḥ prakṣiptāḥ | iti mayā
sudṛḍhaṃ jñātam asti |
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndī</s>, angrily: 'Let those who think themselves clever hear what happened! To defeat you, that rogue urbanite of yours — your city-man — sending the greedy scoundrel <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>, thoroughly tempted with offerings of desired food, and dispatched by the wicked guru — insistently searched out all the pearls where shoots had just appeared, took every last one, planted clusters of thorny vines in their place, and separately transplanted them with care in a single garden bed of his own making. And those of the others were likewise taken and cast into the deep waters of the <s>Kālindī</s>. This I know for certain.'

body.text:
iti niśamya sarvā āhuḥ | ayi
kūṭatva-nāṭaka-naṭana-prakaṭanaika-kāryānindya-mahānandi | ayi
bhaṇḍa-madhumaṅgala-guruprāya-mahā-satīrthe | ayi
vrajaprathita-śaṭha-naṭa-sahita-nāṭya-yogye | tat-priyatame naṭi | ayi
kaliyuga-tapasvini | tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti sabhrūbhaṅgaṃ tām ākṣipya sva-geham āgatya
punaḥ punas tad eva vicārayantī tāsu rādhā bhoḥ sakhyaḥ nāndīmukhī vā
pratārayatu sa dhūrtas tathā vā karotu adhunā tad-vicāreṇa ko lābhaḥ | sāmpratam
anyad duḥkhaṃ na gaṇyate | gurvādito bhayam eva naḥ khedayati | tad vayaṃ tu
tebhyo mauktikeṣu darśiteṣv eva śithilī bhavet | tādṛśāni sarvathaivātra
sudurlabhāni kintu kṛṣṇād eva mūlyena yathā gṛhītāni syuḥ | tatropāyaś
cintyatām |
body.translated_text: Hearing this, all said: 'O <s>Nandī</s>, the great <s>Nandī</s>, whose sole purpose is to display the drama of deceitfulness! O great holy bathing-place comparable to the guru-like scoundrel <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>! O actress fit for drama in alliance with the renowned rogue actor of <s>Vraja</s>! O beloved of that actor! O ascetic of the <s>Kali</s> age! Stay! Stay!' Shaking their brows reproachfully at her and returning home, they pondered this matter again and again. Among them, <s>Rādhā</s> said: 'O friends! Whether <s>Nāndīmukhī</s> deceives or that rogue does as he pleases, what profit is there now in considering that? The present grief is not to be counted. It is only the fear from elders that pains us. We would be relieved only when pearls are shown to them. Such pearls are truly extremely rare here, but they should somehow be obtained from <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> for a price. Let a plan for that be devised.'

body.text:
tataḥ sarvābhir vibhāvyoktam | candramukhī caturā bhavati | suvarṇāni gṛhītvā
gatvā samucita-mūlyena mauktikāny ānayatu |
body.translated_text: Then all discussed and said: '<s>Candramukhī</s> is clever. Let her take gold coins, go, and bring pearls for a suitable price.'

body.text:
tatas tayoktam | sampraty asmābhir upālabdhasya tasya samīpam aham ekākinī
gantum aśaktāsmi | kāñcanalatā mama saṅge samāgacchatu | iti sarvāsām
anumatyā bahu-suvarṇāni gṛhītvā mauktika-vāṭikā-samīpaṃ te ājagmatuḥ | tatra
tad-vāṭikādhikāriṇaṃ subalaṃ mayā saha niviṣṭam abrūtām | he subala śrutam
asmābhir bhavadbhir navya-muktāni vikrīyante | tad imāni śuddha-suvarṇāni
gṛhītvā samucita-mūlyena pravīṇa-pravīṇa-muktā-phalāni dīyantām |
body.translated_text: Then she said: 'Now, to approach one whom we have just reproached — I alone am unable to go. Let <s>Kāñcanalatā</s> come along with me.' With the consent of all, having taken much gold, the two went to the vicinity of the pearl garden. There, they addressed <s>Subala</s>, who was seated with me as the officer of that garden: 'O <s>Subala</s>! We have heard that you sell fresh pearls. Take this pure gold and give us the choicest pearl-fruits for a suitable price.'

body.text:
tataḥ smitvā mayoktam | tadānīm anekadhā prārthyamānaṃ naikam api mauktikam
asmabhyaṃ dattam | asmat-kedārikā-sekārthaṃ dugdha-pārī ca bhavatībhir na
dattā | asmābhir varaṃ kālindī-madhye prakṣeptavyam | tathāpi bhavatīnāṃ
gṛha-sarvasvenāpi paṇīkṛtena nikhila-mauktika-vṛndādapakṛṣṭam ekam api
mauktikaṃ sarvathā na dātavyam |
body.translated_text: Then, smiling, I said: "At that time, though requested in many ways, not even a single pearl was given to us. Nor was a pail of milk given by you ladies for irrigating our small field. We would rather cast them into the middle of the <s>Kālindī</s> (Yamunā river). Even so, even if you were to wager everything in your households, not a single pearl withdrawn from the entire collection of pearls shall be given under any circumstances."

body.text:
tataḥ kāñcanalatayoktam | mauktika-nimittaṃ paty-ādibhyo yadi tāsāṃ bhīr na
bhavet tadāsya kadarthanoktim īdṛśīṃ kā nāma saheta | bhavatu kiṃ kartavyam |
haṭṭa-prasārita-bahuratnā madhurā tāvad dūre tad adya bhoḥ subala svayam eva
bhavatā madhyasthena bhūyatām | ānyatrika-mūlyād asmābhir viśeṣo'pi dātavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Then <s>Kāñcanalatā</s> said: "If those ladies had no fear from their husbands and others on account of the pearls, who indeed would tolerate such contemptuous speech from him? So be it — what is to be done? <s>Madhurā</s>, with its many gems spread out in the market, is far away; so today, O <s>Subala</s>, please be an arbiter yourself. We shall pay even more than the price offered by others."

body.text:
tataś ca viśeṣa-śabda-śravaṇān mayā vihasyoktam | bhavatu nāma
svabhāva-komalena mayā tu bhavatībhir iva kāṭhinyaṃ kartuṃ na śakyate | adattvā
vā anyat kiṃ kartavyam | kintu mauktikārdhinīnāṃ sarvāsāṃ
mauktika-mūlya-nirṇayaḥ kiṃ bhavatībhyām eva bhaviṣyati |
body.translated_text: Then, upon hearing the word 'more,' I laughed and said: "Very well — I, being soft-hearted by nature, am unable to be as hard-hearted as you ladies. What else can be done but to give them? However, will the determination of the price of the pearls for all the ladies desiring pearls be made by you two alone?"

body.text: tābhyām uktam -- atha kim ?
body.translated_text: The two of them said — "Of course!"

body.text:
mayoktam | kas tāvad viśeṣaḥ | tataś candramukhī kiñcid vihasya kāñcanalatām
ālokitavatī | kāñcanalatātha salajjaṃ subalaṃ prati vyājahāra | sakhe subala svayam
eva madhyasthena bhūtvā samādhāya samīcīna-yaśo-bhāras tāvad aṅgīkriyatāṃ
bhavatā |
body.translated_text: I said: "What then is the 'extra' amount?" At that, <s>Candramukhī</s> laughed slightly and glanced at <s>Kāñcanalatā</s>. <s>Kāñcanalatā</s> then bashfully addressed <s>Subala</s>: "Dear friend <s>Subala</s>, please become the arbiter yourself, settle the matter, and accept upon yourself the burden of fair reputation."

body.text:
subalenoktam | vayasya rahasyatayā bahu-mūlyatvaṃ kiyat kāñcanalatayā
prakaṭīkriyate | ātmano'bhīṣṭa-mūlyaṃ svayam eva sphuṭaṃ nigadya na kathaṃ
gṛhyate |
body.translated_text: <s>Subala</s> said: "Friend, how much of the high price is <s>Kāñcanalatā</s> revealing under the guise of secrecy? Why does she not simply state clearly the price she desires and take them?"

body.text:
tato'ham abruvam | sakhe subala candramukhyā abhiprāyo jñātaḥ | muktāphalāni
grahītuṃ kāñcanalataiva vicāryānargha-mūlyatvena parikalpya rādhādibhiḥ prahitya
mama dattāstīti | kintu kāñcana-sañcayato'pi muktāphalānām adhikaṃ mūlyaṃ
jagati prasiddham | tasmād ekayaiva kāñcanalatayā katham etāsāṃ
mūlya-paryāptiḥ | yadi vā asyā bakṣasi svarṇa-sampūṭa-rūpa-phala-dvaye bahavaś
cintāmaṇayo'pi santīti candramukhī vakṣati tathāpi na | yato
vaikuṇṭhanātha-kaṇṭha-sthita-kaustubhato'pi mamaitad ekaṃ muktāphalaṃ
parama-parārdhyam |
body.translated_text: Then I said: "Friend <s>Subala</s>, I have understood <s>Candramukhī</s>'s intention. <s>Kāñcanalatā</s> herself, having deliberated and reckoned the pearls to be of priceless value, has been sent by <s>Rādhā</s> and the others, and has offered herself as payment to me — that is the idea. But it is well known in the world that the value of pearls is greater even than a heap of gold. Therefore, how can <s>Kāñcanalatā</s> alone suffice as the price for all of these? Or even if <s>Candramukhī</s> were to say that within the golden casket of her beautiful form there are also many <s>cintāmaṇis</s> (wish-fulfilling jewels), even then — no! For this single pearl of mine is supremely more precious than even the <s>Kaustubha</s> gem that rests upon the neck of the Lord of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>."

body.text:
tac chrutvā bhrū-bhaṅgena mām avalokayantī kāñcanalatā saroṣam āha -
nirbuddhike candramukhi! tadaiva mayoktaṃ tasya dhṛṣṭasya savidhe mayā na
gantavyam | tathāpi tvayāhyam āgraheṇānīya kadarthitāsmi | tvaṃ muktāphalāny
ādāya samāgaccha aham itaś calitāsmi |
body.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Kāñcanalatā</s>, looking at me with furrowed brows, angrily said: "Foolish <s>Candramukhī</s>! I told you then and there that I should not go near that brazen fellow. Yet you insistently brought me here, and I have been humiliated! You take the pearls and come along — I am leaving from here!"

body.text:
candramukhī āha - kāñcanalate! satyaṃ kathayasi tat katham ekākinyā mayā
mūlya-nirṇayo bhavatu | kathaṃ vā nijane'tra sthātavyaṃ ekayoga-nirdiṣṭānāṃ saha
vā pravṛttiḥ saha vā nivṛttir iti mayāpi gantavyam | ity ubhe eva gamanodyate
dṛṣṭvā mayoktam - subala! tadaiva mayoktaṃ yad etābhyāṃ mūlya-nirṇayo na
bhaviṣyati |
body.translated_text: <s>Candramukhī</s> said: "<s>Kāñcanalate</s>! You speak the truth — so how can I alone determine the price? And how can one remain here by oneself? For those appointed together must either proceed together or withdraw together — so I too must leave." Seeing them both preparing to depart, I said: "<s>Subala</s>! I told you then and there that the price would not be settled by these two."

body.text:
tac chrutvā tayoḥ savidham āgatya subalenoktam - sakhi candramukhi! vayasyasya
mūlya-viṣaye mahān āgraho dṛśyate | tena priya-sakhī rādhā lalitādibhiḥ sahāgatya
samakṣam eva samucita-mūlyaṃ pradāya svepsita-muktāphalāni gṛhṇātu | tatra
mayā madhyasthena bhūtvā sācivyaṃ karaṇīyam |
body.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Subala</s> approached them both and said: "Dear friend <s>Candramukhī</s>! My companion seems to have great insistence regarding the price. So let his dear friend <s>Rādhā</s>, coming with <s>Lalitā</s> and the others, offer a suitable price in person and take the pearls she desires. I shall act as arbiter and counselor in the matter."

body.text:
iti niśamya candramukhī-kāñcanalate tāsāṃ savidhe gatvā sa-roṣam iva sarvaṃ
vṛttaṃ kathayāṃcakratuḥ |
body.translated_text: Hearing this, <s>Candramukhī</s> and <s>Kāñcanalatā</s> went to them and, as if angrily, narrated everything that had transpired.

body.text:
tataś ca rādhā lalitādibhiḥ saha mauktika-bāṭī-prāntam āsādya
candramukhī-dvārā subalam ākārya tam āha - priya-vayasya subala | asmāsu
bhavato niraṅkuśaḥ snehaḥ | ataḥ svayam eva tathā vidhīyatāṃ yathāsmābhiḥ
samucita-mūlyena muktāphalāni labhyante |
body.translated_text: Then <s>Rādhā</s>, together with <s>Lalitā</s> and the others, approached the edge of the pearl-seller's stall and, summoning <s>Subala</s> through <s>Candramukhī</s>, said to him: "Dear friend <s>Subala</s>, your affection for us is unbounded. Therefore, please arrange things yourself so that we may obtain the pearls at a suitable price."

body.text:
tac chrutvā subalena mahyaṃ nivedya mad-vacanena mat-sannidhau tā lalitādayaḥ
samānītāḥ | rādhā tu mamātrāgamanaṃ tvayā
mad-upadrāvaka-sva-priya-vayasyāya sarvathā na prakāśanīyam iti subalam
ābhāṣya man-nikaṭa-stha-kadamba-kuñjāntar nikhila-vṛttāntaṃ niśamayantī
nigūḍham āsthitā |
body.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Subala</s> informed me, and by my word he brought <s>Lalitā</s> and the others into my presence. But <s>Rādhā</s>, having told <s>Subala</s>, 'You must by no means reveal my coming here to your dear friend who torments me,' secretly stationed herself within a <s>kadamba</s>-grove near me, listening to everything that transpired.

body.text:
tato mayā tāḥ sarvā nibhālya rādhā kathaṃ na dṛśyate ity ukte tuṅgavidyayoktam -
 gokula-yuva-rāja! sā khalu sa-praṇayaṃ āryayā jaṭilayā kasyacid
gṛha-kārya-viśeṣasya kṛte rakṣitā gṛhe vidyate |
body.translated_text: Then, having surveyed all of them, when I said, 'How is it that <s>Rādhā</s> is not seen?' <s>Tuṅgavidyā</s> replied: 'O prince of <s>Gokula</s>! She has been affectionately kept at home by the elder <s>Jaṭilā</s> for the sake of some special household task.'

body.text:
tatas tad-avasara eva praviṣṭena madhumaṅgalena
iṅgita-vijñāpita-rādhā-nigūḍha-man-nikaṭa-sthitim avadhārya kiñcid vihasya
mayoktam - tuṅgavidye! muktā-grahaṇecchā tasyā na vidyate iti dṛśyate |
body.translated_text: Then, at that very moment, <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> entered, and by his gestures I ascertained that <s>Rādhā</s> was secretly stationed near me. Laughing slightly, I said: '<s>Tuṅgavidye</s>! It appears that she has no desire to acquire pearls.'

body.text: tatas tayoktaṃ - nahi nahi | tan-muktā-mūlyam asmābhir eva dāsyate |
body.translated_text: Then she said: 'No, no! We ourselves shall pay the price for her pearls.'

body.text:
tadā mayoktaṃ - viśākhaiva rādhā, rādhaiva viśākhā | tatas tan-mūlyaṃ viśākhaiva
dāsyatīti jñāyate | bhavatu tatra samāgraho nāsti, kintu yā khalu svayam āgatya na
gṛhṇāti tasyāś catur-guṇaṃ mūlyaṃ gṛhyatām | mauktikāni ca sādhāraṇāny eva
dīyantām iti me sarveṣāṃ sakhīnāṃ sudṛḍho nirṇayaḥ |
body.translated_text: Then I said: '<s>Viśākhā</s> is indeed <s>Rādhā</s>, and <s>Rādhā</s> is indeed <s>Viśākhā</s>. Therefore it is understood that <s>Viśākhā</s> herself will pay the price. Very well, there is no objection to that. However, for one who does not come in person to take them, four times the price shall be charged, and only ordinary pearls shall be given — this is my firm decision applying to all the <s>sakhīs</s> (girlfriends).'

body.text:
tad anu subalaṃ prati mayoktaṃ - sakhe subala! avacita muktā-pūrṇa-sampuṭān
ānīya purataḥ prasārya vicitya sarva-kaniṣṭhāny eva mauktikāni pūrvakṛtaṃ
tat-kārpaṇyam apy avigaṇayya prathamaṃ tat-kṛte viśākhāyāṃ samarpya tat-sakāśāc
ca tan-mūlyaṃ gṛhyatām | yadi vā prastutaṃ dātuṃ na śaknoti tatas tad-abhinneyam |
tāvat puṣpa-pravāla-corikā gopa-kanyakā yatra rakṣyante tatraivārān
mādhavī-kuñja-kārāyāṃ saṃbadhya rakṣyatām |
body.translated_text: After that, I said to <s>Subala</s>: 'Friend <s>Subala</s>! Bring the boxes filled with selected pearls, spread them out in front, sort through them, and present only the very poorest pearls to <s>Viśākhā</s> on her behalf — disregarding even the previously agreed pittance — and collect the price from her. Or, if she is unable to pay the stated amount, then she is to be treated no differently from a thief. She should be confined and guarded in the <s>Mādhavī</s>-creeper bower prison, right where the <s>gopī</s> girls who steal flowers and coral are kept.'

body.text:
tac chrutvā madhumaṅgalenoktaṃ - priya-vayasya | nirodhe'pi para-rāmābhiḥ
palāyana-vidyāḥ sphuṭam adhītāḥ santi |
body.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> said: 'Dear friend! Even when imprisoned, other men's women have clearly mastered the art of escape.'

body.text:
tadā mayoktaṃ - vayasya! mayāpy etad jñāyata eva | kintu cintā nāsti | yadyapi
para-rāmā-sparśo lajjā-tyāgaś cāsmad-vidhānāṃ svapne'py atīvāyogyas tathāpi -
body.translated_text: Then I said: 'Friend! I know this as well. But there is no worry. Although touching another man's wife and abandoning modesty are utterly inappropriate even in the dreams of men like us, nevertheless —'

body.text: sva-kāryam uddharet prājñaḥ kurvann api vigarhitaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'A wise man accomplishes his purpose even while incurring censure.'

body.text: tathā,
body.translated_text: Likewise,

body.text: āhāre vyavahāre ca lajjām api parityajet |
body.translated_text: 'In matters of food and business, one should abandon even shame.'

body.text:
iti saṃhitā-vacana-balād aham eva prahariko bhavan sarvām eva rātriṃ jāgran
nirantaraṃ nivatsyāmi |
body.translated_text: 'By the authority of these <s>Saṃhitā</s> (scripture) statements, I myself shall become the guard, and remaining awake the entire night, I shall stay on watch without interruption.'

body.text:
iti niśamya subalaḥ sa-smitam āha - puruṣottama! priya-sakhyā viśākhayā etāvati
mahā-saṅkaṭe kiyantaṃ kālaṃ sthātavyam ?
body.translated_text: Hearing this, <s>Subala</s> said with a smile: 'O <s>Puruṣottama</s> (Supreme Person)! For how long must your dear friend <s>Viśākhā</s> remain in such great distress?'

body.text:
tato mayoktaṃ - yad artham iyaṃ rakṣyate sā yāvat niḥśeṣaṃ mūlya-dravyaṃ
prasthāpayati | kiṃ vā kiyad-dravyaṃ gṛhītvā svayam evāgatya dhruvam asyāḥ
snehād ittham atra sthitvā avaśiṣṭa-dravyānayanārtham enāṃ prasthāpayati | tāvad
anayā sthātavyam |
body.translated_text: Then I said: 'She shall be held until she dispatches the full price in goods for which she is being detained. Or else, having taken some portion of the goods, she will surely come herself — and then, out of affection for <s>Viśākhā</s>, she will stay here thus and send her to fetch the remaining goods. Until then, <s>Viśākhā</s> must remain.'

body.text:
iti śrutvā madhumaṅgalaḥ prāha - sakhe! etad-goṣṭhīnām adhīśā sā sarvābhyo'pi
sarva-karmaṇi vicakṣaṇā viśeṣataḥ palāyane gavya-ghaṭṭyāṃ dānādiṣu sarvair
asmābhi punaḥ punaḥ prayakṣīkṛtāsti | tvaṃ tv aniśaam udghūrṇase tena me
mahatī cintā jñāyate |
body.translated_text: Hearing this, <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> said: 'Friend! She who is the mistress of all these assemblies, who is more skilled than all the others in every task — especially in fleeing, in churning milk, in giving charity, and the like — has been witnessed by all of us again and again. But you are perpetually agitated, and so I perceive great cause for worry.'

body.text:
tataḥ smitam apavāryāham avadaṃ - sakhe! alam anayā cintayā | tan-nikaṭe
mamodghūrṇā na janiṣyata eva | yadi vā jāyeta tarhi mad-uttamāṅgasya
tad-vāma-bhujā-mṛṇālīm upadhānīkṛtya
tad-uras-talpollasita-pīta-paṭṭāmbara-vara-vidhūpadhānopari
mad-vāma-kara-pallavam aruṇam abhinyasya tahtā
mauktika-paṇa-nimittaka-vāg-vilāsam ullāsayiṣyāmi | yathā sukhena jāgaryām eva
catvāro rajani-yāmā drutam eva viramanti | athavā
mad-uro-nāma-ghanāndhakāra-viṣama-kārāgārāntas tāṃ praviśya
tat-pārśva-yugalaṃ kaṭhora-bhuja-gārutmatārgalābhyāṃ dṛḍhaṃ saṃruddhya
sukhena nirātaṅkaḥ svapna-vilāsaṃ vitariṣyāmi |
body.translated_text: Then, concealing a smile, I said — 'Friend! Enough of this worry. My dizziness will certainly not arise near her. Or if it does arise, then placing my head upon the lotus-stalk of her left arm as a pillow, and resting my reddish left palm upon the excellent cushion-like yellow silk garment adorning the couch of her bosom, I shall kindle the play of words on the pretext of pearl-trading. Thus pleasantly, in wakefulness itself, the four watches of the night shall pass quickly. Or else, entering the dark and difficult prison-house of my name-filled chest, firmly bolting the two sides with the bars of my stiff <s>Garuḍa</s>-like arms, I shall comfortably, free from anxiety, bestow the delight of sleep.'

body.text:
iti śrutvā sarvāḥ smayamānā babhūvuḥ | rādhā tūdgrīvikayā māṃ viśākhāṃ
sarvāś ca sakhīr avalokayantī āha - candrāvalī-keli-kuraṅga! tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti
anuccair māṃ tarjayantī susmitāsīt | viśākhā tu kuṭila-dṛṣṭyā mām avalokayantī
āha - vraja-dhūrta-dhṛṣṭa! apehai apehīti vadantī sakhī-madhye līnā babhūva |
body.translated_text: Hearing this, all began smiling. <s>Rādhā</s>, looking up at me, at <s>Viśākhā</s>, and at all the <s>sakhīs</s> (friends), said — 'O sporting deer of <s>Candrāvalī</s>! Stop, stop!' — gently threatening me, she smiled beautifully. But <s>Viśākhā</s>, looking at me with a sidelong glance, said — 'O shameless rogue of <s>Vraja</s>! Go away, go away!' — saying this, she hid among the <s>sakhīs</s>.

body.text:
tataḥ sarvābhiḥ subalaṃ praty uktaṃ - subala! vidūṣakatāṃ tyaja | yadi bhavatāṃ
vikrayecchā vartate, tarhi muktāḥ pradarśya samucita-mūlyena pradīyantām | no
ced vayaṃ gṛhaṃ gacchāmaḥ | mathurāta eva mauktiāny ānayitavyāni |
body.translated_text: Then all of them said to <s>Subala</s> — '<s>Subala</s>! Stop playing the jester. If you all wish to sell, then show the pearls and give them at a proper price. Otherwise we shall go home. Pearls can be brought from <s>Mathurā</s> itself.'

body.text:
iti niśamya subalena sampuṭānudghāṭya tābhyāṃ mauktikāni pradarśya māṃ praty
uktaṃ -- priya-vayasya! imāni mauktikāny amūlyāni ābhir gṛha-paty-ādikaṃ
samasta-godhanāni ca vikrīyāpi ekasyāpi mūlyaṃ dātum aśakyam | etāḥ khalu
bhavat-snigdhāḥ sarvān upekṣya tvāṃ jānanti | tasmād etat-pūrva-kṛta-kārpaṇyam
api vismṛtya māṃ ca tva-anugatam avekṣya yat-kiñcin-mūlyaṃ gṛhītvā vinā-mūlyena
dattavad āsām abhīpsita-mauktikāni dātum ājñā kriyatām |
body.translated_text: Hearing this, <s>Subala</s>, having opened the caskets, showed the pearls to them and said to me — 'Dear friend! These pearls are priceless. Even if these [<s>gopīs</s>] were to sell all their household possessions including all their cattle, they would be unable to pay the price of even one. Indeed, they are fond of you; overlooking everyone else, they know only you. Therefore, forgetting their prior display of poverty and considering that I follow you, let an order be given to give them their desired pearls, accepting whatever token price, as if given free.'

body.text:
tato'ham avocam - sakhe! nahi nahi | vayaṃ vāṇijya-vyavasāyinaḥ | bhavatu | kiṃ
kartavyaṃ | bhavad-vacanaṃ ca rakṣaṇīyam | tad yat kiñcid alpam eva mayā mṛgyate
tad dāpayitvaiva dīyantām | kiṃ ca utkocaṃ gṛhītvā bāraṃ bāraṃ mama
ghaṭṭī-dāna-dravyāṇi bhavatā vināśitāni sanītit mama kenāpi kathitam asti
tasmān mūlya-dravyaṃ samakṣam eva mayaivābhyo grahītavyam |
body.translated_text: Then I said — 'Friend! No, no! We are engaged in commerce. So be it — what is to be done? Your word must also be honored. So let whatever small amount I seek be collected, and only then let them be given. Moreover, someone has told me that you, taking bribes, have time and again destroyed my toll-booth goods; therefore, the payment must be received from them directly by me, in plain sight.'

body.text:
subalaḥ kiñcid vihasyāha - bhadraṃ vacaḥ | kiṃ ca etābhiḥ
svīya-svīyābhīpsita-mauktikāni vicitya pṛthak pṛthak kuṭī-kṛtāni dṛṣṭvā
bhavatāpi svābhīpsita-mūlyaṃ kathyatām |
body.translated_text: <s>Subala</s>, laughing a little, said — 'Very well. Moreover, let them select their individually desired pearls and see them arranged in separate piles, and then you too state your desired price.'

body.text:
tato'ham abruvam - bhadraṃ darśayantu sva-svābhīpsita-mauktikāni mūlyaṃ
kathyate mayā |
subalaḥ prāha - priya-vayasya! etāḥ vinayena yan nivedayanti tat kṛpayāvadhārya
bhavate yadi rocate tadā vidhīyatām |
body.translated_text: Then I said — 'Good. Let them show their individually desired pearls; the price will be stated by me.' <s>Subala</s> said — 'Dear friend! Please graciously hear what they modestly request; if it pleases you, then let it be done.'

body.text: tato'haṃ - subala | kathyatāṃ kiṃ nivedayanti yuktaṃ cet kartavyam |
body.translated_text: Then I [said] — '<s>Subala</s>, tell me. What do they request? If it is reasonable, it shall be done.'

body.text:
subalaḥ prāha - evaṃ nivedayanti, madhu-purī tāvad dūre
samagra-mūlya-dravyāṇāṃ ca samācayanaṃ dina-dvaya-madhya eva sampadyate |
gurukulaṃ tu mauktikālaṅkārādy-adarśanāt kṣaṇe kṣaṇe khidyamānaṃ bāḍham
ākrośati | ato'tisnigdhān bhavad-vidhān avagatya lajjām api parihāya
nirjana-vanāntaram āgatānām asmākam ṛṇenaiva mauktikāni dāpayitvā drutam
eva vidāyaḥ kriyatām | mūlya-dravyāṇy asmābhir bhavatām
abhīpsita-vṛddhi-sahitāni dina-dvayābhyantare pariśodhya praheyāṇi yady asmāsu
bhavad-vayasyasya pratītir na jāyate tadā tvam evāsmākaṃ pratibhūr bhaveti |
tasmāt parama-pratīti-pātrābhyaḥ santata-satyavādinībhya etābhyaḥ pratītiṃ kṛtvā
datteṣu mauktikeṣu mūlya-dravyam abhīpsita-vṛddhiś cācirāl lapsyate | tathaitābhiḥ
saha niviḍa-sneho'pi vardhiṣyata eva |
body.translated_text: <s>Subala</s> said — 'This is what they propose: <s>Mathurā</s> city is far away, and the collection of all the payment goods can only be accomplished within two days. Meanwhile, the household elders, not seeing any pearl ornaments, are growing distressed moment by moment and are scolding harshly. Therefore, having recognized loving persons such as yourselves, and having set aside even our shame, we have come to this secluded forest glade. Let the pearls be given to us on credit, and let the farewell be made quickly. The payment goods, together with the interest you desire, shall be settled and sent by us within two days. If your friend does not have confidence in us, then you yourself shall be our guarantor.' Therefore, having placed trust in these supremely trustworthy, ever-truthful [<s>gopīs</s>] and having given the pearls, the payment and desired interest shall be received before long. And moreover, close affection with them shall only increase.'

body.text:
tato'haṃ vihasya - subala! tvaṃ śuddha-buddho'si | āsāṃ vyavahṛtiḥ kiñcin mātrāpi
tvayā na jñāyate | kuṭi-nāṭī-nāī̀oikā-nartakya imā mauktikaṃ gṛhītvā
nija-nija-bhartṛ-mahā-durga-koṣṭheir veṣṭitān sva-sva-guru-kula-mahā-parvatān
praviśya dravyam adattvā yadi khelyantyas tiṣṭheyus tarhi tvayā kiṃ kartavyam |
body.translated_text: Then I, laughing — '<s>Subala</s>! You are simple-minded! You do not know their dealings even a little. These cunning, deceitful, scheming actresses — having taken the pearls, they will enter their respective husband's great fortified treasuries and their own well-guarded household mountains, and if they refuse to pay — then what will you do?'

body.text:
subalaḥ prāha - sakhe! maivaṃ bravīḥ | etāḥ khalu naivaṃ kariṣyanti | yadi vā
kuryus tadojjvala-vanāntārjuna-kokilādibhiḥ saha tatra gatvā svayam ābhiḥ
svīkṛtam | svayaṃ grahāśleṣa-cumbana-svādhara-sudhā-pānādi-rūpa-mūlyam
etāsāṃ bhartṛṣu saṃśrāvya tat-prāpty-arthaṃ tebhyas tathā bhayaṃ
pradarśayiṣyāmi | yathā ta eva drutam amūs tvat-samīpaṃ prasthāpya tad
dāpayiṣyanti |
body.translated_text: <s>Subala</s> said — 'Friend! Do not speak thus! They will certainly not do so. But if they were to, then going there with <s>Ujjvala</s>, <s>Arjuna</s>, <s>Kokila</s>, and the others from the forest, I shall report to their husbands the price they themselves accepted — in the form of their own embrace, kiss, and the drinking of the nectar of their own lips — and I shall create such fear in those husbands that they themselves will quickly send them to you and make them pay.'

body.text:
tan niśamya madhumaṅgalena sa-krodham uktaṃ - re subala! tvaṃ nāmnaiva subalaḥ
pumāṃś cāsi | vastutas tv abalākṛtir muhur dṛṣṭo'si | yataḥ sāmpratam apy āsām
abalānāṃ phutkāraṃ kṣudrād atikṣudratareṣu tad-bhartṛṣu kartuṃ yad icchasi |
tad-bhīru-svabhāvasya tavaitat samucitam eva | tasmāt tvam evātropaviśya mayaiva
vijayādidhāṭīṃ pragṛhya balād āsāṃ bhartṛ-sahita-go-mahiṣyādikaṃ veṣṭayitvā
samānīya ruddhvātra nadīśvara-pure rakṣiṣyate | tadā tā eva svayam āgatya
sva-sva-dravyaṃ sutarāṃ dattvā svaṃ svaṃ patiṃ godhanādikaṃ ca mocayiṣyanti |
body.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> spoke angrily — 'Hey <s>Subala</s>! You are <s>Subala</s> (strong) only in name, and you are male [only nominally]. In reality, you have been seen many times in the form of a weak woman! Since even now you wish to make your petty little threat to the husbands of these weak women — husbands who are meaner than mean! Being timid by nature, this suits you well. Therefore, you sit right here, and I myself, taking up the <s>Vijayā</s>-army formation, shall forcefully round up the cattle, buffalo, and husbands of these [<s>gopīs</s>], bring them here, and imprison them here in <s>Nadīśvara-pura</s>. Then they themselves will come of their own accord and, having paid their full price and more, will free their own husbands and cattle.'

body.text:
tatas tac-chravaṇena janita-mahā-duḥkha-bhareṇaiva mayoktaṃ - prāṇa-sakha
madhumaṅgala! katham evaṃ tvayā mantryate ? vraja-vāsino bhilla-pulindādyā api
me priyebhyo'py adhika-priyāḥ | ete tu sa-gotrāḥ sahodarā mad-abhinnā eva |
tasmād etan-mantraṇam atīvānucitam | subala-bhāṣitam eva kiñcid bhāti | tathāpi
na priya-janaiḥ samam ādāna-pradāna-prayogeṇa rasa-rakṣā na jāyata eva | tathā
ca smṛtiḥ --
body.translated_text: Then, burdened with great distress from hearing that, I said — 'Dear life-friend <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>! How can you counsel thus? The inhabitants of <s>Vraja</s> — even the <s>Bhillas</s>, <s>Pulindas</s>, and others — are dearer to me than my own dear ones. These [<s>gopīs</s>] are of my own clan, my sisters, inseparable from me. Therefore this counsel is most improper. <s>Subala</s>'s words seem somewhat better. Yet even so, through commercial dealings with dear ones, the preservation of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic love) is never achieved. As the saying goes —'

body.text:
naivādānaṃ pradānaṃ hi mitraiḥ saha vitanyate |
kṛte prītyā bhavel lopaḥ kalahas tad-anantaram || iti |
body.translated_text: 'Neither giving nor taking should be extended with friends; if done, affection would be lost, and quarrel would follow thereafter.'

body.text: tataḥ prastutam eva mūlyaṃ dattvā mauktikāni nayantu |
body.translated_text: 'Therefore, let them pay the agreed price and take the pearls.'

body.text:
tac chrutvā sa-krodham iva subalaṃ nibhālya - aye! kauṭilya-pāraṅgata subala!
sarvair eva militvā viḍambayitum eva vayam atrānītā bhavatā | tad yūyaṃ
mauktika-vāṇijya-vyavasāyena rājyaṃ kuruta | vayaṃ calitāḥ sma ity uktvā
calantīnāṃ tāsāṃ savidham āsādya sauhārdam abhivyañjayan subalo lalitāṃ nīcaiḥ
prāha - sakhi lalite! ādāna-pradāna-vyavahārasya sneha-bhaṅga-kāritvāt kevalaĪa
tad-bhayenaiva priya-vayasyena mūlya-nirṇayaṃ prastuta-vitta-lābhaṃ ca vinā
sarvathaiva mauktikāni na deyānīit sarva-prakāreṇāvadhāritam | tasmāt samāgatya
prathamaṃ tāvan mūlyam eva nirṇīyatām | tad-dānopāyaḥ paścāc cintanīyaḥ ity
anunayena tāḥ parāvṛtya mat-samīpam ānīya māṃ praty uvāca - vayasya! narma
hitvā mūlyam eva tāvat kathyatām | tato'ham -- sakhe subala! prathamaṃ tāvat
kasya mauktikānāṃ mūlyaṃ kathanīyam ?
body.translated_text: Hearing that, glaring at <s>Subala</s> as if with anger — 'Ha! O <s>Subala</s>, master of deception! All of you have conspired to bring us here just to mock us! So you all conduct your kingdom through pearl-commerce! We are leaving!' Saying this, as they began to depart, <s>Subala</s> quickly approached them and, expressing affection, said softly to <s>Lalitā</s> — 'Dear <s>Lalitā</s>! Since commercial dealings of giving and taking destroy affection, my dear friend has firmly resolved, precisely out of that fear alone, that the pearls shall absolutely not be given without settling the price and receiving the payment first. Therefore, come back — first let the price itself be determined. The means of payment can be considered afterward.' Thus, with gentle persuasion, he turned them around and brought them to my presence, and said to me — 'Friend! Setting aside the jesting, let the price first be stated.' Then I [said] — 'Friend <s>Subala</s>! First, whose pearls' price should be stated?'

body.text:
subalaḥ prāha - etāsāṃ madhye lalitaiva mukhyā tad etad gṛhīta-mauktika-mūlyaṃ
prathamaṃ nirucyatām |
body.translated_text: <s>Subala</s> said — 'Among these, <s>Lalitā</s> is the chief; so let the price for her chosen pearls be stated first.'

body.text:
tato'haṃ kiñcid vihasya - etad-vāhinīnāṃ pravīṇayā lalitayā samare pauruṣeṇa yadi
mādṛśaḥ puruṣa-siṃhaḥ sakṛd api kuṇṭhitāstrīkartuṃ śakyate | tadāsyāḥ samakṣaṃ
sarvathaivāstrī na bhaviṣyāmi | kiṃ vā santatam amuktāstrī bhūtvā etaṃ puaruṣam
evānukīrtayann imām evānucariṣyāmīti idam eva yat kiñcin mūlyaṃ dattvā
gṛhṇātu |
body.translated_text: Then I, laughing a little: 'If, by the prowess of the skilled <s>Lalitā</s>, the leader of these army-women, a lion among men such as I can even once be rendered weaponless in battle — then in her presence I shall indeed never be without a weapon. Or rather, continuously remaining one whose weapon is not released, ever praising this man alone, I shall follow her.' [Note: wordplay on <s>amuktāstrī</s> — 'one who has not released a weapon' and 'unmarried woman'] 'So let her take it by giving whatever little price there may be.'

body.text:
subalaḥ smitvāha - gokula-vīra! sudīpra-darpa-bharair
mahendra-garva-parvata-kharvanāya sapta-rātram atra
vāma-kara-kamala-kaniṣṭhāṅguli-varāṭaka-śikharopari bhramara iva
govardhana-girir yena vyadhāyi tenoccaṇḍena bhavatā samam abaleyaṃ
kaumalya-lalitā katham iva samitim ativistārayatu |
body.translated_text: <s>Subala</s> smiled and said: 'O hero of <s>Gokula</s>! By whom the <s>Govardhana</s> mountain was held for seven nights atop the tip of the little finger of the left lotus-hand, like a bee, for the humbling of great <s>Indra</s>'s mountain of pride swelling with brilliant arrogance — how can this maiden, delicate with youthful grace, greatly extend battle with you, the formidable one?'

body.text:
madhumaṅgalaḥ prāha - subala! taṃ kathaṃ pūrvam asya paugaṇḍa-kṛtaṃ darpam
atiślāghase ? yad adhunā tāruṇyāmṛta-sekena sa
darpaka-kalpa-taru-lakṣa-lakṣa-guṇaṃ pallavito'sti |
body.translated_text: <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> said: '<s>Subala</s>! Why do you so excessively praise the pride he displayed in his boyhood? For now, with the sprinkling of the nectar of youth, that tree of amorous pride has sprouted a hundred-thousand-fold.'

body.text: subalaḥ prāha - katham iti viditam ?
body.translated_text: <s>Subala</s> said: 'How is that known?'

body.text:
madhumaṅgalaḥ - yad anena pūrvārīṇāṃ sakalānāṃ pūrvaṃ yādṛśa-vaikalyaṃ
kāritam āsīt, sāmpratam etad durgamaṃ tad-dhṛdayaṅgamāna-tanu-parvatān
abhilīlayaiva kena ca nakharāstreṇaiva khaṇḍa-khaṇḍīkṛtya mahāmārādibhis
tato'py atulataravaikalyam āpāditam āste |
body.translated_text: <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>: 'Because, whereas previously he caused such distress to all his former adversaries, now — these body-mountains entering his heart through impassable approaches — with nothing but a claw-weapon, he has playfully cut them to pieces, and through great battles and the like, brought about even more incomparable distress.'

body.text:
tato'haṃ vihasya - subala! satyam anyatra mayā tādṛśenaiva bhūyate | na tv etasyāḥ
purataḥ yasmāt tato'pi pravara-vigrahe vividha-vaicitrī-pravīṇayānayā bāraṃ bāraṃ
bhrū-dhanuṣ-ṭaṅkāreṇaiva huṅkāreṇa helayā stabdhīkṛto'smi | tat katham iyam
abalā bhavatu |
body.translated_text: Then I, laughing: '<s>Subala</s>! Truly, elsewhere I behave exactly so. But not in front of her, because in the more excellent combat of various wondrous skills, she, being adept, has again and again rendered me stiff merely by the twang of her bow-like eyebrows, by a mere exclamation, with disdain. So how can she be called weak?'

body.text:
ity ākarṇanena smera-mukhīḥ sakhīr avalokya svānandottha-vikārān avagūhya
sakrodham iva lalitayoktaṃ - aye subala vidūṣaka! madhumaṅgala-sahacarasya
gokula-bhaṇḍasya bhaṇḍatā-devyā satyaṃ tvam apy āviṣṭo'si | yad asmān
etat-samakṣaṃ samānāyya viḍambana-samudre saṃpātayan kautukaṃ paśyann asaīti
nigadya kuṭila-dṛṣṭyā mām ākṣipantīm āgacchata bhoḥ saralāḥ! āgacchatety
uktvā sarvābhiḥ saha gacchantīṃ tad avasara eva tatrāgatā bhagavatyāḥ
paurṇamāsyā antevāsinī nāndīmukhī tad-gamana-vārtām akhilāṃ sarvābhyaḥ
samavadhārya vyājahāra - sakhi lalite! narma-śālino'sya śrī-vrajendra-nandanasya
parihāsa-vāṅ-mātreṇaiva sva-kāryam upekṣya katham apayānty asi ? kṣaṇaṃ mayā
saha nirvṛtya -
body.translated_text: Hearing this, <s>Lalitā</s> — seeing her friends with smiling faces and concealing her own agitations born of delight — spoke as if angrily: 'O <s>Subala</s>! O jester! Companion of <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>, clown of <s>Gokula</s>! Are you too possessed by the goddess of buffoonery? That you have brought us here before him and are watching with amusement as we drown in an ocean of mockery!' Saying this, casting a sideways glance reproaching me, she said 'Come, O straightforward ones! Come!' and began going with all of them. At that very moment, <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>, a student of the venerable <s>Paurṇamāsī</s>, who had just arrived there, having ascertained from all of them the entire news of their departure, spoke: 'O friend <s>Lalitā</s>! Merely because of the jest-words of this playful son of the lord of <s>Vraja</s>, abandoning your own purpose, how can you depart? Pause a moment with me —'

children.text: apamānaṃ puraskṛtya mānaṃ kṛtvā tu pṛṣṭhataḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Having placed insult in front and honor behind,'

children.text: sva-kāryam uddharet prājñaḥ kārya-dhvaṃso hi mūrkhatā ||
children.translated_text: 'The wise one accomplishes their own purpose; for the destruction of purpose is foolishness.'

body.text:
ity ādi-nyāyena parihāsa-viḍambanāni soḍhvā sthairyam ālambya sva-kāryam
uddhara | kiṃ ca mayā śapathaṃ kṛtvā vyāhriyate | asya narmabhir eva lagnakair iva
mauktikāni dāpayitavyāni | anyathā bhavat-pūrva-kṛta-kārpaṇyam anusmarato'py
abhimāna-śālino'sya narma-prayogo na sambhavati | tad anyasyā mauktika-mūlyaṃ
śrutvā yat kṛte bhadraṃ syāt tad eva vyavahartavyam iti balād iva tāṃ haste gṛhītvā
sarvābhiḥ saha muktākuṭa-nikaṭam ānīya māṃ pratyuktavatī gokula-yuvarāja!
tatra-bhavatyā bhagavatyā śubhāśīḥ śata-pūrvakaṃ bhavantaṃ prati kiñcit
sandiṣṭam asti |
body.translated_text: 'Thus, according to this and other maxims, enduring the jests and mockeries, taking hold of firmness, accomplish your purpose! Moreover, I declare with an oath: through his very jests, like hooks, the pearls are to be obtained. Otherwise, remembering the miserliness you previously caused, the employment of jests by this proud one would not be possible. So let the pearl-price be heard from another, and whatever transaction would be auspicious — let that alone be conducted.' Thus saying, as if by force, seizing her by the hand and bringing her along with all the others near the pearl-heap, she addressed me: 'O prince of <s>Gokula</s>! The venerable <s>Bhagavatī</s> sends you hundreds of auspicious blessings and has some message for you.'

body.text:
tato'haṃ -- nāndīmukhi! kuśalam āste tatra-bhavatī bhagavatī ? tat kathyatāṃ kim
ājñāpayati | tat-sandeśāmṛtenātmānam apyāyāmi |
body.translated_text: Then I: 'O <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>! Is the venerable <s>Bhagavatī</s> well? Then let it be told — what does she command? Let me refresh myself with the nectar of her message.'

body.text:
nāndīmukhī -- imā vatsā rādhādayo vraja-kumārikā asmākam atīva
sneha-pātrāṇi āyuṣmati bhavaty api santataṃ paramānuraktāḥ | tad asmān vīkṣya
atyāgrahaṃ vimucya āsāṃ dātuṃ śakyamāna-mūlyam ādāya maāṣṭa-nidhi-pater
vrajendrasya kumāreṇa bhavatā etad abhīṣṭa-mauktikāni dattvā vayaṃ
santoṣaṇīyā iti bhagavatyāḥ sandeśam imam avakalayya narmāṇi parityajya
muktāphala-dānenaitāḥ santoṣya gṛhāya prasthāpayituṃ mahānubhāvāḥ
sarva-gokula-sukha-kāriṇo bhavanta eva pramāṇam |
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>: 'These dear ones — <s>Rādhā</s> and the other maidens of <s>Vraja</s> — are the objects of our deepest affection. They are also ever supremely devoted to you, O blessed one. Therefore, seeing us, setting aside excessive insistence, accepting whatever price they are able to give — you, the son of <s>Vrajendra</s>, the master of the eight treasuries — should give them the desired pearls and thus satisfy us.' This is the message of the venerable lady. Understanding this, setting aside jests, satisfying them with the gift of pearl-fruits and sending them home — you great-souled ones, the bringers of happiness to all <s>Gokula</s>, are the authority in this.'

body.text:
tato'haṃ sa-ślāghaṃ - nāndīmukhi! pūrvaṃ subala-hastena tat-prahitājñā-kusumaṃ
śirasi nidhāya samagrame eva parityajya lalitā-mauktikānāṃ yaḥ kaścana
mūlyābhāso'nayā saha nirṇīto'sti tam asyā mukhato niśamya tato yat tvayā tyājyate
tad api mayā tyājyam |
body.translated_text: Then I, with praise: 'O <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>! Previously, through <s>Subala</s>'s hand, placing the flower of command sent by her upon my head, I had already agreed completely, setting aside the price of <s>Lalitā</s>'s pearls. Whatever semblance of a price was settled with her — hear that from her mouth; and then whatever you would set aside, I too shall set aside.'

body.text:
ity ākarṇya sakampādharaṃ bhruvaṃ kuṭilayantīṃ lalitāṃ sarvāś ca smita-mukhīr
avalokayantī nāndīmukhī smita-pūrvakam evāha - vraja-yuva-rāja! sa imābhyaḥ
śruto'sti, kintu tādṛṅ narma parihāya amat-samakṣam anyāsāṃ sarvāsām eva
yathā-yuktaṃ mūlyaṃ kathyatām |
body.translated_text: Hearing this, seeing <s>Lalitā</s> whose lower lip was trembling and whose eyebrow was curving, and all the others with smiling faces, <s>Nāndīmukhī</s> spoke with a preceding smile: 'O prince of <s>Vraja</s>! That has been heard by these women, but setting aside such jests, state in our presence the proper price for all the others.'

body.text:
tato mayoktaṃ - nāndīmukhi! āsāṃ sarvato jyāyasī jyeṣṭhā tad asyā
mauktika-mūlyam anayā saha vicārya tvayaiva kathyatām |
body.translated_text: Then I said: 'O <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>! Among all of them, <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s> (the eldest) is the greatest. So deliberate the pearl-price with her and you yourself state it.'

body.text:
nāndīmukhī - vitta-svāminaiva mūlyaṃ prathamaṃ kathanīyam | tat svayam eva
bhavatā tat kathyatām |
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>: 'The owner of the goods should state the price first. So you yourself state it.'

body.text:
tato'haṃ - niśāpater mama hṛdayākāśa-vīthyām uditāyāṃ rādhāyām udayantyām
anurādhāyāṃ sva-maryādām unmucya tayor madhye rāgeṇodayantī jyeṣṭhā
man-mukha-candraṃ tābhyāṃ saha vā pṛthag vā manāg api sva-mukhena
pariṣvajatu iti |
body.translated_text: Then I: 'When <s>Rādhā</s> rises in the sky-path of my heart as the lord of night, when <s>Anurādhā</s> rises — <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, releasing her own limit, rising with passion between the two — let her embrace my moon-face with her own face, along with those two or separately, even slightly.' [Note: <s>Rādhā</s>, <s>Anurādhā</s>, and <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s> are three consecutive <s>nakṣatras</s> (star constellations) near the full moon; <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> uses the astronomical pun to ask for a kiss as payment.]

body.text:
tatas tan niśamya nikuñjāntaritāyāṃ rādhāyāṃ lalitā-viśākhā-jyeṣṭhāsu ca tisṛṣu
bhrū-bhaṅgena krodham abhinayantīṣu mayoktaṃ - nāndīmukhi!
sva-sva-mahā-lābha-karam api bhāṣitam avadhārya katham etāḥ krudhyanti ?
body.translated_text: Then, hearing that, while <s>Rādhā</s> was hidden behind the bower, and <s>Lalitā</s>, <s>Viśākhā</s>, and <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s> — all three — were expressing anger through brow-knitting, I said: 'O <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>! Even though what I said would bring them great gain, why do they become angry?'

body.text:
nāndīmukhī - sundara! gokula-śyāma-niśāpater anya-parigṛhītānāṃ satīnām
asmākam etat-para-puruṣasya satīnām asmākam etat para-puruṣasya
mukha-candra-cumbana-karaṇaṃ dūre tāvad āstāṃ sparśo'pi mahā-pāpāyaiveti
krudhyanti |
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>: 'O beautiful one! O dark lord of <s>Gokula</s>'s night! For chaste women like us, who belong to others — to kiss the moon-face of this other man — far be it! Even mere touch would be a great sin — so they are angry.'

body.text:
ityādi vinoda-līlām ākarṇya satyabhāmā kṛṣṇam āha - nātha! tārā-gaṇane
rādhāyā viśākheti-prasiddham api nāma hitvā sākūtam anurādheti nāma
prayuñjatas tan-narmālāpa-bhaṅgīṃ svasmin svasminn evāvadhārayantyos tayor
vidagdha-rādhā-viśākhayor nyāyya eva roṣaḥ | lalitā kathaṃ kupyati ?
body.translated_text: Hearing this and more of the playful pastimes, <s>Satyabhāmā</s> said to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>: 'O Lord! In the counting of stars, purposefully using the name <s>Anurādhā</s> — which is also well known as <s>Viśākhā</s>'s name — instead of it, the anger of those two clever ones, <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Viśākhā</s>, each understanding the nuance of the jest-talk as referring to herself, was indeed justified. But why does <s>Lalitā</s> become angry?'

body.text: kṛṣṇaḥ - priye! anurādheti lalitāyā evāpara-paryāyaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>: 'O beloved! <s>Anurādhā</s> is also an alternative name for <s>Lalitā</s>.'

body.text:
satyabhāmā - yādavendra! etad apūrva-līlā-kathā-śravaṇena mama manasi tṛptir
alaṃ vṛttir nāsti tat kathaya kathaya |
body.translated_text: <s>Satyabhāmā</s>: 'O chief of the <s>Yādavas</s>! By hearing this unprecedented story of pastimes, my mind has no satisfaction, no sufficiency. So tell more, tell more!'

body.text:
kṛṣṇaḥ - tato'haṃ smita-śavalita-campakalatā-vadana-candram ālokayaṃs tad
gṛhīta-muktā-kūṭaṃ hastena cālayann idam avadaṃ - nāndīmukhi! iyaṃ te
priya-sakhī campakalatā kasmād api siddhāt prāpta-siddhir iti mayā bahu-dinam
anumitam āste |
body.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>: 'Then, gazing at her face — the moon of <s>Campakalatā</s>'s vine-like face, dappled with a smile — and shaking with my hand the collected pearl-heap, I said this: "O <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>! This your dear friend <s>Campakalatā</s> has attained perfection from some <s>siddha</s> (accomplished one) — I have suspected this for many days."'

body.text: nāndīmukhī - katham anumitam ?
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>: 'How did you suspect?'

body.text:
mayoktaṃ - yata iyaṃ campakavallī sthāvarā madhye bṛhat-phala-dvaya-bhārānatāpi
līlayā caṅkramīti | ato mudira-sundare mad-urasi campaka-mālā bhūtvā
sva-saurabha-bhareṇa māṃ vāsayatu | mayāpi sva-siddhi-balāt etad-ājñayaivāsyāḥ
kaṇṭhe sūkṣmatara-marakata-maṇi-mālayā vakṣojayor antare ca
mahendra-nīlamaṇi-nāyakena tvaritam eva bhavitavyam |
body.translated_text: I said: 'Because this <s>Campaka</s>-vine, though immobile, moves about playfully even while bowed by the weight of two large fruits in the middle. Therefore, upon my thundercloud-beautiful chest, let her become a <s>campaka</s> garland, pervading me with the fullness of her fragrance; and I too, by the power of my perfection, at her command, shall quickly become a necklace of the finest emerald gems upon her neck and a great sapphire pendant between her breasts.'

body.text:
subalaḥ - priya-sakhe! caṅkramaṇādinā'syāḥ siddhiḥ sarvair anubhūyata eva | tava
tu kenāpi kadāpi kutrāpi sā naiva dṛṣṭāsti | tasmād duṣkare'smin karmaṇi
sahasaiva pravṛttena bhavatā aydi niṣpādayitum aśakyaṃ syāt tarhi vayam ābhir
upahasiṣyāmahe | ato vicāryaiva pravṛttena bhavitavyam |
body.translated_text: <s>Subala</s> — Dear friend! The <s>siddhi</s> (perfection) of this [art] through walking meditation and such is experienced by all. But yours has never been seen by anyone, anywhere, at any time! Therefore, if you, having rashly undertaken this difficult task, are unable to accomplish it, then we shall be laughed at by these [ladies]. So one must proceed only after careful deliberation.

body.text: tato'haṃ - subala! mama siddhiṃ paśyann api na paśyasi ? mayā kiṃ kartavyam ?
body.translated_text: Then I [said] — <s>Subala</s>! Though seeing my <s>siddhi</s>, you do not see it? What am I to do?

body.text:
nāndīmukhī - madhurāṅga | kadā kutra kā siddhis tvayā niṣpāditāsti | sā
kathyatāṃ, sarve śuśrūṣavaḥ santi |
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s> — O sweet-limbed one! When, where, and what <s>siddhi</s> has been accomplished by you? Let it be told — all are eager to hear!

body.text:
tato mayoktaṃ - deva-yātrāyām ambikā-vane śaraṇāgatatvena tāta-pādayoḥ patitaṃ
mahājagaraṃ pādāṅguṣṭha-sparśa-mātreṇaiva sarvālaṅkṛti-bhūṣito
vidyādhara-rājo mayā vyadhāyi | girīndra-rājo govardhanaś ca saptāham
eka-kareṇaiva chatrākam ivānāyāsenaivādhāri | kāliya-viṣa-jvālā-vimohitaḥ
subalādi-vayasya-gaṇaḥ sva-dṛṣṭi-mātreṇaiva sa-cetanaḥ sphuṭam akāri | bāraṃ
bāraṃ mahādāvānalo'py amṛtīkṛtya sukhenaiva sphuṭam apāyi | evam ādayo
bahavaḥ siddhi-prabhāvā gokule kena nānubhūtāḥ santi ? tad ativistareṇālam |
iti niśamya īṣat-smayamānā lalitā prāha - nāndīmukhi! eṣa te durlalito nāgaraḥ
sarvam etat satyaṃ kathayati | kintu sa kālo gataḥ | yatra brahmacarya-balena tat
sarvaṃ niṣpāditam āsīt | sāmprataṃ
nṛśaṃsa-kaṃsa-sevaka-govardhana-malla-gṛhiṇyāḥ padmā-śaivyā-prabhṛtīnāṃ ca
vrajāṅganānāṃ santata-sambhoga-vilāsena dūṣita-brahmacāritvād asyāntarhitāḥ
sarvās tāḥ siddhayaḥ |
body.translated_text: Then I said — At the festival procession to the gods, in the grove of <s>Ambikā</s>, by the mere touch of my big toe, I transformed a great serpent who had fallen at my father's feet seeking refuge into a <s>Vidyādhara</s> king fully adorned with all ornaments. And the king of mountains, <s>Govardhana</s>, was held up for seven days with a single hand, effortlessly, like a mushroom. The group of friends — <s>Subala</s> and others — who were bewildered by the flames of <s>Kāliya's</s> poison were clearly revived to consciousness by a mere glance of mine. Again and again, even great forest-fires were turned to nectar and easily and clearly drunk up. Many such manifestations of <s>siddhi</s>-power — by whom in <s>Gokula</s> have they not been experienced? Enough of excessive elaboration! Having heard this, <s>Lalitā</s>, smiling slightly, said — <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>! This spoiled gallant of yours speaks all this truly. But that time has passed, when all that was accomplished by the power of celibacy. Now, through the constant amorous dalliance with the wife of the servant of the cruel <s>Kaṃsa</s>, the wrestler <s>Govardhana</s>'s wife, and with <s>Padmā</s>, <s>Śaivyā</s>, and other women of <s>Vraja</s>, his celibacy having been corrupted, all those <s>siddhis</s> have vanished.

body.text:
tato'haṃ kiñcid vihasya - lalite! tejīyasāṃ na doṣāya vahneḥ sarva-bhujo yathā ity
asya padyasyārtham abuddhaiva tvyedam ucyate | tat-tad-arthaḥ śrūyatāṃ | yathā
sarva-bhakṣaṇenāpi vahnes tejo-glānir na bhavet | pratyuta tad-vṛddhir mahaty eva
bhavati | tathā bhavādṛśīnām uttama-varāṅganānām
avirata-madhura-rasopabhoga-mādhuryeṇa mamāpi siddhir nirantaram ujjvalā
bhavantī parama-vṛddhim evādhikatarām avāpa |
body.translated_text: Then I, laughing slightly — <s>Lalitā</s>! You speak this without understanding the meaning of the verse: 'For the mighty, there is no fault, just as fire devours all.' Listen to its proper meaning: just as fire's brilliance is not diminished even by consuming everything — rather, its increase is very great indeed — so too, through the sweetness of uninterrupted enjoyment of the finest essence with supreme women such as yourselves, my <s>siddhi</s> also, constantly radiant, has attained the very highest increase.

body.text:
madhumaṅgalah -- lalite! satyaṃ bravīti priya-vayasyaḥ | siddhiś cen na vṛddhim
āyāti tarhi muktaḥ kathaṃ bhūmau prārohanti ? prārūḍhāś ca kathaṃ sarvataḥ
prasāriṇyā vallikā bhavantyaḥ pracurataraṃ phullanti phalanti ca ?
body.translated_text: <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> — <s>Lalitā</s>! My dear friend speaks truly. If <s>siddhi</s> does not increase, then how do pearls sprout on the ground? And having sprouted, how do they, becoming creepers spreading in all directions, abundantly bloom and bear fruit?

body.text:
lalitā vihasya - ārya madhumaṅgala! tat kiṃ bhavat-priya-vayasyasya siddheḥ
prabhāvaḥ ?
body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s>, laughing — Noble <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>! Is that then the power of your dear friend's <s>siddhi</s>?

body.text: madhumaṅgalaḥ - tat kasya ?
body.translated_text: <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> — Then whose [power] is it?

body.text: lalitā -- vṛndāvana-bhūmer eva |
body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s> — Of the land of <s>Vṛndāvana</s> itself!

body.text:
rādhā svagataṃ - lalite! etat kāminī-saṅgasya cety ucyatām iti rādhayoktaṃ
viśākhāpy anubhāṣitavatī |
body.translated_text: <s>Rādhā</s>, aside — '<s>Lalitā</s>! Let it also be said that this is [the result] of association with amorous women' — thus spoke <s>Rādhā</s>, and <s>Viśākhā</s> too echoed the same.

body.text: tato'haṃ - tat katham atraiva bhavatībhir upta-muktā hiṃsrā jātāḥ ?
body.translated_text: Then I [said] — Then how is it that the pearls sown by you ladies right here have become wild?

body.text: lalitā - bho vidagdha-śiromaṇe! muktāḥ kiṃ hiṃsrā bhavanti ?
body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s> — O crest-jewel of clever ones! Do pearls become wild?

body.text: mayoktaṃ - tat kathaṃ muktā notpannāḥ ?
body.translated_text: I said — Then how is it that pearls have not grown?

body.text: lalitā - bhūmi-viśeṣasya bījasya ca vaiguṇyāt |
body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s> — Because of the deficiency of both the particular soil and the seed!

body.text:
rādhā svagataṃ - lalite! kṣetrasyāsya guṇād apy ucyatām ity etad viśākhāpy
uktavatī |
body.translated_text: <s>Rādhā</s>, aside — '<s>Lalitā</s>! Let it also be said that it is due to the virtue of this field' — thus <s>Viśākhā</s> too has spoken.

body.text: nāndīmukhī - lalite! satyam eva kathayati viśākhā |
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s> — <s>Lalitā</s>! <s>Viśākhā</s> speaks the truth indeed!

body.text: lalitā - katham iva ?
body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s> — How so?

body.text:
nāndīmukhī - yasmāt sarvadā sarvāṅgīṇa-mukti-viṣa-vallari-mahoṣara-bhūmau
santata-paramānanda-kara-prema-bharojjvalita-bhakti-pīyūṣa-sura-valli-sarasatara
-mahā-kṣetre'smin vṛndāvane dhruvam āgantukā ye kecana jantavo bhaktā eva
bhavanti kathaṃ nu muktā bhavantu |
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s> — Because in this <s>Vṛndāvana</s> — which is a supremely fertile great field, ever overflowing with the most succulent celestial creeper of devotion blazing with the fullness of love that produces constant supreme bliss, a greatly barren land of the creeper of the poison of all-encompassing liberation — whatever beings come here inevitably become devotees; how could they become liberated?

body.text:
lalitā vihasya - viśākhe | sphuṭaṃ kāminī-saṅgasya iti bhavad-vāg-vilāso'pi
sa-sandarbho bhaviṣyati tad vivṛtya kathyatām |
body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s>, laughing — <s>Viśākhā</s>! Clearly your verbal play about 'association with amorous women' will also be well-composed — so explain it in full!

body.text:
viśākhā - ārūḍha-yogo'pi nipātyate'dhaḥ-saṅgena yogī kim utālpa-siddhir iti
nyāyenāsya kāye manasi gotre ca śyāmalatarasya sa-cchidra-vaṃśī-rasikasya
kṣaṇa-mātra-saṅgena muktā api bhūmau garbha-vāsena jananam āsādya
ca-cchidrībhūya saṃsāra-guṇa-baddhā babhūvuḥ |
