body.translated_text: <s>Viśākhā</s> — By the maxim 'Even a yogī who has advanced in yoga is cast down by association — what then of one with little <s>siddhi</s>?' — through even a moment's association with this one, who is supremely dark in body, mind, and lineage, and who delights in the flute full of holes, even the liberated ones, reaching birth through a sojourn in the womb upon the earth, became full of holes and bound by the qualities of <s>saṃsāra</s>.

body.text: tato'haṃ - viśākhe! nikhilam eva satyaṃ kathayasi |
body.translated_text: Then I [said] — <s>Viśākhā</s>! You speak the complete truth.

body.text: subalaḥ - vayasya! katham iva |
body.translated_text: <s>Subala</s> — Friend! How so?

body.text:
tato mayoktaṃ - mama kāma-vilāsādhyāpakasya saundarya-vaidaghdyādi-guṇān
viśeṣeṇa nāradādi-mukhād ākarṇya daṇḍakāraṇya-vāsino jīvan-muktāḥ
kaṭhora-tapasyākulam ācarya gokula-vane'smin pravara-gopa-gṛheṣu janim
aṅgīkṛtya vraja-vilāsinyo bhūtvā susāra-vaidagdhyādi-guṇair āvṛtya etā iva
mad-urasi sraja iva vilasanti | tathaivāpare parama-muktā api mad-acintya-guṇair
ākṛṣṭā asmin vraja-vane nitya-siddha-sthāvara-jaṅgameṣu
paśu-pakṣi-bhūruhādayo bhūtvā mām ānandayantaḥ paramānandam āsvādayanto
nandayanti |
body.translated_text: Then I said — Having heard from the mouths of <s>Nārada</s> and others especially about the qualities of beauty, cleverness, and so forth of me, the teacher of the arts of love, the liberated souls dwelling in the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest, undertaking severe austerities, accepted birth in the best cowherd households of this <s>Gokula</s> forest and, becoming <s>Vraja</s> damsels, adorned with the finest qualities of cleverness and the like, sport upon my chest like garlands. Likewise other supremely liberated ones too, attracted by my inconceivable qualities, have become the eternally perfect moving and stationary beings — animals, birds, trees, and so forth — in this <s>Vraja</s> forest, and delighting me, savoring supreme bliss, they rejoice.

body.text: subalaḥ - vayasya! sādhu varṇitam |
body.translated_text: <s>Subala</s> — Friend! Well described!

body.text:
lalitā kiñcid vihasya - mahā-siddhaś ced bhūmi-bheda-guṇaṃ vinā tava siddheḥ
prabhāvān muktā jāyante tarhi parama-siddho'pi bhavān
kiñcin-mātrādhika-dravya-lābhāya tad-vikraya-kṣudra-vṛttau kathaṃ pravṛtto'sti ?
body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s>, laughing slightly — O great <s>siddha</s>! If, without the special virtue of the land, pearls are born by the power of your <s>siddhi</s>, then why has one of supreme <s>siddhi</s> such as yourself engaged in the petty occupation of selling them for the sake of gaining a mere trifle more of wealth?

body.text:
tato'haṃ - mūrkhe lalitike! yauvana-dhana-garvitābhir bhavatībhir yathā
sva-dharmaṃ parityajya itas tataś cañcalyate tathā svadharma-pariniṣṭha-vaiśya
śiromaṇi-śrī-vraja-rājasya eka-putreṇa mayāpi svadharmaṃ parityajya kim
ucchṛṅkhalena bhavitavyam ? yataḥ kṛṣi-vāṇijya-go-rakṣā-kuśīdaṃ tūryam ucyate
iti vaiśyānām asmākaṃ catasro vṛttayo bhavanti | āsām eka-vṛttyācaraṇenaiva
sarva-siddher vṛddhis tac-catuṣṭayam ācarato mama punaḥ siddhiḥ
parama-kāṣṭhām ārūḍhaiva paraṃ virājate |
body.translated_text: Then I [said] — Foolish <s>Lalitā</s>! Just as you ladies, proud of the wealth of your youth, abandon your own <s>dharma</s> and wander about here and there restlessly, should I too — the only son of <s>Śrī Vraja-rāja</s>, the crest-jewel of <s>Vaiśyas</s> firmly established in his own <s>dharma</s> — abandon my own <s>dharma</s> and behave wantonly? For 'agriculture, trade, cattle-rearing, and money-lending are declared as the fourth [varṇa's occupations]' — we <s>Vaiśyas</s> have four occupations. By the practice of even one of these, all <s>siddhi</s> increases; for me, who practices all four, my <s>siddhi</s> reigns supreme, having ascended to the highest pinnacle.

body.text:
nāndīmukhī sa-smitaṃ - svadharma-niṣṭha-yuvarāja! bhavataḥ
kṛṣi-vāṇijya-gorakṣā-tisro vṛttayaḥ spaṣṭam anubhūyanta eva vṛddhi-jīvikā tu
kadāpi nāvakalitāsti |
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>, smiling — O crown-prince devoted to your own <s>dharma</s>! Your three occupations of agriculture, trade, and cattle-rearing are clearly experienced [by all]. But the occupation of money-lending has never been noticed.

body.text:
tato'haṃ - nāndīmukhi! sāpy asmābhiḥ kriyamāṇāpi tvayā kiṃ na jñāyate ?
sāmpratam api muktātyantābhāva-saṅkṣobhinībhir etābhiḥ saha
saṃkāmita-svadharmaṃ muktāpāra-vyāpāra-vṛddhi-vṛttiṃ vidhātum ārabdhavān
asmi |
viśākhā kiñcid vihasya - subala! yatra yo rajyati, sa khalu vinindyam api tad eva
ślāghyatayotkīrtayati | atas tāvat suṣṭhu adharmasyāpi śobhanatvena varṇanam
asya tva-priya-sakhasya nāyogyam |
body.translated_text: Then I [said] — <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>! Do you not know that it too is being practiced by us? Even now, agitated by the extreme scarcity of pearls, together with these [ladies], I have begun to conduct business in the pearl trade with my own <s>dharma</s> transferred [to this enterprise], to institute the occupation of profit through the pearl commerce. <s>Viśākhā</s>, laughing slightly — <s>Subala</s>! Wherever one is attached, one extols even that which is blameworthy as praiseworthy. Therefore it is not unfitting for this dear friend of yours to describe even <s>adharma</s> beautifully as if it were virtuous.

body.text:
subalo vihasya - nāndīmukhi! na kevalam asau dhanasya vṛddhiṃ labhate, kintv
anyeṣāṃ padārthānām api kṣaṇe kṣaṇe vṛddhiṃ labhamāno'sti ||
body.translated_text: <s>Subala</s>, laughing — <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>! Not only does he gain increase of wealth, but he is gaining increase of other things too, moment by moment!

body.text: nāndīmukhī -- kasya kasya ?
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s> — Of what [things]?

body.text:
subalaḥ - prathamaṃ pratyaṅge manasija-koṭi-vijayi-nava-tāruṇyasya netrāñcale
cañcala-kamala-vinindi-ghūrṇanasya bhāṣite ca sudhā-sārojjvala-mādhurīṇām |
body.translated_text: <s>Subala</s> — First, in every limb, of fresh youth that conquers ten million <s>Kāmadevas</s>; in the corner of the eyes, of a rolling [glance] that reproaches the restless lotus; and in speech, of sweetness radiant with the essence of nectar.

body.text: madhumaṅgalaḥ - subala! itara-padārthānāṃ vṛddhiṃ kiṃ tvayā vismṛtā ?
body.translated_text: <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> — <s>Subala</s>! Have you forgotten the increase of other things?

body.text: subalaḥ - smārya keṣām |
body.translated_text: <s>Subala</s> — Remind me — of what?

body.text:
madhumaṅgalaḥ -
makara-kuṇḍala-maṇi-mañjīra-hāra-valaya-keyūra-maṇi-mudrikādibhiḥ
parama-saundarya-darpādika-madhura-keli-vilāsānām |
body.translated_text: <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> — Of sweet amorous sports of supreme beauty and pride, [adorned] with <s>makara</s>-earrings, gem-anklets, necklaces, bracelets, armlets, gem-rings, and the like!

body.text: lalitā - ārya! anyataraika-vastunaḥ kathaṃ vṛddhiṃ saṅgopitavān asi |
body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s> — Noble one! How have you concealed the increase of one other thing?

body.text: nāndīmukhī - katarasya ?
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s> — Of which one?

body.text: lalitā - ballava-kula-sādhvīnām adharāmṛtocchiṣṭasya |
body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s> — Of the nectar-remnants from the lips of the virtuous women of the cowherd clan!

body.text:
rādhā sa-smitaṃ - lalite! satyaṃ satyaṃ vapur ākhyāti bhojanam ity etat
praguṇatara-rasāyana-pānenaiva bāhu-yugale
suvṛttendra-nīlārgalā-darpa-dalana-valanasya, vakṣasi
mārakata-kavāṭāhaṅkāra-vidhvaṃsi-vistārasya, ūru-dvaye ca
marakata-kadalī-stambha-garva-sarvaṅkaṣa-suvṛttitāyāḥ, vadane ca
śārada-śaśadhara-parārdha-mādhurya-saṅkoca-kāri-nirbhara-suṣamāyāḥ,
caraṇayoḥ nava-rasāla-pallava-praśasti-vitrāsi-mādhuryasya, sarvāṅge
madhuratara-sanniveśa-kuśala-lajjā-kāri-subhaga-sauṣṭhavasya, vapuṣi ca
nava-nava-mudirendīvaraindranīla-prabhā-hāri-visāri-prakaṭojjvalatā-bharasya,
yenāsya sakalāntaram apy abhivyāpya vilasitam iti tan mṛduu-bhāṣitāmṛtaṃ
viśākhayāpi sa-smita-sphuṭa-sulapita-kusumena suvāsitaṃ vyadhāyi |
body.translated_text: <s>Rādhā</s>, smiling — '<s>Lalitā</s>! Truly, truly, the body reveals one's nourishment' — thus, by drinking a most excellent <s>rasāyana</s> (elixir) alone: in the pair of arms, the grace that crushes the pride of well-rounded sapphire bolts; in the chest, the breadth that destroys the arrogance of emerald doors; in the pair of thighs, the well-roundedness that completely scrapes away the pride of emerald plantain pillars; in the face, the overflowing beauty that causes the supreme sweetness of the autumn moon to contract; in the feet, the sweetness that alarms the fame of fresh mango sprouts; in all limbs, the charming elegance that puts to shame the skillful arrangement of the sweetest forms; and in the body, the mass of manifest radiance that steals and surpasses the splendor of ever-fresh rain-clouds, blue lotuses, and sapphires — by which its entire interior too is pervaded and made radiant — thus that nectar of soft speech was perfumed by <s>Viśākhā</s> too with the flower of her smiling, clear, playful words.

body.text:
madhumaṅgalaḥ sa-parāmarśaṃ - vayasya! para-ramaṇī-madhurādhara-lolupaṃ
tvām etā dhūrtā miṣṭa-miṣṭa-vacana-mādhurī-bhareṇa parilobhayantyaḥ
pracuratara-vṛddhiṃ pratiśrāvya mauktikāny ādāya jaṭilādi-durgam āsthāya
mūlam api na dāsyanti | vṛddhi-vārtā tu dūre vartatām iti suṣṭhu vijñāyāhaṃ
mitreṇa hitam āśāṃsanīyam iti vijñāpayann asmi | agre tubhyaṃ yad rocate |
body.translated_text: <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>, remonstrating — 'Friend! These cunning ones, enticing you who are greedy for the sweet lips of other men's wives, with the weight of excessively sweet words, having promised abundant interest, will take the pearls and, retreating to the fortress of <s>Jaṭilā</s> and others, will not give even the principal. The talk of interest is far off indeed. Thus, knowing well that a friend should wish the best for a friend, I am advising you. Henceforth, whatever pleases you.'

body.text:
tato'haṃ daśanai rasanāṃ sandaśya - sakhe! imā gāndharvādayaḥ kulāṅganāḥ
prakāmādāna-pradāne mahā-śucayas tad ajānataiva tvayedam ucyate tac chrūyatāṃ
sāmpratam eva svādharāmṛtopaḍhaukanena mām atīva santoṣya gāndharvayā
mat-sakāśāt prātar gṛhīta-kamal-rāga-rekhikā-yugalena nija-vakṣoruhaṃ
paribhūṣya mad-urasi tad eva caturguṇīkṛtya sāyam eva vitīrṇam | lalitayā ca
paraśvaḥ sāyam amṛta-srāvi-cumbaka-ratnam ekam ādāya kali-krameṇa
tri-guṇī-kṛtya pariśodhitam | viśākhayāpi niśīthe paramāgraheṇa
man-madhurādharāmṛtam ādāya sva-sarva-bhūtaṃ tad eva prātar bahu-guṇīkṛtya
pradāya bāḍham āpyāyito'smi | campaka-latādayaś ca bāraṃ bāraṃ
sva-svābhīṣṭa-padārtham āgraheṇābhigṛhya kāścid dviguṇīkṛtya kāścit
triguṇīkṛtya pradāya mām atīva santoṣitavatyaḥ | kintu āsu jana-dvayī kevalaṃ
pradāne kiñcid anyādṛśa-vyavasāyā vartate |
body.translated_text: Then I, biting my tongue with my teeth — 'Friend! These <s>Gāndharvā</s> and others are noble clan-women, most scrupulous in generous giving and taking. You speak thus only out of ignorance. So listen — just now, by offering the nectar of her own sweet lips, <s>Gāndharvā</s> greatly delighted me; and the pair of ruby-streak earrings taken by her from me in the morning, having adorned her own bosom with them, was returned to my chest quadrupled that very evening. And <s>Lalitā</s>, the day before yesterday evening, having taken one ambrosia-dripping kiss-jewel, in the course of play, returned it tripled and settled the account. <s>Viśākhā</s> too, at midnight, having insistently taken the nectar of my sweet lips, early next morning returned that very same thing greatly multiplied, and thoroughly satisfied me. <s>Campakalatā</s> and the others too, again and again, having insistently taken their respective desired articles, some returning them doubled, some tripled, have thoroughly delighted me. But among these, a pair of two persons alone is somewhat of a different resolve regarding payment.'

body.text: nāndīmukhī - katarā sā ?
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s> — 'Who are those two?'

body.text:
tato'haṃ - ekā raṅgaṇavallī mad-vakṣasi
nija-vakṣaḥ-sthit-nistala-madhura-phala-yugalasya trirāropaṇam urīkṛtya
mat-kara-mardana-phala-dvayaṃ gṛhītvā sakṛd eva tad-arpitaṃ avaiśiṣṭaṃ
dvir-arpaṇaṃ gati-kriyām ācarya nādyāpi karoti | kācid anyā raṅgaṇamālā-sahacarī
tulasī nāmnī dviguṇīkṛtya dātum uktvā mad-eka-parirambha-stavakaṃ samādāya
sāmpratam idānīṃ deyaṃ tadānīṃ deyam iti kālaṃ kṣapayantī mūlam api na
dadāti |
body.translated_text: Then I said — 'One is <s>Raṅgaṇavallī</s>, who, having promised the triple offering upon my chest of the pair of smooth, sweet fruits situated on her own bosom, and having received the pair of fruits kneaded by my hands, made the offering but once and has not yet performed the promised second and third offerings, even now remaining remiss. Another, the companion of <s>Raṅgaṇamālā</s>, named <s>Tulasī</s>, having promised to give double, took from me a single cluster of embrace, and saying "I shall give now" and "I shall give then," keeps wasting time and does not give even the principal.'

body.text:
madhumaṅgalaḥ - ayi raṅgaṇavallī-tulasyau! yuvayoḥ sakāśād
albhyamānātma-divya-dravyo'pi priyaṃvado'smat-priya-vayasyaḥ sahaja-sāralyato
bhavad-vidhāsu priyam eva vakti | tathāpy etādṛśe'py asmin vañcana-cāturīm
ācarantībhyāṃ bhavatībhyāṃ kṛtaghnatvāt loka-dharmato bhayaṃ na kriyate |
body.translated_text: <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> — 'O <s>Raṅgaṇavallī</s> and <s>Tulasī</s>! Even though our dear friend <s>Priyaṃvada</s> (Sweet-speaker), who has not received his own celestial goods from you, says only pleasant things to ladies such as you out of innate simplicity — even so, do you who practice such arts of deception not fear the consequences of ingratitude according to worldly <s>dharma</s>?'

body.text:
tad ākarṇya cāru hasantī lalitā prāha - sakhyus tavārya madhumaṅgala! bhāṣitaṃ
tat pīyūṣataḥ priyataraṃ nahi kasya goṣṭhe pratyakṣaraṃ pratipadaṃ
tad-alīkatogra-śakrāśanasya nahi ced iha bhūri-gandhaḥ | tataḥ sahāsa-kolāhalaṃ
sādhu lalite! sādhu varṇitam iti sarvās tās tām āliṅgatavatyaḥ | rādhā ca tathaiva
manasā |
body.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Lalitā</s>, laughing beautifully, said — 'O noble <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>! Your friend's speech — is it not dearer than nectar? For is there anyone in the whole of <s>Goṣṭha</s> (the cowherd settlement) in whose ears, syllable by syllable, word by word, it does not strike like a fierce thunderbolt of <s>Indra</s> through its falsehood? If not, indeed there would be much fragrance here!' Then, with laughing uproar, all saying 'Well said, <s>Lalitā</s>! Well described!' embraced her. And <s>Rādhā</s> did the same in her heart.

body.text:
nāndīmukhī - mohana! katham apratītiḥ kriyate ? lalitā-prema-pātrīyaṃ
raṅgaṇa-mālikā, dvitīyā ca viśākhā-priya-śiṣyā tad etābhyām eva te prbodhya tad
avaśyaṃ dāpayiṣyate | yathā tābhyāṃ saha bhavataḥ śuddha-bhāvena punaḥ punar
eṣa vyavahāro nirvahati | yadi vā dāpayituṃ na śakyate tadā tad-avaśiṣṭa-dravyaṃ
tat-snehāt tābhyāṃ svayam eva dāpyate | ete api yadi te jhaṭiti dātuṃ nāṅgīkurutas
tarhi kenāpi bhavān anuyoktuṃ na śakyate | bhavatā tv
anaṅga-mañjarī-sahodarāgrataḥ kriyamāṇa eva phutkārārambhe tābhyām eva
sādhvasena svīkṛta-vṛddhi-sahitaṃ tad drutaṃ sutarāṃ vitariṣyate |
tataḥ sarvāsu nāndīmukhīṃ māṃ ca sa-bhrū-kuṭi-kauṭilyam īkṣamāṇāsu kiñcid
upasṛtya tuṅgavidyā sāntaḥ-smitam āha - bho bhoḥ sakhyaḥ! apūrvaikā vārtā
śrūyatām |
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s> — 'O charmer! Why is distrust created? This <s>Raṅgaṇamālikā</s> is the beloved of <s>Lalitā</s>, and the second is <s>Viśākhā</s>'s dear disciple — so you should be counseled through these two alone, and they will surely make them pay. Just as through pure affection with them your transactions continue again and again — and if they cannot make them pay, then whatever remaining goods they owe, those two will themselves pay out of affection for them. And even if these too do not agree to pay immediately, then no one can blame you. But if you were to begin hissing threats in the presence of <s>Anaṅga-mañjarī</s>'s elder sister, then those two, out of sheer fear, will quickly give what is owed together with the interest.' Then, as all were looking at <s>Nāndīmukhī</s> and at me with slightly furrowed brows, <s>Tuṅgavidyā</s> approached a little and, with an inner smile, said — 'O friends! Hear an extraordinary piece of news!'

body.text: sarvāḥ - sakhi! kā sā ?
body.translated_text: All — 'Friend! What is it?'

body.text: tuṅgavidyā - ekaḥ kānta-darpa-nāmācāryaḥ śruto'sti |
body.translated_text: <s>Tuṅgavidyā</s> — 'There is a teacher named <s>Kānta-darpa</s> (Pride of Love), it is heard.'

body.text: lalitā - paramparayā śruto'sti bhadreṇa na jñāyate |
body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s> — 'We have heard of him by tradition, but the good man is not known to us.'

body.text:
tuṅgavidyā - tat-priya-śiṣyeṇa śyāmala-miśra-nāmnā tat-kṛta-sūtrāṇāṃ
sandhi-catuṣṭayākhyāta-kṛd-vṛttaya iti vyākhyātāś catasro vṛttayo yāḥ kṛtāḥ santi
tāḥ kiṃ bhavatībhir dṛṣṭa-caryo bhavanti ?
body.translated_text: <s>Tuṅgavidyā</s> — 'His beloved student, named <s>Śyāmala-miśra</s>, has composed four commentaries called "<s>vṛttis</s> on the four <s>sandhis</s>" as an exposition of his master's <s>sūtras</s> — have you ladies seen their application?'

body.text:
viśākhā -- viṣṇu viṣṇu tad-vṛtti-darśanaṃ tāvad-dūre'stu sa eva kadāpi na
karṇa-gocarīkṛto'sti |
body.translated_text: <s>Viśākhā</s> — '<s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>! Far from seeing those commentaries — we have never even heard of them!'

body.text: lalitā sākūtaṃ - tuṅgavidye! kutrāsau tvayā paricitaḥ ?
body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s>, meaningfully — '<s>Tuṅgavidyā</s>! Where did you become acquainted with him?'

body.text:
tuṅgavidyā - sakhīsthalyā eka-mahā-padmāpsarasā tad-vṛtti-pāī̀ohārthaṃ taṃ
mṛgayituṃ sāya atrāgatam āsīt |
body.translated_text: <s>Tuṅgavidyā</s> — 'A great lotus-<s>apsaras</s> (celestial nymph) from the abode of a friend came here yesterday evening seeking the study of his commentary.'

body.text: tato'haṃ - tuṅgavidye! etāvad-dūra-bhūmau kathaṃ tat-sañcāraḥ ?
body.translated_text: Then I said — '<s>Tuṅgavidyā</s>! How does he travel across such vast distances?'

body.text:
tuṅgavidyā - nikāma-vanyāvṛddhi-sāmarthyena | ity ākarṇya sarvāḥ smitaṃ
kurvanti sma |
body.translated_text: <s>Tuṅgavidyā</s> — 'By the power of unbounded forest growth.' Hearing this, all smiled.

body.text: lalitā - tatas tataḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s> — 'Then? Then?'

body.text:
tuṅgavidyā - śyāmala-miśrādvitīyenālīka-rāja-paṇḍitena prathamaṃ
narma-pañjikā̆ā̆aṃ kraya-vikraya-pañjikāṃ ca vidhāya sāmpratam alīka-pañjikā
tathādāna-pradāna-pañjikā ca prapañcitā anukrameṇa nāmnāntareṇa ca
prapañcitaitat-pañjikā-catuṣṭayaṃ bhavatībhiḥ śrutam astīti manye |
body.translated_text: <s>Tuṅgavidyā</s> — 'Together with <s>Śyāmala-miśra</s>, a false royal scholar (<s>Alīka-rāja-paṇḍita</s>) first composed a jest-register (<s>narma-pañjikā</s>) and a buying-and-selling register (<s>kraya-vikraya-pañjikā</s>), and now has further elaborated a falsehood-register (<s>alīka-pañjikā</s>) and a giving-and-taking register (<s>ādāna-pradāna-pañjikā</s>). In sequence and also by other names, this set of four registers has been elaborated — I believe you ladies have heard of it.'

body.text: lalitā - atha kiṃ so'pi suṣṭhu anubhūyamāno'sti |
body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s> — 'Indeed! That too is being thoroughly experienced by us!'

body.text:
tuṅgavidyā - tebhyo'pi parama-samīcīna-tīvra-dhī-prāgalbhyena tat-satīrthena
kuhaka-bhaṭṭena tad-vrtti-catuṣṭayasya ṭīkā yugapat-kartum ārabdhāḥ santi |
body.translated_text: <s>Tuṅgavidyā</s> — 'Moreover, their fellow-student <s>Kuhaka-bhaṭṭa</s> (Master Fraud), with supremely excellent, acute, and bold intellect, has begun composing commentaries (<s>ṭīkās</s>) on all four of those treatises simultaneously.'

body.text:
campakalatā - tuṅgavidye! tvaṃ sarva-vidyā-viśāradāsi tad eṣāṃ catūrṇāṃ
śāstra-kāriṇāṃ nāma-dheya-niruktim avagantuṃ sarvās tvatto'bhilaṣanti |
body.translated_text: <s>Campakalatā</s> — '<s>Tuṅgavidyā</s>! You are learned in all arts, so all of us desire to understand from you the etymological derivation of the names of these four authors.'

body.text:
viśākhā - ācārya-bhaṭṭayor arthaḥ spaṣṭa eva tan-miśra-paṇḍitayoḥ sa tāvan
nirucyatām |
body.translated_text: <s>Viśākhā</s> — 'The meanings of <s>ācārya</s> (teacher) and <s>bhaṭṭa</s> (master) are quite clear; so let those of <s>miśra</s> and <s>paṇḍita</s> be explained.'

body.text: tuṅgavidyā vihasya - doṣo'py asti guṇo'py asti tena miśrena miśreta iti miśraḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Tuṅgavidyā</s>, laughing — 'There is both fault and virtue; being mixed (<s>miśra</s>) with them, he is a <s>Miśra</s>.'

body.text: nāndīmukhī - kataro vā doṣaḥ kataro vā gunaḥ ?
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s> — 'What is the fault and what is the virtue?'

body.text:
tuṅgavidyā - vaidagdhyāvaidagdhayor avicāreṇaiva yatra kutrāpi sarvatra pravṛttir
iti doṣaḥ | sāralyādhikyena uttamānuttamāvicāreṇaiva vaiṣamyaṃ vinā sarvatra
samatayā pravṛttir iti mahān guṇaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Tuṅgavidyā</s> — 'The fault is that, without discriminating between skill and lack of skill, he engages everywhere indiscriminately. The virtue is that, through excess of simplicity, without discriminating between high and low, he engages everywhere equally, without partiality — and this is a great virtue.'

body.text: lalitā smitvā - tad asyaitan-miśratā padavī samucitaiva |
body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s>, smiling — 'Then this "mixed" title is indeed well-suited to him.'

body.text: citrā - paṇḍito'pi nirucyatām |
body.translated_text: <s>Citrā</s> — 'Let <s>paṇḍita</s> be explained too.'

body.text:
tuṅgavidyā - sad-asad-vicārikā buddhiḥ paṇḍā | tayā yuktaḥ paṇḍitaḥ iti | ayaṃ tu
buddhi-gauraveṇa pūrva-parayoḥ para-vidhir balavān iti vicārya parā asad-vicārikā
yā sā paṇḍā tām evottaramtveāśritas tad-yuktatvāt paṇḍita iti |
body.translated_text: <s>Tuṅgavidyā</s> — '<s>Paṇḍā</s> is the intellect that discriminates between good and bad. One who possesses it is a <s>paṇḍita</s>. But this one, by the weighty principle that "between the former and the latter, the latter prevails," has taken refuge in the latter — namely, the <s>paṇḍā</s> that discriminates what is bad (<s>asad-vicārikā</s>) — and being possessed of that, he is a "<s>paṇḍita</s>."'

body.text: citrā - sakhi tuṅgavidye! sandhyādi-catuṣṭayasyāpy arthaḥ prakāśya kathyatām |
body.translated_text: <s>Citrā</s> — 'Friend <s>Tuṅgavidyā</s>! Let the meanings of the four <s>sandhis</s> and the rest also be clearly explained.'

body.text:
tuṅgavidyā - citre! asmad-goṣṭhyāṃ tat-prapañcena lalitaiva dakṣā tat saiva
kathayatu |
lalitā - citre! etat-prasaṅga-leśo'pi mayā kadāpi na śruto'pi tad
etat-prakaraṇa-vyākhyātrī tuṅgavidyaiva tad-arthaṃ jānāti |
body.translated_text: <s>Tuṅgavidyā</s>: '<s>Citrā</s>! In our gathering, it is <s>Lalitā</s> herself who is skilled in the elaboration of that subject — let her narrate it.' <s>Lalitā</s>: '<s>Citrā</s>! I have never even heard a trace of this topic. <s>Tuṅgavidyā</s> herself, who can explain this subject, knows its meaning.'

body.text: citrā - tuṅgavidye! mac-chirasā śāpitāsi tvayaiva vyākhyāyatām |
body.translated_text: <s>Citrā</s>: '<s>Tuṅgavidyā</s>! I adjure you by my head — you yourself must explain it!'

body.text:
tato'tilajjayā svayam asaṃkathya rādhikātiprīti-pātrīṃ manāg apy anucyamānāṃ
tadīya-sukhada-savidhāṃ bhū-cāraṇa-varya-kiśorīṃ tuṅganarmākhya-vaihāsikīṃ
cakṣuḥ-kūṇanena sa-smitam ālokayantyāṃ tuṅgavidyāyāṃ, tuṅganarmā kiñcit
sannidhāya sa-smita-man-mukham avalokayantī nijagāda - citre! sa tāvad
artho'smābhir na jñāyate kintu tayāpsarasā punaḥ punar āgatya sa-vinayaṃ svayam
āgraha-bhareṇa suprasannīkṛtāt yathārtha-padavīka-miśra-varād adhītya
tad-vṛtti-catuṣṭaya-vyākhyānam asmat-sahita-tuṅgavidyāgrataḥ sāṅgaṃ yad akāri
tat samāsena mayā kathyamānaṃ śṛṇuta -
body.translated_text: Then, out of extreme shyness, not speaking herself, when <s>Tuṅgavidyā</s> was looking with a wink and a smile at <s>Tuṅganarmā</s>, the foremost among jester-maidens roaming the earth who was the companion of the most delightful <s>Rādhikā</s> and was not being called upon even slightly — <s>Tuṅganarmā</s>, approaching a little, looking at their faces with a smile, spoke: '<s>Citrā</s>! We do not know that matter. But that celestial nymph, having come again and again and respectfully, with great earnestness, having herself been well propitiated, having studied from the one rightly called Miśra-vara the explanation of the four commentaries on that, performed a complete exposition before <s>Tuṅgavidyā</s> together with us. Listen as I narrate that in summary —'

body.text:
prathamaṃ śṛṇu dūtī-dvārā vā kṛtābhiyogena yūnor milanaṃ sandhiḥ | tasya vṛttir
vivaraṇa-matisārādir iti |
body.translated_text: 'First hear: the meeting of a young couple, whether through a messenger or through a declared effort, is called <s>sandhi</s> (union). Its <s>vṛtti</s> (mode) is <s>vivaraṇa</s> (exposition), <s>matisāra</s> (essence of thought), and so forth.'

body.text:
tataḥ kucālambha-pariṣvaṅga-cumbanādhara-pāna-rūpāṇāṃ śṛṅgāra-bhedānāṃ
catuṣṭayam eva catuṣṭayam | tasya tasya vṛttir nakha-kṣatādiḥ,
bāhu-bandha-bhṛṅgy-ādiḥ, gaṇḍa-sthale savilāsa-mukha-kamalāropaṇādiḥ,
savaidagdhya-daṃśādir iti |
body.translated_text: 'Then the four kinds of erotic variations — touching the breasts, embracing, kissing, and drinking of the lips — these four are indeed the four [types of <s>śṛṅgāra</s>]. The <s>vṛtti</s> of each is respectively: nail-scratching and the like; arm-binding and bee-like [hovering] and the like; placing the lotus of one's face playfully upon the cheek and the like; and skillful biting and the like.'

body.text:
tato'nyonya-narma-lapitam ākhyātam | tasya vṛttiḥ paraspara-jayākāṅkṣayā
nigūḍhārtha-prahelikādi-prayoga iti |
body.translated_text: 'Then mutual playful conversation (<s>narma-lapita</s>) is described. Its <s>vṛtti</s> is: the employment of riddles with hidden meaning and the like, for the purpose of mutual victory.'

body.text:
citrā sa-smitaṃ - tuṅganarman! aśruta-caraitad apūrvārtha-vyākhyānam
asmat-karṇa-gocarīkṛtaṃ, bhavatyā tat kṛd-vṛtter apy arthaḥ suṣṭhu nirucyatām |
body.translated_text: <s>Citrā</s>, smiling: '<s>Tuṅganarman</s>! This unprecedented explanation of matters never before heard has been brought within the range of our ears. Please also explain clearly the meaning of the verbal root and its derivative (<s>kṛd-vṛtti</s>).'

body.text:
tuṅganarmā -- ānandaṃ karotīti ānanda-kṛt sambhogaḥ | tasya vṛttiḥ
śītkāra-cakṣr nirmīlanādir iti | kiṃ ca kānta-darpācāryādy-avatāriṇā
kalāpa-priyeṇa siddha-kumāreṇānena tat-tad-vigrahāntareṇaiva yat
kalāpa-vyākaraṇam āvirbhāvitaṃ tatrātyantāpādeyatvena atiśaya-rahasyatvena ca
prakaṭam anigadya bhaṅgyā nāma-dheyāntareṇa ca yat kiñcit nigūhitaṃ tad
bhavad-vidha-rasika-snigdha-vidagdha-janair vidagdha-buddhi-sakhībhiḥ
samasadhika-vicāreṇa samanubhavanīyam iti |
body.translated_text: <s>Tuṅganarmā</s>: '<s>Ānanda-kṛt</s> means "that which produces bliss" — that is <s>sambhoga</s> (erotic union). Its <s>vṛtti</s> is: making the sound "śīt," closing of the eyes, and so forth. Furthermore, regarding the <s>Kalāpa-vyākaraṇa</s> (analysis of the peacock-feather garland) that was revealed by this accomplished prince (<s>siddha-kumāra</s>), the <s>Kalāpa-priya</s> (lover of the garland / grammar), who descended as <s>Kānta-darpācārya</s> (teacher of the pride of love) and others, through each of those different embodiments — what was not openly stated due to its extreme preciousness and supreme secrecy, but was concealed through indirect expression and under different names — that should be savored through equal and superior investigation by affectionate, refined connoisseurs like yourselves, with the help of witty-minded female friends.'

body.text:
campakalatā kiñcid vihasya - tuṅgavidye! etad-bhaṭṭa-pādānāṃ tvāv eva bhujau
tatrāpy atīva sukumārau tat katham ekadaiva ṭīkā-catuṣṭayaṃ lekhituṃ śaknotu |
body.translated_text: <s>Campakalatā</s>, laughing a little: '<s>Tuṅgavidyā</s>! This learned master has only these two arms, and those exceedingly delicate — how could he write four commentaries at once?'

body.text:
tuṅgavidyā -- mugdhe! nijendra-jāla-balenāyaṃ bhuja-catuṣṭayam api
prāduṣkartuṃ śaknoti |
body.translated_text: <s>Tuṅgavidyā</s>: 'O naive one! By the power of his own <s>indrajāla</s> (magic), he is capable of manifesting even four arms!'

body.text:
lalitā -- satyaṃ satyaṃ vāsantika-rāsollāsa-mahotsave
parama-rāsa-sthalī-nikaṭa-varti-praviṣṭaka-nāmāraṇya-khaṇḍāntar-nikuñjāntar
āle'pi para-rāmā-ratnam apahartuṃ nikhila-ballavī-vṛnda-vañcanāya ca
sva-paricyāyakādbhuta-nija-mādhurī-santatim avaguṇṭhya kuhaka-balād evānena
caturbhujatvam āviṣkṛtam āsīt |
body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s>: 'Truly, truly! At the great spring <s>Rāsa</s>-festival of delight, near the supreme <s>Rāsa</s>-ground, within a bower deep inside the forest grove called <s>Praviṣṭaka</s>, in order to steal the gem among other women and to deceive the entire company of cowherd girls, concealing the continuous stream of his own extraordinary sweetness by the force of his magic, he indeed manifested his four-armed form!'

body.text:
viśākhā - lalite! satyam etat sarvam asyakuhaka-bala-vijṛmbhitam eva yat
priya-sakhyā saha gadya-padyair narmālāpa-goṣṭhyāṃ tāṃ jetuṃ
nija-kuhaka-pāṇḍityena samprati vṛddhi-vṛttim ācaratā pada-dvayasya vṛddhiḥ
kadācid yad anena kriyate tac cāsmābhir api dṛṣṭam asti |
body.translated_text: <s>Viśākhā</s>: '<s>Lalitā</s>! Truly, all this is nothing but the display of his magical power. When engaging in playful conversation in prose and verse with his dear friend, trying to defeat her through his scholarly magical skill, he now practices the <s>vṛddhi</s>-augmentation rule for two syllables — we have even seen him do that sometimes!'

body.text:
sudevī - viśākhe! caturṇām eteṣāṃ śāstra-kāriṇāṃ prāyeṇaika eva vyavasāyaḥ
kathaṃ dṛśyate ?
body.translated_text: <s>Sudevī</s>: '<s>Viśākhā</s>! These four composers of <s>śāstras</s> appear to have practically the same single enterprise — how is that?'

body.text:
nāndīmukhī - sudevi! etad vivaraṇam alpākṣareṇa tuṅganarmaṇā yad akāri tat kiṃ
tvayā nahi śrutam ?
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>: '<s>Sudevī</s>! Did you not hear the brief explanation that <s>Tuṅganarman</s> gave about this?'

body.text:
sudevī - yāva-grāma-stha-priya-sakhyāṃ tadānīṃ datta-manaskayā mayā tat
samyaktayā nāvadhāritaṃ tat kṛpayā tvayaiva vistareṇa saṃkathya śrāvyatām |
body.translated_text: <s>Sudevī</s>: 'At that time my mind was fixed upon my dear friend who was at <s>Yāva</s>-village. I did not attend to it properly. Please kindly narrate it in detail.'

body.text:
nāndīmukhī - sudevi! śrūyatām | vastuta ete catvāraḥ kuhaka-bhaṭṭa-nāmā eka
eva kumāro bhavati | sa eva kṛtya-bheda-vinoda-sampādanāyātmanaḥ
prakṛṣṭatara-kuhaka-prabhāvāt prakaṭitenaikena vigraheṇaiva kānta-darpācārya
iti apareṇa śyāmala-miśra iti padavīm adhyārūḍho vartate | alīka-rāja-paṇḍitena
samaṃ tu sphuṭam asya pṛthag-vigrahatā nāsty eva kintv ayam eva sadā dharmī
kumāraḥ | sphuṭam atra vilāsa-viśeṣollāsa-karaṇāya kiñcit
prakāśa-bhedenālīka-rāja-paṇḍiteti nāmāntaram urarīkṛtya kāmam ātmīyānām
ātmanaś ca paramānanda-kallolam āsphālayan viharate |
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>: '<s>Sudevī</s>, listen! In truth, these four are a single prince named <s>Kuhaka-bhaṭṭa</s> (Magician-Scholar). He himself, for the entertainment of diverse playful tasks, by the power of his own superior magic, has adopted in one openly manifested form the title <s>Kānta-darpācārya</s> (Teacher of the Pride of Love), and in another the title <s>Śyāmala-miśra</s>. With <s>Alīka-rāja-paṇḍita</s> (the Illusory Royal Scholar), there is clearly no actual separate embodiment — rather, this very prince is the constant subject. Clearly, in order to produce the delight of special amorous play, assuming a somewhat different mode of manifestation and adopting the alternate name <s>Alīka-rāja-paṇḍita</s>, he freely sports, making waves of supreme bliss for his own circle and for himself.'

body.text:
tato'haṃ - haṃho! yac caturbhujatvādika-līlāyitam akhilam asmābhiḥ
siddhatā-prabhāvair evāvirbhāvyate | tan mūrkhābhir ābhir ugrābhiḥ
kuhaka-bhaṭṭābhir nija-nikṛṣṭa-kuhaka-prabhāvair eveti santatam udghuṣyate |
body.translated_text: Then I [said]: 'Ha! All these playful displays such as the four-armed form and the like are manifested by us through the power of <s>siddhi</s> (perfection). But these foolish, fearsome women — these <s>Kuhaka-bhaṭṭa</s>-women — ceaselessly proclaim that it is all through the power of their own inferior magic!'

body.text:
iti mad-vacaḥ samākarṇya sarvāḥ - anena siddha-gosvāminā sva-prabhāveṇa
nijālīkatāpi siddhī-sampādya sva-mukhenaiva paraṃ nirdhāritā vyadhāyīti sarvair
nirbharam ullāsyamāne hāsa-kutūhale |
body.translated_text: Hearing my words, all of them [said]: 'This <s>Siddha-gosvāmin</s>, by his own power, has himself established even his own fictitiousness as a perfection and declared it openly from his own mouth!' — and all were overflowing with laughter and delight.

body.text:
ahaṃ svagataṃ - bho āścaryam āścaryam amūbhir vāvadūka-ballavībhir
vacana-prakāśa-paripāṭībhir bāḍham alīkataiva mayi siddhīkṛteti manasi vibhāvya
lajjayā mayā tad-anākarṇita-mudrayaiva tāḥ suṣṭhv avadhāryeva kiñcid vihasya
vyāhṛtaṃ - bho mugdhā yauvanāndhā vilāsinyaḥ! yady atra nahi vaḥ pratītis tarhi
sarveṣāṃ samakṣam eva sva-siddhiṃ darśayan prathamam asyāḥ kaṇṭhe vana-mālā
bhavāni iti vihasya campakalatām upasarpan - vayasya siddhasya tava
para-ramaṇī-sparśaḥ parama-nyāyya iti vihasya vadatā madhumaṅgalena
nivartito'ham avadaṃ - sakhe! siddhasya siddhayā saṃyogo mithaḥ
paramānanda-lābhāyaiva bhavati | uktaṃ ca śrī-nāradena - paramānanda-lābhāya
sva-yūthyām eva saṃśrayed iti |
body.translated_text: I [said] to myself: 'How wonderful, how wonderful! By these talkative cowherd women, through their ordered display of clever speech, my fictitiousness has indeed been established in their minds.' Conceiving this and out of embarrassment, with a pretense of not hearing, having noted them well, laughing a little, I declared: 'O naive, youth-intoxicated, playful women! If you have no faith in this, then I shall demonstrate my <s>siddhi</s> before everyone's eyes — first I shall become a forest garland upon this one's neck!' — and laughing, approaching <s>Campakalatā</s> — I was stopped by <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> who said laughingly: 'Friend! For a perfected one, touching another's woman is most improper!' I said: 'Friend! The union of a perfected one with a perfected woman is for the mutual attainment of supreme bliss. And <s>Śrī Nārada</s> has said: "For the attainment of supreme bliss, one should resort to a woman of one's own group."'

body.text:
iti niśamya hasantīṣu sarvāsu paramānanda-janita-kampādi-sāttvika-vikārān
bhaneevācchādayantī campakalatā prapalāyya kuñjāntarāle praviṣṭā rādhāṃ
pṛṣṭhe samāliṅgya nilīnāsīt |
body.translated_text: Hearing this, while all were laughing, <s>Campakalatā</s>, unable to conceal the <s>sāttvika</s> transformations (trembling and the like) born of supreme bliss, fled and entered the depths of a bower, embraced <s>Rādhā</s> from behind, and hid.

body.text:
tato'haṃ citrāṃ mauktikāni haste cālayann uktavān - citre! samakṣam āgatya
mauktika-mūlyaṃ śṛṇu śṛṅgāra-karma-vicakṣaṇāyās tava mūrti-mañjuṣikāyāṃ
tat-sādhanāni bahūni santīti tvat-prāṇa-preṣṭha-sakhyā kathitam asti | tair
vicitra-śṛṅgāreṇa mat-pratyaṅgāni tathā bhūṣaya yathāham api
tvad-vakṣaḥ-stha-kāñcana-ghaṭa-dvayam ardha-candra-patrāṅkurādibhiḥ
santoṣeṇālaṅkṛtya tām ānandayāmīti |
body.translated_text: Then I, moving pearls in my hand, said to <s>Citrā</s>: '<s>Citrā</s>! Come before me and hear the price of these pearls. Your dearest friend has told me that in your bodily jewel-box there are many means for the adornment of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic arts). With those, adorn my limbs with variegated ornaments so that I too may adorn the two golden pots upon your chest with half-moon leaf-sprouts and the like, and thereby delight her!'

body.text:
tac chravaṇataḥ sa-krodhaṃ citrā - aye aviratam
ativikaṭa-bhaṇḍatoccaṇḍa-caṇḍikāviṣṭa! aye trijagati
prasiddha-dhṛṣṭatodbhaṭa-bāṭikā-kuraṅga-kuṭumbinī-kula-naṭa! tva-yogyābhis
tat-tat-sādhana-karma-karmaṭhābhis tābhir eva sa-santoṣaṃ sucitritena bhavatā tā
eva suślāghaṃ suvareṇa santatam anukīrtyantāṃ itas tvaritam apasaratu svāmī |
body.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Citrā</s> angrily: 'Oh you who are ceaselessly possessed by terribly vulgar, fierce <s>Caṇḍikā</s>! Oh you who are famous in the three worlds as the bold theater-deer and clan-dancer of the <s>Kuṭumbinī</s> family! Let your worthy accomplices skilled in those various arts ceaselessly and contentedly praise you, O well-painted one! Master, quickly remove yourself from here!'

body.text: ity ākarṇanena jāta-hāsāḥ sarvās tāṃ suṣṭhu tuṣṭuvuḥ |
body.translated_text: Hearing this, all burst into laughter and heartily praised her.

body.text:
tad anu nāndīmukhī - gokula-maṅgala!
sakala-gokula-jana-jīvātu-mukha-candra-prakāśaṃ bhavantaṃ akasmād vimanaskam
iva saṃvīkṣya bhavad-ekāyuṣām asmākaṃ hṛdayāni
marma-vraṇa-vedanā-vahni-jvālitānīva sphuṭanti santi | tatas tan-nidānam avaśyaṃ
kṛpayā prakāśyatām | yathā bhagavatī-dvārā tat-pratīkāraṃ jhaṭiti niṣpādya
śrīmantaṃ bhavantaṃ bāḍham ānandaivātmānaṃ sandhukṣayāma |
body.translated_text: Then <s>Nāndīmukhī</s> said: O auspicious one of <s>Gokula</s>! Seeing you, whose moon-like face is the very life-elixir of all the people of <s>Gokula</s>, suddenly becoming as if distressed in mind, our hearts — for whom you alone are our life — are bursting as though set ablaze by the fire-flames of pain from a wound to our vital parts. Therefore, please mercifully reveal the cause of this, so that through the grace of <s>Bhagavatī</s> we may swiftly accomplish a remedy for it and thoroughly fan the flames of joy in your blessed self.

body.text:
iti nāndīmukhī-vacanam ākarṇya savaiklavyam iva mayoktaṃ -- nāndīmukhi
śrūyatām |
adṛṣṭāśruta-cara-cāru-cāturya-niravadya-mahā-vaidagdhya-viovidha-sudurbodha
-narma-karma-svādhyāya-prathamācāryāyāḥ
samasta-kalyāṇa-guṇa-maṇi-mañjuṣāyāḥ
sva-parijana-gaṇa-jīvanī-bhūta-smita-nava-ghana-sāra-suvāsita-bhāṣita-pīyūṣāyāḥ
śacy-ādi-saubhāgyavatī-vṛnda-varṇyamān-saubhāgya-bharāyāḥ santatam
indirādi-gaurī-gaṇa-mṛgyamāṇa-saundarya-rasa-sphurita-nakhāñcala-pratīkāyāḥ
sura-nara-gaṇa-gandharva-vidyādhara-muni-vara-vandita-bhuvaneśvarī-śata-vand
yamāna-padāravindāyāḥ, samasta-vaikuṇṭhato'pi paramottama-parama-vyomato'pi
bṛṃhita-mahā-mahimottara-vṛndāṭavī-mahā-yoga-pīṭha-mahā-siṃhāsane
saṃbhṛta-mahāratnābhiṣekāyāḥ mahādevyāḥ
sudhā-sāgara-mathanotthita-rādhety-akṣara-yugala-ghanībhūta-tat-sārāṃśa-kalas
a-dvaya-vinirmita-rādheti-nāma-dheyād
apūrvāmṛta-sāra-vikāra-viśeṣeṇāpyāyita-śītkārita-caturdaśa-bhuvanāyāḥ,
santata-saurabhya-niravadhi-saundarya-nistula-kaumalya-nirbhara-varāruṇyādi-vin
irjita-raktotpala-kula-caraṇa-paricaraṇaika-jīvine sakala-varivasyā-viśāradāya
mahyaṃ svayam āhūyāsaṅkocatayā mat-kāmita-pratyaṅga-sevā yat tayā na dīyate |
atas tasya mayi madhurāṃ prītim anavadhārya tat-pūrṇāṃśāṃ yathārtha-nāmnīṃ
tuṅgavidyāṃ bhagavatī-mukhāt niśamya satvarābhīṣṭa-lābhāya enāṃ
gurutvenāsādyāsyāḥ sakāśāt mahādevī-mantra-rājaṃ didīkṣiṣur ahaṃ tvāṃ
bhagavaty-advitīyāṃ prapanno'smi |
body.translated_text: Hearing these words of <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>, I spoke as if with agitation: O <s>Nāndīmukhi</s>, listen! She who is the foremost preceptress in the self-study of the craft of <s>narma</s> (amorous jest) — of unseen, unheard-of, wondrous, beautiful, skillful, faultless, great <s>vaidagdhya</s> (cleverness), of manifold and most difficult-to-comprehend varieties; she who is the jewel-casket of all auspicious qualities; she whose speech is nectar perfumed with the essence of fresh clouds of smiles that are the very life-giving elixir of her retinue; she whose burden of good fortune is praised even by the assemblies of fortunate women headed by <s>Śacī</s>; she whose very toenail-tips shimmer with the essence of beauty perpetually sought after by the hosts of <s>Indirā</s> and the company of <s>Gaurī</s> and others; she whose lotus feet are worshipped by hundreds of <s>Bhuvaneśvarīs</s> who are themselves adored by the best among gods, humans, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Vidyādharas</s>, and sages; she who has been ceremonially anointed with great jewels upon the great throne of the great <s>yoga-pīṭha</s> (sacred seat) of <s>Vṛndāṭavī</s> (the forest of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>), whose surpassing great glory exceeds even the supreme <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> and even the highest transcendent sky; she, the <s>Mahādevī</s> (Great Goddess), whose name <s>Rādhā</s> — that pair of syllables condensed from the quintessential portion of the nectar-ocean churned forth — whose extraordinary transformation of unprecedented ambrosial essence has refreshed and cooled all fourteen worlds with delight; — to me, who lives solely for the service of her feet which have vanquished the dynasty of red lotuses by their perpetual fragrance, boundless beauty, incomparable tenderness, and abundant lovely reddishness, and who am expert in all forms of devoted attendance — she herself summoned me, yet out of shyness does not grant me the service of her limbs that I desire. Therefore, unable to ascertain her sweet affection toward me, having heard from <s>Bhagavatī</s> of <s>Tuṅgavidyā</s>, who bears the fitting name 'lofty knowledge' and who is the full portion of that affection — desiring to quickly obtain my heart's desire, I wish to approach her as my <s>guru</s> and receive from her the <s>mantra-rāja</s> (king of mantras) of the <s>Mahādevī</s>. I take refuge in you, O incomparable attendant of <s>Bhagavatī</s>!

body.text:
nāndīmukhī vihasya | sulakṣaṇa prathamaṃ tāvat śāstra-nirṇīta-gurūpasattir
vidhīyatām |
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s> laughed and said: O auspicious one, first let the proper approach to the <s>guru</s> as prescribed by the scriptures be duly performed!

body.text:
mayoktam | bhadraṃ vacaḥ prathamaṃ guru-śiṣyayoḥ parīkṣaiva nyāyyā | tatas
tisras triyāmāḥ kutrāpi nirjana-kuñje kṣaṇe mahilāṃ kṣaṇe pumāṃsaṃ māṃ
sampādya sva-vidyāyāḥ prabhāvam asau darśayatu | tato viśrabhya
parama-sambhrameṇa mayāpy asyāś
caraṇa-yāvābharaṇa-śroṇi-mardana-vakṣoja-kaṇḍūyana-veṇī-bandhanādi-paricaryās
sarvāpekṣayā kriyamāṇāsu suprasanneyaṃ tvat-sevayā parama-prasannāsmīti
nirucya māṃ manobhavānanda-kara-nikuñja-maṇḍapa-vedikāṃ prāpayya bho
vicakṣaṇa mad-vakṣaḥ-sthala-kārttasvara-maṅgala-ghaṭa-yugalaṃ svakara-yugalena
spṛśan mṛgamada-kuṅkumādi-paṅka-lepa-pūrvakaṃ maṇi-puṣpa-mālābhir
veṣṭayety ādibhāṣitamantrair ghaṭaṃ sthāpayitvā,
sva-vakṣoja-mahā-prasāda0kuṅkumena mama lalāṭādiṣu tilakaṃ kṛtvā
mṛgamadena mad-vakṣasi mahā-devī-nāma-mudrām abhilikhya bāhu-dvayaṃ ca
tac-caraṇa-cihna-saubhāgya-mudrābhir aṅkīkṛtya sva-kaṇṭhād ekāvalī-mālām
uttārya mat-kaṇṭhe nidhāya mama vakṣaḥ-pārśvayoḥ sva-kucau aṃsa-dvaye
bāhulate mukhe ca svādharaṃ aparāṅgānyāgamānabhijñena mayā sphuṭam
ajñātāny api paramāgamācāryeyaṃ svayaṃ tad-arpaṇa-sthāne'rpayatu iti ṣaḍ-aṅgāni
vinyasya ṣaḍ-akṣara-mantra-rājasyāsya svayambhū-ṛṣi-gāyatrī chandaḥ
śrī-gāndharvā devatā sa-bindu-prathama-varṇo bījaṃ śaktir upāsyopāsakayor
mithaḥ-suyukta-rati-janana-pūrvakābhīṣṭa-kāma-siddhaye viniyoga ity ādi
pūrvāṅgaṃ yathā-vidhi sampādya,
body.translated_text: I said: Very well! First, indeed, a mutual examination between <s>guru</s> and disciple is proper. Therefore, for three nights, in some secluded bower, transforming me one moment into a woman and one moment into a man, let her demonstrate the power of her <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge). Then, with confidence and supreme eagerness, as I perform for her all manner of services — anointing her feet with lac-dye, massaging her hips, scratching her breasts, braiding her hair, and so forth — when she is well-pleased, let her declare 'I am supremely pleased by your service,' and then lead me to a bower-pavilion-platform that bestows the bliss of <s>Manobhava</s> (the god of love), saying: 'O clever one, touch with both your hands the pair of golden auspicious water-pots upon my chest, and smearing them first with a paste of musk and saffron, encircle them with garlands of gems and flowers' — with such spoken <s>mantras</s> let her establish the pots. Then, making a <s>tilaka</s> on my forehead and other parts with the <s>kuṅkuma</s> <s>mahā-prasāda</s> (great grace) from her own breasts, inscribing the seal of the <s>Mahādevī</s>'s name on my chest with musk, marking both my arms with the auspicious seals bearing the signs of her feet, removing the single-strand necklace from her own neck and placing it upon mine, and then — her own breasts upon the sides of my chest, her arms upon both my shoulders, and her own lower lip upon my mouth — and the remaining limbs, unknown clearly to me who am unversed in the <s>Āgamas</s> (tantric scriptures), let this supreme preceptress of the <s>Āgamas</s> herself place them in their proper positions of offering. Thus having arranged the six limbs, and having duly completed the preliminary rites — the self-born sage is the <s>ṛṣi</s> of this king of six-syllabled <s>mantras</s>, <s>Gāyatrī</s> is its meter, <s>Śrī Gāndharvā</s> is the deity, the first syllable with <s>bindu</s> is the seed, the <s>śakti</s> is as stated, and its application is for the fulfillment of one's desired aims through the mutual well-joined <s>rati</s> (union) of the worshipped and the worshipper —

children.translated_text: Then, upon the stage of the bower on the bank of her own lake, joyfully,
playfully delighting the rows of assembled spectators with humorous dances —
She who is fair-complexioned, clad in red garments, beautiful, with lovely eyes and a sweetly smiling face,
the dark one, the fulfiller of all desires of <s>Śyāma</s> (the dark one, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) — I take refuge in <s>Rādhikā</s>.

body.text:
iti dhyānaṃ ca suciraṃ kārayitvā kṛpayā mahyaṃ kāmine kāma-bīja-puṭitaṃ
mantra-rājam upadiśya māṃ kṛtārthīkarotu |
body.translated_text: Having thus made me meditate upon this <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation verse) for a long time, may she mercifully instruct me, the lover, in the <s>mantra-rāja</s> (king of mantras) enclosed within the <s>kāma-bīja</s> (seed syllable of desire), and thereby fulfill me!

body.text: tad anu --
body.translated_text: Then follows —

children.translated_text: She whose form is manifested from the blazing <s>cintā-ratna</s> (wish-fulfilling jewel) of great <s>bhāva</s> (divine emotion),
she who shines splendidly with the finest fragrant unguent of the loving affection of her <s>sakhīs</s> (girlfriends), ||1||
Bathed by the waves of the nectar of compassion, by the streams of the nectar of youth,
and by the floods of the nectar of charm — she who puts <s>Indirā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) to shame, ||2||
She whose limbs are veiled by the silken garment of modesty, anointed with the saffron of beauty,
her body artfully decorated with the dark, radiant musk of <s>Śyāmala</s> (her dark beloved), ||3||
Trembling, tears, horripilation, stupefaction, perspiration, choked voice, and reddening,

children.text: unmādo jāḍyam ity etai rathanir navabhir uttamaiḥ ||4||
children.translated_text: ecstasy and stupor — with these nine supreme <s>ratnas</s> (jewels, i.e., <s>sāttvika-bhāvas</s>), ||4||
she is embraced by ornaments fashioned from these, wearing garlands of flowers strung from her qualities,
adorned with the perfumed garments of her steadfast-and-restless nature, ||5||
Her hair-braid is concealed <s>māna</s> (jealous pique), her <s>tilaka</s> gleams with good fortune,
her ears are delighted by earrings made of hearing <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s name and fame, ||6||
Her lips are reddened by the betel of passionate attachment, her collyrium is the crookedness of <s>prema</s> (divine love),
she is perfumed with the camphor of smiles flowing from playful speech, ||7||
Within the inner palace of her fragrance, upon the couch of pride, playfully
she is seated, adorned with the restless agitation of the wonders of <s>prema</s>, ||8||
Her breasts are concealed by the fine bodice tied with loving anger,
she is the finest <s>kacchapī</s> <s>vīṇā</s> (lute) of fame and beauty that desiccates the faces and hearts of her co-wives, ||9||
In the midst of her own <s>sakhīs</s>, her lotus-hand playfully resting upon their shoulders,
the dark one, she who serves the honey-wine of the fragrant love-god's delight to <s>Śyāma</s>, ||10||

children.text: tvāṃ natvā yācate dhṛtvā tṛṇaṃ dantair ayaṃ janaḥ |
children.translated_text: Bowing to you, this person begs, holding a blade of grass between his teeth:
Revive this greatly suffering one by sprinkling him with the nectar of servitude to you! ||11||

children.text: na muñcec charaṇāyātam api duṣṭaṃ dayāmayaḥ |
children.translated_text: A compassionate one does not abandon even a wicked person who has come seeking shelter;

children.text: ato gāndharvike hā hā muñcainaṃ naiva tādṛśam ||12||
children.translated_text: therefore, O <s>Gāndharvikā</s> (<s>Rādhā</s>), alas, alas! Do not abandon this one who is such (a supplicant)! ||12||
This <s>stava-rāja</s> (king of hymns) named '<s>Premāmbhoja-maranda</s>' (the honey of the lotus of divine love) —
whoever recites it, which is the cause of <s>Śrī Rādhikā</s>'s mercy, shall attain servitude to her. ||13||

body.text: imaṃ stava-rājam apy upadiśatu ||
body.translated_text: Let her instruct me in this <s>stava-rāja</s> (king of hymns) as well!

body.text:
tataḥ śrī-guror labdhābhīṣṭa-kāmo'smi iti sagadgadaṃ vadantaṃ sakampaṃ
tac-caraṇa-kamalayoḥ patitaṃ māṃ sānandaṃ samutthāpya samāliṅgya
svādharocchiṣṭa-pīyūṣa-prasādaṃ saṃbhojya ca sva-mukhodgīrṇa-tāmbūlaṃ
man-mukhe vitaratu | brahmacāriṇo mama tāmbūla-bhakṣaṇam anucitam iti cet
tarhi karpūra-vāsita-nija-mukha-vāsena man-mukha-śuddhiṃ vitanotu | tataḥ
kṛtārthena mayaitad-abhīpsitāni anyāny api bahūni ca muktāphalāni dakṣinātvena
samarpyamāṇāni kṛpayā svīkṛtya mām anugṛhṇātu ||
body.translated_text: Then, as I said with faltering voice 'I have obtained my heart's desire from <s>Śrī Guru</s>!' and fell trembling at her lotus feet, let her joyfully raise me up, embrace me, feed me the nectar-<s>prasāda</s> (grace) of the remnants of her own lips, and place in my mouth a betel that has been in her own mouth. If it be said that betel-chewing is improper for me, a <s>brahmacārī</s> (celibate student), then let her purify my mouth with the camphor-scented fragrance of her own mouth. Thereupon, let her graciously accept the many <s>muktāphalas</s> (pearls — also: fruits of liberation) and other desired offerings presented by me, now fulfilled, as <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (ritual fee), and thus bestow her grace upon me!

body.text:
iti niśamya sarvāsu sa-smitaṃ tuṅgavidyā-mukham avalokayantīṣu tayāpy
ucchalitāntarānandam āvṛtya bhrū-bhaṅgena saroṣam iva mām īṣad avalokya
bhāṣitaṃ | nāndīmukhi tvaṃ siddhā tapasviny asi | tasmād etad-vidhinā tvam
evainaṃ dīkṣaya | tadāsya siddhāto mantra-grahaṇāt svābhīṣṭa-kāma-lābho jhaṭiti
sampatsyata iti vyāhṛtya sakrodhaṃ gṛhāya gacchantīṃ kareṇa gṛhītvā vyāghoṭya

children.text: viśākhā vihasya nāndīmukhīṃ prāha -- nāndīmukhi! asya samprati
children.translated_text: <s>Viśākhā</s> laughed and said to <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>: O <s>Nāndīmukhi</s>! For this one who has now

children.text: prāpta-vyalīkasya dīkṣā-dāne mahān eva pratyavāyaḥ syād ity ācāryeyaṃ tvāṃ
children.translated_text: committed an offense, there would be a great calamity in giving him initiation — that is why the <s>Ācāryā</s> (preceptress, i.e., <s>Tuṅgavidyā</s>) is
angry with you!

body.translated_text: Hearing this, as all the <s>sakhīs</s> looked with smiles toward the face of <s>Tuṅgavidyā</s>, she too suppressed the joy surging within her and, with a furrowed brow, glanced at me as if with anger and said: <s>Nāndīmukhi</s>, you are an accomplished <s>tapasvinī</s> (ascetic woman). Therefore, you yourself initiate him according to this procedure! Then, since his reception of the <s>mantra</s> would be from a <s>siddhā</s> (perfected one), he will swiftly attain his desired object! — Having said this, as she was leaving angrily for home, catching her by the hand and pulling her back,

body.text:
nāndīmukhī -- mithyā-vādini viśākhe! sakala-sadharma-rājīva-bandhor
gokula-rājasya sat-tanaye katham alīka-parivādam āropayasi |
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s> said: O false-speaking <s>Viśākhā</s>! How can you cast a false accusation upon the good son of the king of <s>Gokula</s>, who is the friend of all the righteous, like the sun to the lotuses of virtue?

body.text: viśākhā -- tubhyaṃ śape satyam evaitad doṣam |
body.translated_text: <s>Viśākhā</s>: 'I swear to you — this is truly a fault.'

body.text: nāndīmukhī -- kas tāvad doṣaḥ ?
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>: 'What fault is that?'

body.text: viśākhā -- ucchiṣṭa-bhojanam |
body.translated_text: <s>Viśākhā</s>: 'The eating of leftovers (<s>ucchiṣṭa-bhojana</s>).'

body.text: nāndīmukhī -- kasya ?
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>: 'Whose?'

body.text: viśākhā -- dāsyāḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Viśākhā</s>: 'Of a maidservant.'

body.text: nāndīmukhī vihasya -- kā tāvat sā dāsī ?
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>, laughing: 'Who is that maidservant?'

body.text:
viśākhā -- śākhoṭa-vana-vāsinī kācin māyayā gopīva bhūtvā
kaṃsa-bhṛtya-govardhana-malla-gṛhiṇīm āsādya tām uvāca candrāvali! tvaṃ
bhuvaneśvaryāś caṇḍikāyāḥ priya-paricārikāsi | aham api tad-gaṇa-madhye
ekāsmi | tataḥ sneha-bhareṇa tva-sakhītvam icchāmi | tac chrutvā samīcīnam etad
ity āliṅgya sā candrāvalī yāṃ sakhyena parijagrāha saiva |
body.translated_text: <s>Viśākhā</s>: 'A certain one dwelling in the <s>Śākhoṭa</s> forest, having become a <s>gopī</s> by magic, approached the wife of the <s>Govardhana</s> wrestler — a servant of <s>Kaṃsa</s> — namely <s>Candrāvalī</s>, and said to her: "O <s>Candrāvalī</s>! You are the beloved attendant of <s>Caṇḍikā</s>, the mistress of the worlds. I too am one among her retinue. Therefore, out of deep affection, I desire your friendship." Hearing this, <s>Candrāvalī</s> said "This is fitting," embraced her, and accepted her as a friend — she is that very one.'

body.text: nāndīmukhī -- saiva kā ?
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>: 'That very one — who?'

body.text: viśākhā -- apūrvā padmā sā sarvatra prasiddhā bhavatyāpi jñāyate |
body.translated_text: <s>Viśākhā</s>: 'The unprecedented <s>Padmā</s> — she is famous everywhere and is known to you as well.'

body.text: nāndīmukhī -- kiṃ tad ucchiṣṭam ?
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>: 'What was that leftover?'

body.text: viśākhā -- tan mecakādhara-kupī-sthitaṃ parama-pāvanaṃ madhu ||
body.translated_text: <s>Viśākhā</s>: 'That supremely purifying nectar stored in the dark-lipped flask.'

body.text:
etan niśamya kiñcit smayamānāṃ rādhikām avalokayantas tat-sabhāsadaḥ sarve janā
jahasuḥ | tato nāndīmukhī -- viśākhe! kenāpy etad dṛṣṭam asti ?
viśākhā -- atha kim |
body.translated_text: Hearing this, all the people in the assembly laughed, looking at <s>Rādhikā</s> who was smiling slightly. Then <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>: '<s>Viśākhe</s>! Has anyone seen this?' <s>Viśākhā</s>: 'Of course!'

body.text: nāndīmukhī -- kena ?
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>: 'By whom?'

body.text:
viśākhā - vividha-giridhātu-paricchadān ānetuṃ priya-sakhyā gāndharvayā
preṣitābhyāṃ mallī-bhṛṅgībhyāṃ mānasa-gaṅgā-nikaṭoṣara-taṭe prakaṭam
evaitat parama-pāvanaṃ karma paraśva eva sākṣād avalokyāgatya sarvāsāṃ purato
vivicya kathitam |
body.translated_text: <s>Viśākhā</s>: 'By <s>Mallī</s> and <s>Bhṛṅgī</s>, sent by our dear friend <s>Gāndharvā</s> to bring various mountain minerals. On the bank of <s>Mānasa-gaṅgā</s>, on a saline shore, this supremely purifying deed was clearly witnessed just the day before yesterday. Having come and reported it, it was told in detail before all.'

body.text:
nāndīmukhī sacintam iva -- sakala-gokula-jīvanībhūtasyāsya kathaṃ
tad-doṣa-dhvaṃso bhavati ?
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>, as if with concern: 'How can the fault of this one, who has become the very life of all <s>Gokula</s>, be destroyed?'

body.text: viśākhā -- prāyaścittācaraṇenaiva |
body.translated_text: <s>Viśākhā</s>: 'Only through the performance of <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiation).'

body.text:
nāndīmukhī -- tato bhagavatītas tad-doṣa-vihita-niṣkṛtiṃ sampādya puruṣottamam
enaṃ śuddhaṃ vidhāya dīkṣayantu bhavaytaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>: 'Then let the venerable <s>Bhagavatī</s> accomplish the prescribed expiation for that fault and, having purified this <s>Puruṣottama</s> (Supreme Person), let you all initiate him.'

children.text: tac chrutvā campakalatā prāha -- mugdhe! ujjvala-maṇi-saṃhitāyām eva vivṛto'sti
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Campakalatā</s> said: 'O innocent one! It is already explained in the <s>Ujjvala-maṇi-saṃhitā</s> —'

children.text: tan-niṣkṛti-vidhir bhavatyāḥ prāyeṇa gocaro na bhavatīti tayaiva kathā-prasaṅge
children.translated_text: 'The procedure for that expiation is mostly beyond your scope' — this has been
stated by her in the course of that very conversation.

body.text: nāndīmukhī -- atra tat-saṃhitāṃ kas tāvaj jānāti ?
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>: 'Who here knows that <s>Saṃhitā</s>?'

body.text: campakalatā -- priya-sakhī gāndharvaiva |
body.translated_text: <s>Campakalatā</s>: 'Our dear friend <s>Gāndharvā</s> herself.'

body.text:
nāndīmukhī -- adhunā sā kilātra sabhā-madhye na vidyate | tat katham idaṃ
jhaṭiti nirvahatu ?
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>: 'Now she is reportedly not present here in the midst of the assembly. So how can this be accomplished immediately?'

body.text:
viśākhā -- tad-advitīyeyaṃ tato'dhīta-sandarbha-tat-saṃhitā-lalitā nirantaraṃ tad
abhyasyantī suṣṭhu taj jānantī tan nirūpayiṣyati |
body.translated_text: <s>Viśākhā</s>: '<s>Lalitā</s>, who is unrivaled by her, who has studied the compositions and that <s>Saṃhitā</s> from her, who constantly practices it and knows it well — she will determine it.'

body.text: nāndīmukhī sa-kāku -- sakhi lalite! vicārya yathocita-niṣkṛtir ādiśyatām |
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>, with a pleading tone: 'O friend <s>Lalitā</s>! Having deliberated, let the appropriate expiation be prescribed.'

body.text:
lalitā kiñcid vihasya -- priya-sakhi! kṛta-vaylīko jano yadi sabhā-madhye svayam
āgatya niḥśeṣaṃ svayam aghaṃ niṣkāpaṭyena nivedyānutapati, tadaivāsya
prāyaścittaṃ kāryate iti purāna-kṛdbhiḥ nirṇitam asti | tathā hi --
body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s>, laughing a little: 'Dear friend! If a person who has committed a transgression comes to the assembly of their own accord, confesses all their sins without deception, and repents — only then is the expiation to be performed. Thus it has been determined by the ancient authors. As follows —'

body.text:
saṃkathya svam aghaṃ goṣṭhyāṃ paścāt tapati yaḥ sphuṭam |
tasyaiva niṣkṛtiḥ sāṅgā munibhiḥ kāryate'khilā || iti |
body.translated_text: 'One who confesses their sin in the assembly and afterward clearly repents — only for such a one is the complete expiation with all its parts performed by the sages.'

body.text:
ity ākarṇya nāndīmukhyāṃ man-mukhaṃ sākūtam ālokayantyāṃ mayi ca
subala-madhumaṅgalābhyāṃ saha lalitā-savidham āsādya kiñcid vivakṣamāṇe sati,
viśākhā prāha -- he dhīra! kāmāturāṇāṃ na ghṛṇā na lajjeti svabhāvataḥ kāminā
tvayā yat kṛtaṃ tat kṛtam eva | adhunā tv etat tasyāḥ puro vivicya tat sarvaṃ
kathaya |
body.translated_text: Hearing this, while <s>Nāndīmukhī</s> was looking at my face meaningfully, and I, along with <s>Subala</s> and <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>, had approached <s>Lalitā</s>'s vicinity and was about to say something, <s>Viśākhā</s> said: 'O patient one! "For those afflicted by desire, there is no shame, no modesty" — what was done by you, a lover by nature, was done. But now, in her presence, narrate all of it in detail.'

body.text:
tato'haṃ smitam apavārya sānutāpam iva -- lalite! caturthe'hani
vighaṭita-gavānveṣaṇe gaurī-tīrtham evāptasya mama gaurī-mandirān niḥsṛtya
kācid gaurī sahacarī carcikā haṭhena mad-urasi savya-kucenāhatya
mādhavī-catuḥśālikāntarālaṃ mām ānīya kampamānasya mama mukhe
tāmbūla-carvitaṃ pradāya yat kiñcit kṛtavatī tan-mohito'haṃ kim api nāvediṣam |
paraśvo'pi suvarṇa-sūtreṇa vividha-kusumair grathita-mālām ādāya
rādhā-kuṇḍa-taṭa-nikuñja-nāgarīṃ gāndharvām anusmarato mama
mālya-haraṇa-kuṇḍa-taṭa-nikaṭa-mandārodyāna-parisare sā carcikā punar apy
āvirbhūya balenaiva mama vāma-gaṇḍaṃ paricumbya mukhe svādhara-pīyūṣam
arpitavatī tad etad agha-yugala-nirāśāya
tan-mukha-kamalocchiṣṭa-madhu-pāna-rūpaṃ prāyaścittam ādiśatu bhavatī |
body.translated_text: Then I, concealing a smile, as if with remorse: 'O <s>Lalitā</s>! On the fourth day, when the search for scattered cows reached <s>Gaurī-tīrtha</s> itself, a certain <s>Gaurī</s> (fair woman) came out of the <s>Gaurī</s> temple. Her companion <s>Carcikā</s> forcefully struck my chest with her left breast, brought me into the enclosure of the <s>Mādhavī</s> four-pavilioned bower, and placed chewed betel into my trembling mouth — she did something, but bewildered by her, I could not perceive what. The day before yesterday too, while taking a garland strung with various flowers on a golden thread and remembering <s>Gāndharvā</s>, the bower-dwelling lady at the bank of <s>Rādhā-kuṇḍa</s>, that <s>Carcikā</s> appeared again in the vicinity of the <s>Mandāra</s> garden near the garland-stealing bank of the <s>Kuṇḍa</s>, and forcefully kissing my left cheek, placed the nectar of her own lips in my mouth. So let this lady prescribe the expiation for this pair of sins — in the form of drinking the leftover lotus-mouth-nectar of that one — so that I may be freed from sin.'

body.text:
madhumaṅgalo vihasyāha -- vayasya! bhadrataram idaṃ niṣkṛtaṃ yat tad aghasyaiva
vṛddhiṃ vitanoti |
body.translated_text: <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>, laughing, said: 'Friend! This is a most auspicious expiation that only increases the growth of that very sin!'

body.text: tato'ham -- dhiṅ mūrkha! kim api na jānāsi | viṣasya viṣamauṣadham iti | yathā --
body.translated_text: Then I: 'Shame on you, fool! You know nothing! "Poison is the medicine for poison." As follows —'

body.text: vahni-santāpato naśyed vahni-santāpajo braṇaḥ | iti |
body.translated_text: 'A wound caused by fire-heat is destroyed by fire-heat.' Thus —

body.text: evaṃ --
body.translated_text: Likewise —

body.text: darayet kaṇṭakaṃ viddhaṃ kaṇṭakenaiva paṇḍitaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'The wise one removes a piercing thorn with a thorn itself.'

body.text: ity ādivad ucchiṣṭa-bhojana-doṣam ucchiṣṭa-bhojanam eva darayati |
body.translated_text: In the same way, the sin of eating leftovers is removed by eating leftovers itself.

body.text:
madhumaṅgalaḥ -- evaṃvidha-pāpa-vyādhi-cikitsāyāṃ tvam eva sad-vaidyo'si tat kiṃ
lalitām anuvartase ?
body.translated_text: <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>: 'In the treatment of such sins-as-diseases, you yourself are the good physician. So why do you follow <s>Lalitā</s>?'

body.text: tato'ham -- sakhe |
body.translated_text: Then I: 'Friend!'

children.text: jñāta-sāro'pi khalv ekaḥ sandigdhaḥ syāt sakarmaṇi |
children.translated_text: 'Even one who knows the essence may indeed become doubtful in his own treatment.'
'Therefore, even a physician's treatment is performed by others.'

body.text:
iti niśamya lalitā smayamānā prāha -- he deva! devyā saha devasyaiva saṅgaḥ
sampatsyate tat katham asmākaṃ mānuṣīṇāṃ sā gocarībhavatu ?
body.translated_text: Hearing this, <s>Lalitā</s>, smiling, said: 'O lord! The union of a god will only happen with a goddess — so how can she, being one of us mortals, come within his reach?'

body.text:
tato mayoktaṃ -- lalite! sā kutrāpi mānuṣi bhavatīnām adūra eva virājamānā
vartate |
body.translated_text: Then I said: 'O <s>Lalitā</s>! She is not a goddess anywhere — she is a mortal, shining not far from you all.'

body.text:
tataḥ sarvāsu sakautukaṃ sa-śaṅkaṃ karṇākarṇi keyam iti vicārayantīṣu rādhā
svagataṃ -- etasya dhūrtasya narma-nyāsa etad-goṣṭhyām eva bhaviṣyatīti lakṣyate |
body.translated_text: Then, as all of them were curiously and apprehensively whispering ear to ear, deliberating 'Who is she?' — <s>Rādhā</s> said to herself: 'It appears that this rogue's jest-deposit will be placed right in this very assembly.'

body.text:
viśākhā -- deva! kathyatām kutra sā yathaināṃ saṃstutya sabhā-madhye samānīya
bhavat-kāryam acirād asmābhir niṣpādyate ?
body.translated_text: <s>Viśākhā</s>: 'O lord! Tell us where she is, so that having praised her and brought her to the midst of the assembly, we may accomplish your purpose without delay.'

body.text:
tato'haṃ -- viśākhe! bhavad-goṣṭhyām eva taḍid iva virājayantī sā | kiṃ
dīrgha-netrayāpi tvayā na dṛśyate ?
body.translated_text: Then I: 'O <s>Viśākhe</s>! In your very assembly, she shines like lightning. Can even you, with your long eyes, not see her?'

body.text:
iti mad-gambhīrālāpam ākarṇya lalitāyām anyāsu sarvāsu ca ātmany ātmani tāṃ
narma-bhaṅgīm āśaṅkya parasparam ālokayantīṣu viśākhayoktaṃ -- lampaṭa! kiṃ
campakalatā ?
body.translated_text: Hearing my profound speech, as <s>Lalitā</s> and all the others each suspected the jest's nuance as referring to herself and looked at one another, <s>Viśākhā</s> said: 'O libertine! Is it <s>Campakalatā</s>?'

body.text: tato'haṃ -- na hi na hi |
body.translated_text: Then I: 'No, no!'

body.text: viśākhā -- kiṃ jyeṣṭhā |
body.translated_text: <s>Viśākhā</s>: 'Is it <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>?'

body.text: ahaṃ -- na hi na hi |
body.translated_text: I: 'No, no!'

body.text: subalaḥ -- raṅgadevī-sudevyayor ekatarā bhaviṣyati |
body.translated_text: <s>Subala</s>: 'It must be one of <s>Raṅgadevī</s> or <s>Sudevī</s>.'

body.text: ahaṃ -- anayor ekatarāpi na |
body.translated_text: I: 'Neither of those two either.'

body.text: viśākhā -- āṃ niṣkṛti-kāriṇī lalitaiva bhaviṣyati |
body.translated_text: <s>Viśākhā</s>: 'Ah! It must be <s>Lalitā</s> herself — the one prescribing the expiation.'

body.text: tato'haṃ -- viśākhe! iyam api na |
body.translated_text: Then I: 'O <s>Viśākhe</s>! Not this one either.'

body.text: viśākhā -- iyam api na eṣāpi na asāv api na | tat kiṃ ito'ntarhitā |
body.translated_text: <s>Viśākhā</s>: ''Not this one either, not that one either, nor that one!' Then has she disappeared from here?'

body.text: tato'haṃ -- dhūrte! tvam eva tāṃ jānāsi | smṛtvā paśya |
body.translated_text: Then I: 'O cunning one! You yourself know her. Remember and look!'

body.text:
lalitā -- hā hā sakhi viśākhe! tāṃ prakāśya vikalasyāsya kārya-siddhiṃ drutam
āpādaya |
body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s>: 'Ah, ah! O friend <s>Viśākhe</s>! Reveal her and quickly accomplish the purpose of this distressed one.'

body.text:
viśākhā smṛtim abhinīya -- lalite! yā mayā jñāyate sā devī-manuṣyayor ekatarāpi
na syāt |
body.translated_text: <s>Viśākhā</s>, feigning recollection: 'O <s>Lalitā</s>! The one I know — she would be neither a goddess nor a mortal.'

body.text: nāndīmukhī -- goṣṭha-madhye devīṃ mānuṣīṃ vā vinā kā punar itarā ?
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>: 'In the midst of the cow-settlement, besides a goddess or a mortal, who else could there be?'

body.text: viśākhā -- sā khalu śaṅkhinī |
body.translated_text: <s>Viśākhā</s>: 'She is indeed a <s>śaṅkhinī</s> (conch-woman).'

body.text: lalitā -- kā tāvat sā ?
body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s>: 'Who is she?'

body.text: viśākhā smitvāha -- sā durmukhī padmā yayāsya vyalīkaṃ kṛtam asti |
body.translated_text: <s>Viśākhā</s>, smiling, said: 'She is that wicked-faced <s>Padmā</s>, by whom his transgression was committed.'

body.text:
tuṅgavidyā -- sakhi viśākhe! sā śaṅkhinīti saṃkathya kathaṃ kaluṣam utpādayasi
? eṣā khalu bahutithaṃ kātyāyanī-devyā bahutara-sevā-prasādataḥ sākṣāt
kātyāyanī vṛtāsti |
body.translated_text: <s>Tuṅgavidyā</s>: 'O friend <s>Viśākhe</s>! How do you create confusion by calling her a <s>śaṅkhinī</s>? This one, through much devoted service to the goddess <s>Kātyāyanī</s>, has indeed been chosen as a veritable <s>Kātyāyanī</s> herself.'

body.text:
tac chrutvā madhumaṅgalādiṣu hasatsu mayoktaṃ -- viśākhe! tal-lajjayā yadi tvam
anyataḥ kṣipasi tan mayaiva kathyate |
body.translated_text: Hearing this, as <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> and the others laughed, I said: 'O <s>Viśākhe</s>! If you deflect to another out of embarrassment, then I myself shall tell.'

body.text: viśākhā -- kathaya kathaya |
body.translated_text: <s>Viśākhā</s>: 'Tell, tell!'

body.text: tato mayoktaṃ -- sā carcikā-devī tvam eva |
body.translated_text: Then I said: 'That goddess <s>Carcikā</s> is you yourself.'

body.text:
tataḥ sā sarvāḥ smayamānā vilokya sakampādharam āha -- aye cañcala vañcaka!
gopa-niṣṭhūra!
kaṃsāsura-sevaka-duṣṭakāliṅga-malla-gṛhiṇī-hāridra-rāga-carcita-sarvāṅga!
vidagdhya-sat-khaṇḍa! cāturya-sac-candra-virahita!
tad-dhṛta-sneha-lubdha-tat-keli-koli-kānana-cara |
ayukta-padmā-śaṅkhinī-parivṛḍha |
avaidagdhya-raṅga0milita-pañcabāṇa-rasa-vyāpāri-mahādhūrta-vaṇig-vara! etad
dhārṣṭya-jambula-guḍa-haṭṭaṃ tatraiva śākhoṭa-vane gatvā prasāraya | ito drutam
apasara ||
body.translated_text: Then she [<s>Rādhā</s>], surveying all of them with a smile, with trembling lower lip, said: 'Oh you fickle deceiver! Cowherd brute! One whose entire body is smeared with the turmeric-dye from the garment of the wicked wife of the <s>Kāliṅga</s> wrestler, a servant of the demon <s>Kaṃsa</s>! A fragment of six pieces of wit! Devoid of the genuine moon of cleverness! One who roams in the grove of colliding sports, greedy for the affection held by those [women]! Wrongly associated with <s>Padmā</s> and <s>Śaṅkhinī</s>! O foremost rogue-merchant dealing in the five-arrowed <s>rasa</s> (erotic sentiment), mingled with the theater of artlessness! Take this impudent <s>jambul</s>-candy shop to that <s>Śākhoṭa</s> forest and spread it there! Get away from here quickly!'

body.text:
iti śrutvā rādhā anuccaiḥ sa-ślāgham āha -- priya-sakhi viśākhe! vijayinī bhava
yan man-mānasa-gata-sambodhanoktyā māṃ sukhayanty asi ||
body.translated_text: Hearing this, <s>Rādhā</s> said softly with pride: 'Dear friend <s>Viśākhā</s>! May you be victorious — for by addressing me with the words conceived in your mind, you make me happy!'

body.text:
raṅgadevī -- sakhi viśākhe! tvaṃ kathaṃ kupasīty uktvā sakhi lalite! śākhoṭavanīṃ
mādhavī-catuḥśālikātvena mānasa-gaṅgā-taṭoṣara-pradeśaṃ
mālya-haraṇa-saras-tīra-mandārodyānatvena, padmā-śaṅkhinī-mukhocchiṣṭaṃ ca
priya-sakhī-viśākhādharāmṛtatvena nirūpya svamukhenaiva sānutāpaṃ sva-duritam
aśeṣam anena vidagdha-dhūrtena sva-kadarya-kārya-prakaṭana-janiṣyamāṇa-lajjayā
arthottha-vyaṅgenaiva tvayi niveditam | tad upadiśāsya prāyaścittam ||
body.translated_text: <s>Raṅgadevī</s>: 'Friend <s>Viśākhā</s>! How can you be angry?' Then she said: 'Friend <s>Lalitā</s>! He has depicted the <s>Śākhoṭa</s> forest as a <s>Mādhavī</s> four-pillared pavilion, the bank of <s>Mānasa-Gaṅgā</s> as a <s>Mandāra</s> garden by the garland-lake shore, and the lip-remnants of <s>Padmā</s> and <s>Śaṅkhinī</s> as the lip-nectar of dear friend <s>Viśākhā</s> — and thus with his own mouth, remorsefully, all his offenses have been reported to you by this clever rogue through indirect suggestion born of the embarrassment that would arise from openly revealing his miserly deeds. So prescribe his <s>prāyaścitta</s> (penance)!'

body.text:
iti śrutvā lalitā vihasya -- ārya madhumaṅgala! sakhe subala! sannidhāya śrūyatām
prāyaścittam ||
body.translated_text: Hearing this, <s>Lalitā</s>, laughing: 'Noble <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>! Friend <s>Subala</s>! Attend and hear the <s>prāyaścitta</s>!'

body.text: citrā -- sakhi lalite!
body.translated_text: <s>Citrā</s>: 'Friend <s>Lalitā</s>!

children.translated_text: When wealth is present, the <s>prāyaścitta</s> is fourfold;
moreover, for princes, the penalty is considered sixfold.'

body.text: iti smṛti-vākyaṃ smṛtvaiva prāyaścittam ādiśyatām ||
body.translated_text: 'Recalling this scriptural statement of the <s>Smṛti</s>, let the <s>prāyaścitta</s> be prescribed!'

body.text:
lalitā -- mugdhe! tato'pi rāja-putrāṇāṃ niṣkṛtiḥ syād dviṣaḍ-guṇā iti pāṭhaḥ
saṃhitā-saṃmato mayā jñāyate | ṣaḍguṇeti kathaṃ bhaṇyate ?
body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s>: 'O simple one! "Moreover, for princes, the penalty should be twice-sixfold" — this is the reading approved by the <s>Saṃhitā</s>, as I know it. How can you say "sixfold"?'

body.text:
citrā -- etac-chāstra-vijñayā tvayā yaj jñāyate tad eva satyam |
kintugovardhanoddharaṇa-dāvāgni-vimocana-śaṅkhacūḍādi-mardanādibhiḥ

children.text: katidhānena yuvarājena vayaṃ na rakṣitāḥ sma ? tasmād
children.translated_text: 'by how many deeds has this young prince not protected us? Therefore,'
'overlooking the now manifold defects committed by him, let [the penance] be determined at sixfold, out of compassion,'
'let it be so determined.'

body.translated_text: <s>Citrā</s>: 'Whatever you know through your expertise in this scripture — that alone is true. But by how many acts has this young prince protected us — through the lifting of <s>Govardhana</s>, the rescue from the forest fire, the crushing of <s>Śaṅkhacūḍa</s> and others —'

body.text: lalitā -- bhadraṃ tva-kathitam evedam anuṣṭhīyate | ādau pāpa-mocane snātvā

children.text: tathā mānasa-gaṅgāyāṃ tri-dināni snātaḥ sann eka-viṃśati-dināni
children.translated_text: 'and likewise, having bathed in <s>Mānasa-Gaṅgā</s> for three days, for twenty-one days,'
'let him first remove the mouth-impurity by drinking the <s>pañcāmṛta</s> (five nectars) from the lips of <s>Mallī</s> and <s>Bhṛṅgā</s>.'
'Afterwards, the twice-sixfold penalty is to be performed.'

body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s>: 'Good — what you say shall indeed be done. First, having bathed in the sin-releasing [pool],'

body.text:
iti śravaṇena kapaṭa-kopa-vikaṭo madhumaṅgalaḥ prāha -- lalitike!
sad-dhamra-setu-vrajendrayor etan-mātra-putrasya
tathāsmad-vidha-vayasya-vargāṇāṃ sakala-gokula-vāsinām apy eka-jīvātor asya
ceṭikā-pulindī-juṣṭa-bhakṣaṇena jāti-dhvaṃsaḥ kartum ārabdho bhavatībhis tad
aham atidrutaṃ gatvā vṛttam etat sa-viśeṣam āśrāvya etat-pitarāv atrānīya etat
saṅkaṭād amuṃ mocayan sauhṛdaṃ vitanomi | iti nigadya phutkṛtya drutaṃ
gacchantaṃ madhumaṅgalaṃ subalaḥ kare gṛhītvā balād iva nivartayāmāsa |
lalitā -- anārya baṭo! asmat-priya-sakhī-praṇayi-sakhyor anayor māhātmya-vijñāne
tvam anabhijño'si | tad bhavan nāndīmukhī-mukhād etac chrūyatām ||
body.translated_text: Hearing this, <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>, with feigned terrible anger, spoke: '<s>Lalitikā</s>! For the only son of both <s>Saddharmasetu</s> and <s>Vrajendra</s>, for companion-groups such as ourselves, and for all the residents of <s>Gokula</s> — all living as one life — the destruction of caste is being initiated by you ladies through eating food partaken by tribal <s>Pulindī</s> women! So I shall go very quickly, report this matter in full detail to his parents, bring them here, and release him from this predicament — thus I extend my friendship!' Saying this, he huffed and began leaving quickly. <s>Subala</s>, seizing <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> by the hand, forcibly turned him back. <s>Lalitā</s>: 'O ignoble <s>Brahmin</s> boy! Of the greatness of these two — our dear friend and her beloved — you are ignorant. So let this be heard from the mouth of <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>!'

body.text: nāndīmukhī -- bhrātar madhumaṅgala!
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>: 'Brother <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>!'

children.translated_text: 'On the beautiful <s>Govardhana</s> hill, <s>Rādhā-kuṇḍa</s> is dear to <s>Hari</s>;'

children.text: yathā rādhā priyā viṣṇos tasyāḥ kuṇḍaṃ priyaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: 'just as <s>Rādhā</s> is dear to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, so too is her pond dear to him.'

body.text: tathā --
body.translated_text: 'Likewise —'

children.text: vaikuṇṭhāj janito varā madhupurī tatrāpi rāsotsavāt
children.translated_text: 'Superior to <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> is the city of <s>Mathurā</s>; superior to it, due to the <s>Rāsa</s>-festival,'
'is <s>Vṛndāvana</s> forest; superior to it, due to its connection with the generous-handed Beloved, is <s>Govardhana</s>;'
'superior to all, due to being flooded with the nectar of the love of the Lord of <s>Gokula</s>, is <s>Rādhā-kuṇḍa</s> —'

children.text: kuryād asya virājato giri-taṭe sevāṃ vivekī na kaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'shining here on the hillside — what discerning person would not serve it?'

body.text:
ity ādy-anusāreṇa
śrī-bhagavatī-guru-śrī-devarṣi-prabhṛti-mahā-mahā-munīndra-gaṇair
varṇita-mahā-mahimnaḥ śrī-govardhanopari-virājamānasya rādhā-kuṇḍasya
dakṣiṇa-taṭe giri-darī-vāsinyāḥ pūrṇāḥ pulindya urugāyety ādi
śrī-śukadeva-varṇita-mahā-saubhāgya-bharayoḥ pulinda-rāja-sutayor anayor
adhara-galita-parama-pāvana-pañcāmṛtam etad-durita-nāśakaṃ kiṃ na syāt ? anyac
ca śrūyatām | vraja-navīna-yuva-dvandva-ratnaṃ prati viśākhādi-dvārā kvacit
svayaṃ vā lajjām abhinīya mṛdu

children.translated_text: 'the special benefit of the particular service they desire — <s>Raṅgamālā</s> and these others,'
'though supreme intimate friends, behave as if they were servants,'
'for the sake of obtaining the special service they desire.'

body.translated_text: 'Thus, in accordance with this and other [statements] by the assembly of supreme sages headed by the venerable <s>Bhagavatī</s>-<s>Guru</s>, the divine sage <s>Devarṣi</s> [<s>Nārada</s>], and others — on the southern bank of <s>Rādhā-kuṇḍa</s>, resplendent atop <s>Śrī Govardhana</s>, which has been praised for its supreme glory — of those two <s>Pulinda</s> prince and princess dwelling in a cave of the hill, endowed with great fortune described by <s>Śrī Śukadeva</s> [beginning with the verse] "<s>urugāya</s>" and so forth — would not the supremely purifying <s>pañcāmṛta</s> (five nectars) fallen from their lips destroy these sins? And furthermore, hear this: For the sake of obtaining the supreme bliss born of the collection of humorous arts, examined through playful speech — sometimes through <s>Viśākhā</s> and others as intermediaries, sometimes by herself presenting a gentle show of modesty toward the new young jewel-couple of <s>Vraja</s> — and likewise for obtaining'

body.text:
etad-avasaraa eva netra-kuṇanena goṣṭhī-madhyāt tulasīm āhūya
bandhurātibandhura-sugandhī-gandha-phalī-sadṛkṣa-dakṣiṇa-kara-kaniṣṭhāṅg
uli-śikharākṛṣṭa-sva-sīmanta-sindūra-rasa-prakaṭita-tat-saurabha-prasara-rūpa-s
urūpa-lipi-pracayenāti-suvāsitīkṛta-kanaka-ketakī-kusuma-dala-bhūta-varṇa-dūta
ekaḥ | śrī-gāndharvayā tat-kareṇa lalitādiṣu sañcāritaḥ | tatas taṃ lalitā śirasi
nidhāya sakhībhiḥ saha rahaḥ paripaṭhya nāndīmukhī-kare sa-smitam arpitavatī |
body.translated_text: At that very moment, summoning <s>Tulasī</s> from the midst of the gathering by a wink of the eye, a letter-messenger was dispatched — in the form of a golden <s>Ketakī</s> flower petal made supremely fragrant by an assemblage of beautiful and well-formed letters manifesting the spreading fragrance of <s>sindūra</s> (vermilion) paste drawn from her own hair-part by the tip of the little finger of the right hand, resembling a beautiful, exquisitely fragrant fruit — one [letter] was circulated by <s>Śrī Gāndharvā</s> [<s>Rādhā</s>] through her hand among <s>Lalitā</s> and the others. Then <s>Lalitā</s>, having placed it upon her head, having read it privately with the <s>sakhīs</s>, entrusted it with a smile into <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>'s hand.

body.text: nāndīmukhī smitvānandam abhinīya vakṣasi nidhāya vācayati --
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>, smiling, expressing joy, placing it upon her chest, reads aloud:

body.text:
svasti
