śrīnāndīmukhī-śrī-lalitā-śrī-viśākhā-prabhṛti-prāṇa-preṣṭha-sakhī-vargeṣu
pariṣvaṅga-parārdha-raṅga-pūrvikā kasyāścid vijñaptir iyam --
body.translated_text: '<s>Svasti</s> (auspicious greetings)! To the dearest-of-life groups of friends headed by <s>Śrī Nāndīmukhī</s>, <s>Śrī Lalitā</s>, and <s>Śrī Viśākhā</s> — preceded by the supreme festivity of embrace — this is a certain one's petition:'

body.text:
śrīdāma-subala-bhadrasenādi-pramukha-priya-vayasya-gaṇaiḥ saha
govardhana-parisare sambhṛta-gocāraṇa-paramāmodasya
vraja-rāja-nija-jīvita-parārdha-śatādhika-parama-priyatama-tanayasya
vrajendra-mahiṣī-sva-prāṇa-parārdha-paripakva-hiraṇmayeṣṭakāghaṭā-ghaṭita-
mahā-mandirāntarāla-vinirmita-prāṇa-parārdha-vividha-ratna-khacita-mahā-par
yaṅka-kṛṄpta-vātsalya-nānā-vidha-kusuma-suvāsita-sukumāra-sutūlikopari-sama
dhigata-śayana-keli-paramānandasya
mat-prāṇa-parārdhārbuda-parārdha-śata-nirmañchyamāna-vāma-caraṇa-kaniṣṭ
hāṅguli-nakhāñcala-pratīkasya
nava-mṛgamada-parimalita-navanīta-nīlotpala-dala-kula-racita-sundara-sukumāra
-vigrahasya dhīra-lalitasyāsya etāvat kaṭhora-prāyaścitta-śravaṇena mama hṛdayaṃ
navanītam iva vidravavad āste |
body.translated_text: 'Of that most-beloved son of the <s>Vraja</s>-king, whose supreme delight is the pasturing of cows in the environs of <s>Govardhana</s> together with <s>Śrīdāma</s>, <s>Subala</s>, <s>Bhadrasena</s>, and other groups of dear companions; who is dearer to his father than a hundred-thousand-fold of his own life's half; whose supreme bliss lies in the sleeping-play upon the supremely soft and fragrant feather-bed, adorned with various flowers of maternal affection, arranged upon the great couch inlaid with the myriad precious gems — life's half — fashioned within the inner chambers of the great mansion constructed with baked golden bricks ripened as the half of the life-force of the queen of <s>Vrajendra</s>; who appears as the likeness of the toe-nail tip of the little finger of the left foot that churns a hundred-thousand-crore halves of my life-force; whose beautiful, delicate body is fashioned from clusters of fresh blue-lotus petals anointed with fresh <s>mṛgamada</s> (musk) and fragrant butter; who is the <s>dhīra-lalita</s> (gentle and playful) hero — by the hearing of such severe <s>prāyaścitta</s> for him, my heart melts as if it were butter.'

body.text: tataḥ --
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore —'

children.translated_text: 'For those who show signs of remorse, who are tender-bodied,'
'and who are affectionate — the penalty is properly determined only according to the <s>Tantra</s> (esoteric scripture).'

children.text: ity ujjvala-saṃhitā-vacanam ananusmṛtyaiva lalitayā yat pañcāmṛta-pāna-rūpaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Without even recalling this statement of the <s>Ujjvala-saṃhitā</s>, the fact that <s>Lalitā</s> has prescribed the <s>pañcāmṛta</s>-drinking as <s>prāyaścitta</s> merely for mouth-cleansing,'

children.text: prāyaścittaṃ kevala-mukha-śodhanāya ca tantreṇa vidhāyāsmin nirdoṣe vihite
children.translated_text: 'and has arranged it according to the <s>Tantra</s> for this blameless one —'

children.text: mama mahaty eva nirvṛtir jāyate ity alam ativistareṇa ||
children.translated_text: 'in this I find great satisfaction indeed. Enough of excessive elaboration.'

body.text:
ihaiva prāṇa-pratima-praṇayi-sakhyau mallī-bhṛṅgyay prati
sa-praṇaya-pariṣvaṅga-sañcāraḥ kāryaś ca |
body.translated_text: 'Moreover, let an affectionate embrace be conveyed here to the life-resembling intimate friends <s>Mallī</s> and <s>Bhṛṅgī</s>.'

body.text:
rāja-putro'yaṃ parama-pavitro mahā-vilāsī ca | tan nija-caraṇa-kmala-ghātena
kaṅkelli-latikāṃ puspitīkṛtya tan-makaranda-prasyanda-gaṇḍūṣaiś caturviṃśatyā

children.translated_text: 'let him specially wash his own mouth, and preparing the sweet <s>pañcāmṛta</s> scented with the camphor of his smile,'

children.text: premṇā śanaiḥ śanais tathā pāyayitavyaṃ yathāsya sukumārasya duritaṃ drutam
children.translated_text: 'let it be lovingly and gently administered to drink, in such a way that the sin of this tender one quickly departs'
'and supreme happiness is also produced.'

body.translated_text: 'This prince is supremely pure and a great connoisseur. Therefore, by the touch of his own lotus-foot, let him make the <s>Kaṅkeli</s> (Aśoka) vine bloom, and with twenty-four mouthfuls of its exuding nectar,'

body.text:
iti niśamya sāntarānandaṃ rādhā-nikuñjam avalokayati mayi smitvā lalitā prāha
-- yadyapi kṛtānutāpa-lakṣāṇām ity ādi sāmānya-vacanāntaraṃ
body.translated_text: Hearing this, with inner joy, she [<s>Rādhā</s>] gazes at the <s>Rādhā</s>-bower; with a smile at me, <s>Lalitā</s> spoke: 'Although the general statement beginning with "For those who show signs of remorse" [applies],'

children.translated_text: '[yet the rule states:] "When wealth is present, the <s>prāyaścitta</s> is fourfold."'
'And even there, for princes, the expiation should be twelve-fold.'

body.text: iti viśeṣa-vacanena sāmānya-viśeṣayor viśeṣa-vidhir balavān iti nyāyenāsya

children.text: dviṣaḍ-guṇam eva prāyaścittaṃ yuktam eva pṛthak pṛthak nirūpitam asti tathāpy
children.translated_text: twelve-fold expiation alone has been separately determined as fitting. Nevertheless,

children.text: ājñā gurūṇāṃ hy avicāraṇīyeti tad-ājñāṃ śirasi nidhāya tantreṇaiva kārayitavyam
children.translated_text: 'the command of the <s>guru</s> is not to be questioned' — placing that command upon one's head, it must be carried out according to the prescribed method

body.translated_text: By virtue of the principle that, between a general rule and a specific rule, the specific rule is the stronger — this

body.text:
tataḥ śiṣye vidyā garīyasīti mayokte lalitā sākūtam āha -- nāndīmukhi!
saundarya-rasa-bhareṇāpyāyita-nikhila-gokula-jananayanāravindāṃ
para-rāsa-sthalī-vihāriṇīṃ parama-rasa-taraṅgiṇīṃ raṅgiṇi-sahacarīṃ hariṇīm etāṃ
parihāya bāḍham ayasa-vidagdha-kṛṣṇasāra-yuvā sakhī-sthaly-upaśalye
tad-vāstavya-śaivyā-sahacarī-mṛgatṛṣṇikāṃ muhur muhur dhāvati | tathā
gāndharvā-sarovara-nikuñjāṅgane saurabha-prasara-parivāsita-sakala-diśāṃ
campakalatā-sakhīṃ kāñcana-yūthikām apahāya govardhana-malla-gṛhakoṇa-sthāṃ
nirgandha-puṣpavatīṃ kuṣmāṇḍa-latāṃ tan nikaṭa-stha-nīrasoṣara-sthala-padmāṃ
ca ta-sahacarīṃ cañcalo'yam avidagdha-bhramaraḥ punaḥ punar uḍḍīyoḍḍiyānusarati
tad etad ālambanāvadagdhya-rūpa-vairūpyeṇa vṛndāvana-maheśvarī-sahacarī
madhurā ratir aprasannā satī etac chyāmala-rasaṃ na puṣṇāti | tasmāt tathainam
anabhijñaṃ yukta-mādhurībhiḥ prabodhaya | yathā tām avidagdhāṃ
rasa-gandha-śūnyāṃ sarvadaiva vihāyaināṃ vṛndāvana-mahā-devīṃ
sarvato-bhāvenānusarati | tarhi tat-priya-sakhī madhurā ratiḥ svayam eva
paramojjvalā bhavantī etad abhīṣṭa-kāmān sampādayiṣyaty eva |
body.translated_text: Then, when I said 'the knowledge of the disciple is most weighty,' <s>Lalitā</s> said pointedly: '<s>Nāndīmukhī</s>! Abandoning this doe (<s>hariṇī</s>), the companion of the playful one (<s>raṅgiṇī</s>), who is the supreme stream of <s>rasa</s>, who sports at the supreme <s>rāsa</s>-ground, and whose beauty-filled <s>rasa</s> nourishes the lotus-eyes of all the people of <s>Gokula</s> — this inexperienced young <s>kṛṣṇasāra</s> (black-spotted) deer repeatedly runs after the mirage that is the companion of <s>Śaivyā</s> who dwells in the rival's ground near the bed of friends. Likewise, in the courtyard of the bower by the lake of <s>Gāndharvā</s>, abandoning <s>Kāñcana-yūthikā</s> (the golden jasmine), the friend of <s>Campakalatā</s>, whose fragrance perfumes all directions — this fickle, unskilled bee repeatedly flies after the scentless <s>kuṣmāṇḍa</s>-creeper standing in the corner of the <s>Govardhana</s>-wrestler's house and the waterless, saline ground-lotus that is her companion. Because of this unsightliness of improper attachment, <s>Madhurā Rati</s>, the companion of the queen of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, being displeased, does not nourish this dark <s>rasa</s>. Therefore, with fitting sweetness, enlighten this ignorant one, so that, always abandoning that unskilled one devoid of even the scent of <s>rasa</s>, he follows this great goddess of <s>Vṛndāvana</s> with his whole being. Then her dear friend <s>Madhurā Rati</s>, herself becoming supremely radiant, will surely fulfill his heart's desires.'

body.text:
ity akhila-vilāsa-rasa-mādhurīm āpīya satyabhāmā vyājahāra -- prāṇanātha! etad
apūrva-rasa-sāgare nimajjantyā mama manāg api tṛpteḥ paryāptir na vidyate |
body.translated_text: Having drunk in the sweetness of all erotic <s>rasa</s>, <s>Satyabhāmā</s> exclaimed: 'Lord of my life! Plunging into this unprecedented ocean of <s>rasa</s>, my thirst finds not the slightest satisfaction.'

body.text:
kṛṣṇaḥ -- priye! etad gokula-vilāsānanda-niṣkuṭe viharamāṇasya mama tvat-praśna
eva mat-priya-vayasya-samaya-rāja-vasantollāsa iti tām āliliṅgati |
body.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>: 'Beloved! For me who sports in this garden of the bliss of <s>Gokula</s>'s amorous play, your very question is like the delight of the king of seasons — the spring festival of my dear friend's assembly.' — and he embraced her.

body.text: satyabhāmā sānandaṃ -- tatas tataḥ ?
body.translated_text: <s>Satyabhāmā</s>, joyfully: 'Then what? Then what?'

body.text:
kṛṣṇaḥ -- tataḥ subalaḥ sasmitam āha -- priyavayasya! priya-sakhīyam indulekhā
durdurūḍhāt sva-bhartur bhāsvarākhyād udvignā mām iṅgitena prerayati | tad
asyāḥ mauktik-mūlyaṃ nirṇīya tad dattvā jhaṭiti gṛha-kṛtyāya gantum
ājñāpyatām |
body.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>: 'Then <s>Subala</s> said with a smile: "Dear friend! This <s>Indulekhā</s>, your dear friend's companion, is distressed because of her hard-to-mount husband named <s>Bhāsvara</s>, and signals me to send her away. So determine the pearl-price for her, give it, and quickly command her to go home for household duties."'

body.text:
tato'haṃ -- sakhe satyaṃ satyaṃ mayy atīvānurakteyaṃ mām api tyaktuṃ na śaknoti |
tato'pi suṣṭhu bibhetīty aham api jānāmi | tad etan mauktika-mūlyaṃ śṛṇu --
yathārtha-nāmnīyaṃ mad-viraham asahamānā kāya-dvayaṃ kṛtvā
śyāmalatara-mad-vakṣo-nabhasi śāṇita-nakhāgreṇa racitām ekāṃ sva-mūrtiṃ
saṃrakṣatu | aham apy asahyaitad-virahas tāvad asyāḥ vakṣoja-parvatopari
sva-vidyā-balenārdha-candra-yugalībhavann udayaṃ karomi | tadaiṣā
labdha-mahā-ratnam iva sarvato māṃ celāñcalenāvṛṇotu | rahasi ca kṣaṇe kṣaṇe
sa-romāñcam avalokayantī paramānandam āsādayatu | athavā
mṛga-lāñchana-rahitāyā etasyā hṛn-madhye mañjula-kṛṣṇa-sāro'haṃ bhavāmīti |
body.translated_text: 'Then I [said]: "Friend, truly, truly! She is so deeply attached to me that she cannot even bear to leave me. And yet she is truly afraid of him — I know this too. So hear this pearl-price: Since she, whose name is apt, cannot bear separation from me, let her make two bodies and preserve one image of herself, fashioned with sharpened nail-tips upon the darkest sky of my chest. And I too, unable to bear separation from her, shall rise as a pair of half-moons upon the mountain-peaks of her breasts by the power of my art. Then, as if she has obtained a great gem, let her cover me on all sides with the edge of her garment. And in private, gazing at me moment by moment with goosebumps, let her attain supreme bliss. Or rather, I shall become the beautiful black deer (<s>kṛṣṇasāra</s>) in the heart of this one who is without the mark of the deer (the moon)."'

body.text:
tataḥ sakampādharaṃ kuṭilaṃ mām avalokayantīm indulekhām ālokya smayamānā
tuṅgavidyā prāha -- nāgara! raṅgadevīyaṃ yathārtha-nāmnī tad asyā
mauktika-paṇaḥ praṇiyatām |
body.translated_text: Then, seeing <s>Indulekhā</s> looking at me with trembling lips and a sidelong glance, <s>Tuṅgavidyā</s> said with a smile: 'O gallant one! This <s>Raṅgadevī</s> has an apt name too — so set a pearl-price for her!'

body.text:
tato'ham -- sakhi raṅgadevi! rāsa-madhye tava lāsya-vilāsollāsaḥ santatam
ālokito'sti | tad adhunā nikuñja-mandirāṅgane rahasi tad-viśeṣam anubhavitum
abhilaṣāmi | tad ehi sva-vakṣoja-kanaka-kumbhau mad-urasi tathā nartaya

children.translated_text: that I am delighted,
and by the gift of the great favor of the nectar of my own lower lip, which is the very treasure of the entire community of cowherd women,
I shall delight you."'

body.translated_text: 'Then I [said]: "Friend <s>Raṅgadevī</s>! I have constantly beheld the delight of your graceful dancing at the <s>rāsa</s>. Now I desire to experience that special dance in private, in the courtyard of a bower-pavilion. So come — dance those golden pots of your breasts upon my chest in such a way

body.text:
tac chrutvā apaihi bhaṇḍa-śekhara! apaihīty uktvā kuṭilaṃ mām avalokya
viśākhā-pṛṣṭhāntaritāyāṃ raṅgadevyāṃ sudevī sa-smitam āha -- rasika-śekhara!
ballavī-kula-bhukta-muka-sujuṣṭa-mahā-prasādāsvādaneneyaṃ tvaritam eva
siddhim āsādayantī sphuṭam asmān api siddhārthāḥ kṛtavaty eva |
body.translated_text: Hearing that, she said 'Away with you, O crown of buffoons! Away!' and, looking at me with a sidelong glance, as <s>Raṅgadevī</s> hid behind <s>Viśākhā</s>, <s>Sudevī</s> said with a smile: 'O crown of connoisseurs! This one, by tasting the great favor of the lip well-enjoyed by the foremost of the cowherd clan, will quickly attain perfection — and clearly she has already made us too accomplished!'

body.text:
subalaḥ -- vayasya! sudevī sva-mauktika-mūlyaṃ śrotu-kāmā
śrīmad-bhavan-mukham īkṣamāṇeyam utkaṇṭhate |
body.translated_text: <s>Subala</s>: 'Friend! <s>Sudevī</s>, eager to hear her own pearl-price, gazes at your auspicious face in anticipation.'

body.text:
tato'ham -- sakhe subala! sudevīyam akṣa-keli-dakṣeti prasiddhā tac chapatham eva
dadad asmi kenāpi kasyāpi pakṣo na grāhyaḥ | āvām eva sva-buddhi-balena
kheliṣyāvaḥ | tatra yady aham anayā suṣṭhu jīyeyaṃ, tarhi vāmena vakṣojena
mad-vakṣṣasi mām āpīḍya mama sarvasva-bhūtam adharaṃ dviḥ pibatu | yadi vā
mayedaṃ jīyate, tadā sva-dakṣiṇa-kaṭhina-vakṣojaṃ mad-dakṣiṇa-kareṇa nikāmaṃ
pīḍayitvā dviḥ svādharāmṛtam āpāyayatv iti |
body.translated_text: 'Then I [said]: "Friend <s>Subala</s>! This <s>Sudevī</s> is renowned as skilled in dice-games. So I give this oath: neither of us shall take anyone's side. We two alone shall play by the strength of our own wits. If I am thoroughly defeated by her, then let her press me to her chest with her left breast and drink my lip — the essence of my all — twice. And if she is defeated by me, then let her offer her firm right breast to be pressed to my heart's content by my right hand, and let her give me the nectar of her lip to drink twice."'

body.text:
tataḥ sā bhrū-bhaṅgena mām avalokayantī sāsūyaṃ viśākhām āha -- ayi viśākhe!
sarva-kālam eva narma-svarṇa-vikrayy asau mahājanaḥ | sāmpratam eva
muktā-maṇi-vyāpāram ārabhya tato vṛddhim alabhamānaḥ punaḥ sva-vṛttim
evārabdhavān asti | tataḥ parārdha-dvi-guṇa-pañcabāṇa-lalitāṃ
kāñcana-mudrā-tatim itaḥ prakāma-mūlyena pragṛhya tayaiva muktāphalāny asmād
ānayantu bhavatyaḥ | mayā tu gṛhāya gamyate |
body.translated_text: Then she, looking at me with a frown, said to <s>Viśākhā</s> with jealousy: 'O <s>Viśākhā</s>! This great merchant is always trading in the gold of jests. Having just now taken up the pearl-and-gem trade and finding no profit in it, he has again commenced his former profession. So let your ladyships take from here, at a full price, the row of golden coins as lovely as the twice-doubled five-arrowed one (<s>Kāma</s>), and with those very coins have the pearls brought from him. As for me, I am going home.'

body.text:
iti calitum udyatāñcale gṛhītvānaṅga-mañjaryā nivartitā sa-krodham iva sākūtaṃ
punar āha -- keli-lampaṭa! nikāmam akṣa-keli-nipuṇeyam anaṅga-mañjarī tvayā
saha dīvyantī te garva-parvataṃ kharvayiṣyati |
body.translated_text: As she lifted the border of her garment to depart, she was stopped by <s>Anaṅgamañjarī</s> who seized it, and she said again, as if with anger yet pointedly: 'O dice-addict! This <s>Anaṅgamañjarī</s>, exceedingly skilled in dice-games, playing against you, will level your mountain of pride!'

body.text:
tatas tad-vacana-mādhuryam avadhārya mayoktaṃ -- asyās tv abalāyās tat-keliṣu kā
śaktiḥ ? kintumad-vakṣo-harid-grāva-haritālīya-rekhikāyā rādhikāyāḥ
prāṇa-sahodareyaṃ mayy atīva snihyati | mama ca mānasa-madhukaraḥ param
asyām anavaratam anuvrajyati | ataḥ samucita-paṇam antarāpi sutārāṇi suvṛttāni
bahūni mauktikāny apy asyai vitariṣyāmi | paraṃ ca nirjana-nikuñja-vedikāyāṃ
smara-puñjarākṣarāṇy asyāḥ pañcāśad aṅga-pratyaṅgeṣu sva-hastena vinyasya
svāṅgaṃ svāṅgenālinṅgya mantreṇaināṃ vyāpayya tathā siddha-mantram ekam
upadiśāmi yathā tad-grahaṇa-mātrād anaṅgaṃ sāṅgaṃ viracayya santuṣṭena tena
prasādīkṛta-sva-sarvasva-svarūpa-vilāsa-ratnāni mantra-gurau mayi dakṣiṇātvena
sa-vinayam upaḍhaukayati | tataḥ suprasannena mayā tādṛg-āśīḥ-śatam ādhāsyate
yena viṣama-śara-vilāsācāryeti padavīm āsādya dvi-guṇaṃ mām eva bhaktyā
paricarati |
body.translated_text: Then, savoring the sweetness of her words, I said: 'What power does this delicate girl have in such games? However, since she is the very soul-sister of <s>Rādhikā</s> — the line of golden <s>haritālī</s> upon the emerald stone of my chest — she is deeply affectionate toward me. And my mind-bee ceaselessly follows after her. Therefore, besides a fitting wager, I shall also bestow upon her many pearls — lofty, well-rounded, and excellent. Moreover, upon the platform of a secluded bower, I shall inscribe the syllables of the love-cage upon her fifty limbs and sub-limbs with my own hand, embrace each of my limbs with hers, pervade her with the <s>mantra</s>, and teach her one perfected <s>mantra</s> such that, merely upon receiving it, having fully fashioned <s>Anaṅga</s> (the god of love) with all his limbs, he, being gratified, will respectfully offer in homage to me as <s>mantra-guru</s> the jewels of amorous play that are his very essence as a <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (fee). Then, being well pleased, I shall bestow a hundred such blessings upon her that, having attained the title of "Teacher of the Arts of the Crooked-arrowed One," she will serve me with doubled devotion.'

body.text: iti mad-bhāṣita-kusuma-stavakaṃ śravaṇāvataṃsīkṛtya sakampādharaṃ mām īṣad

children.text: avalokayantī smita-subhaga-vadanābhir ābhiḥ snehenotphullatayā tad-agrajayā ca
children.translated_text: gazed upon by these women with smiling, lovely faces and with affection in full bloom, and by her elder sister also

children.text: sa-smitaṃ sa-snehaṃ ca nirīkṣyamāṇā tulasī-raṅgaṇamālikayor upapṛṣṭham
children.translated_text: with a smile and with tenderness, she hid behind
<s>Tulasī</s> and <s>Raṅgamālikā</s>.

body.translated_text: Having made this bouquet of my words into ear-ornaments, looking at me slightly with trembling lips,

body.text: satyabhāmā smitvā -- prāṇanātha! tatas tataḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Satyabhāmā</s>, smiling: 'Lord of my life! Then what? Then what?'

body.text:
kṛṣṇaḥ -- tadānīm eva mallī-bhṛṅgībhyām ānīya dattaṃ lekha-dvayam | sarvābhiḥ
samam eva vācayitvā paramotphullā lalitā tayor ekaṃ lekhaṃ subala-haste
samarpitavatī |
body.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>: 'Just then, two letters were brought and delivered by <s>Mallī</s> and <s>Bhṛṅgī</s>. When all had read them together, <s>Lalitā</s>, supremely delighted, placed one of those two letters in <s>Subala</s>'s hand.'

body.text: tato'ham -- lalite! kasyāyaṃ lekhaḥ ?
body.translated_text: 'Then I [said]: "<s>Lalitā</s>! Whose letter is this?"'

body.text: lalitā smitvā -- lekha eva kathayiṣyati |
body.translated_text: '<s>Lalitā</s>, smiling: "The letter itself will tell you."'

body.text:
tataḥ subale lekham udghāṭya laghu laghu vācayati sati nāndīmukhī -- subala!
sphuṭam eva vācaya |
body.translated_text: 'Then, as <s>Subala</s> opened the letter and began reading softly, <s>Nāndīmukhī</s> [said]: "<s>Subala</s>! Read it out clearly!"'

body.text: subalaḥ smitvā -- sakhe! apūrva-patrīyam avadhāryatām |
body.translated_text: '<s>Subala</s>, smiling: "Friend! Pay attention — this is an extraordinary letter."'

body.text: ahaṃ -- sakhe! vācaya mamāpi mahatī śuśrūṣā vartate |
body.translated_text: I: 'Friend! Read it — I too have a great desire to listen.'

body.text:
subalaḥ -- svasti
samasta-saṃmukha-sarvopamā-yogya-bandha-prbandha-sad-guṇa-prkara-parivṛteṣu
śrī-subalābhidhāna-priya-narma-sakha-mahānubhāveṣu yāvaṭābhidha-grāmato
rādhāyāhḥ
praṇaya-bhara-pīyūṣa-paripūritākṣara-prakara-sumiṣṭa-piṣṭaka-pariveṣāṇa-hir
aṇmaya-bhājana-rūpŪ'yaṃ svastimukham --
body.translated_text: <s>Subala</s>: 'Blessings! To the greatly fortunate one named <s>Śrī Subala</s>, the dear jesting-friend, enveloped by clusters of excellent qualities worthy of every comparison with all those present — from <s>Rādhā</s>, from the village named <s>Yāvaṭa</s> — this auspicious-faced letter, in the form of a golden vessel serving sweetly blended confections of words filled with the nectar of love's fullness —'

body.text:
bhavat-prāṇa-bandhu-pāda-padmānāṃ bhavādṛśāṃ ca maṅgala-kulam
anavarata-virājamānam api vraja-maṇḍale śaśvan nitarāṃ virājatām || kāṛyam idam
anyad api avadhehi priya-jana-sakāśāt kara-grahaṇam anucitam iti bahutaram api
kara-dravyam apahāyaiva etāvad-dinaṃ kim api noktam āsīt | samprati
mauktika-vyayena kṣubhyad-guru-jana-dīyamāna-mahānuyoga-nicayena kṣaṇam
api nirvṛti-lavam alabhamānayā yat kiñcin mayā vijñāpyamānam asti | tad-aguṇam
avigaṇayya mad-vṛndāvana-janapade yamunopakaṇṭha-kedārikāyāṃ
bhavat-prāṇa-bandhunā samprati kṣetrājīvatām āśrayatā kṛta-mauktika-kṛṣer
lalitayā saha lekha-pratilekham ācārya samucita-kara-dravym iha tvaritam eva
prahitya dīyatāṃ, yathā dravyeṇaiva mathurāto mauktikāny ānāyya gurubhyaḥ
pradāya kadana-sāgarād asmād uttarāmaḥ | athavā
bahu-mūlya-mauktikotpatti-bhūmeḥ karasyāpy atibāhulyād etad-dravya-pradāne
yadi bhavādṛśām aśaktiḥ syāt tarhi pañcabhir militvā samucita-mūlyaṃ nirṇīya
etad-dravya-parivartanena mauktikani lalitā-haste deyānīti kiṃ bahunā
paramābhijña-vareṣv iti |
body.translated_text: 'May the auspicious family of the lotus feet of your life-friend, and of those such as yourself, though ever-shining, shine even more perpetually throughout the district of <s>Vraja</s>. The matter is this further: understand that it is improper to accept payment from dear ones by hand. Though much payment-in-goods was due, nothing at all was said until now. But at present, being unable to obtain even a moment's respite from the heaps of severe questioning given by the elders who are distressed by the pearl expenditure, there is something I must humbly submit. Overlooking its faults, and considering that your life-friend — who now resides as a farmer in our <s>Vṛndāvana</s> district, having taken up pearl-farming on a garden bed near the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s> — should exchange letters with <s>Lalitā</s>, determine the appropriate payment-in-goods, and quickly send it here, so that with those goods, pearls may be brought from <s>Mathurā</s>, given to the elders, and we may be rescued from this ocean of torment. Or alternatively, since the pearl-producing land is also abundant in payment goods, if those such as yourself are unable to provide such goods, then let the five of them meet together, determine a suitable price, and give the pearls into <s>Lalitā</s>'s hand in exchange for those goods. In short — to those supremely knowledgeable and excellent ones.'

body.text:
etan niśamya paramānanda-pūrṇenāpi mayā sākūtam uktaṃ -- ayi malli! ayi
bhṛṅgi! bhavad-īśvarī sukhaṃ vartate ?
body.translated_text: Hearing this, though filled with supreme bliss, I said with deliberate intent: 'O <s>Mallī</s>! O <s>Bhṛṅgī</s>! Is your mistress well?'

body.text: mallī-bhṛṅgau -- śrīman-nātha-caraṇa-śubhānudhyānena |
body.translated_text: <s>Mallī</s> and <s>Bhṛṅgī</s>: 'Through the auspicious meditation upon the blessed lord's feet.'

body.text: tatas tan-nikuñja-diśaṃ tiryag-avalokayann ahaṃ -- kutra vartate sā ?
body.translated_text: Then, casting a sidelong glance toward the direction of her bower, I said: 'Where is she?'

body.text:
te yāvaṭābhidha-grāme |
ahaṃ -- kiṃ kurvatī tiṣṭhati ?
body.translated_text: They: 'In the village named <s>Yāvaṭa</s>.' I: 'What is she doing?'

body.text:
te lalitā-devī-prabhṛtīnāṃ varma-diśam avalokayantī
vṛndāvana-rājya-sārvabhauma-kāmam utkaṇṭhiteva virājamānā vartate |
body.translated_text: They: 'Looking toward the direction of <s>Lalitā-devī</s> and the others, she is shining as if longing for the sovereignty of the kingdom of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>.'

body.text:
tato'haṃ -- sakhe subala! ,amue liṭiolayā lalitayaiva kasyacid dvārā lekhayitvā
lekho'yaṃ vitīrṇo'sti |
body.translated_text: Then I: 'Friend <s>Subala</s>! This letter was surely composed by the cunning <s>Lalitā</s> through someone as intermediary.'

body.text: subalaḥ -- nahi nahi | rādhāyā eva sva-hasta-likhita-varṇānāṃ vinyāso'yam |
body.translated_text: <s>Subala</s>: 'No, no! This is the arrangement of letters written by <s>Rādhā</s>'s own hand.'

body.text:
tato'ham -- sakhe! tat tāvad idaṃ darśayati tad-dhastād ākṛṣya lekham ālokya
sa-camatkāram ātmagataṃ -- aho akṣarāṇāṃ paṅkti-vistṛtir iyaṃ man-netrayoḥ
pīyūṣa-vartikeyva pratibhātīty ānanda-janita-pulakān vismaya-sañcāri-bhāvenaiva
kṛtān iti bhaṅgyā vikhyāpya prakāśaṃ vihasya āścaryam āścaryam
ākāśa-kusumam iva dhūrtābhir etābhiḥ kim apy anyad akasmād eva
samutthāpitam |
body.translated_text: Then I: 'Friend! Then show it.' Snatching the letter from his hand and looking at it with wonder, I said to myself: 'Ah! This spread of rows of letters appears to my eyes like a nectar-pencil!' — thus making known through the gesture of the transient mood of astonishment that the horripilation was indeed born of delight — then openly laughing: 'Wonder! Wonder! Like flowers in the sky, these cunning women have suddenly contrived something out of nothing!'

body.text:
madhumaṅgalaḥ -- vayasya!
vikaṭa-kuṭināṭi-kapaṭa-nāṭikā-tāṇḍavodbhaṭa-naṭāCārya-mahā-naṭīm imāṃ
tad advitīyāṃ durlalitāṃ lalitāṃ vāg-vilāsābhāsa-mātreṇaiova parājity a avatiṣṭha
te dhriyate yāvad eko'pi ripus tāvat kutaḥ sukham ity ādi saṃsmṛtya sarvāsām
asmad-vṛndāvana-rājya-kāṅkṣiṇīnāṃ dhūrtānāṃ tatim imām ito vṛndāvanāt
jhaṭiti vidrāvaya | tato niṣkaṇṭaka-rājye madhurāṇi rasavanti phalāny upabhujya
sukhenaivāhaṃ nṛtyann iva vasāmi |
body.translated_text: <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>: 'Friend! Having defeated this incomparable, mischievous <s>Lalitā</s> — the great actress, the master-dancer performing the spectacular dance of the fierce drama of crooked deceit — by the mere semblance of word-play alone, stand firm! Remembering that "as long as even one enemy remains, how can there be happiness?" and the like, quickly drive away from our <s>Vṛndāvana</s> this entire line of cunning women who desire our kingdom! Then, in a kingdom free of thorns, enjoying sweet and juicy fruits, I shall dwell happily as if dancing.'

body.text: tato mayoktaṃ -- lalite! iyam asmad-vṛndāṭavī | bhavat-sakhyā rājyaṃ kuto jātam |
body.translated_text: Then I said: 'O <s>Lalitā</s>! This is our <s>Vṛndā</s>-forest. How has your friend's kingdom come about?'

body.text:
lalitā -- parama-kapaṭin! tad-rājya-mahābhiṣeka-mahotsavaṃ samakṣam ākalayyāpi
kim evaṃ gopāyasi ?
body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s>: 'O supremely deceitful one! Having witnessed the great coronation festival of that kingdom with your own eyes, why do you conceal it thus?'

body.text:
tato'ham -- lalite! samakṣa-darśanaṃ tāvad-dūre 'stu tac-chravaṇam api jātam astīti
nāhaṃ smarāmi ?
body.translated_text: Then I: 'O <s>Lalitā</s>! Far from seeing it with my own eyes — I do not even remember having heard of it.'

body.text:
viśākhā --lalite! asya tāvad dūṣaṇaṃ nāsti |
ballava-sādhvī-śata-dharmollaṅghana-janita-tamaḥ-pracayenāntarhitam asty asya
cetas tat-saṃsargī ca tādṛśa iti etad-vayasyayor anayor api | tat katham ete smarantu
nāma ? tasmāt tat kathana-pīyūṣa-prasyandena karṇa-vivareṣu praveśiten bāḍham
amīṣāṃ cetāṃsi kāruṇyenāvirbhāvaya yathaiṣāṃ smṛtiḥ sampadyate |
body.translated_text: <s>Viśākhā</s>: 'O <s>Lalitā</s>! There is no fault of his in this. His mind is hidden by the mass of darkness born from transgressing the <s>dharma</s> of hundreds of cowherd women — and through that association, his companions too are of such character. So how can they possibly remember? Therefore, by pouring the nectar of that narration into the cavities of their ears, graciously cause their minds to manifest, so that their memory may be restored.'

body.text:
tatas tadānīm evāgatāṃ sarvābhir evānanditāṃ vṛndām āliṅgya lalitā sa-smitam
āha -- vṛnde! bhadrāvasare tvaṃ prāptāsi | tat tvayaiva nirvarṇyatāṃ
mahotsava-raṅgaḥ |
body.translated_text: Then, embracing <s>Vṛndā</s> who had just arrived and been welcomed by all, <s>Lalitā</s> said with a smile: 'O <s>Vṛndā</s>! You have arrived at an auspicious time. So let you yourself describe the great festival spectacle.'

body.text:
vṛndā sa-vinayānandaṃ -- sakhi lalite! tvan-mukha-padmād
viniṣyandamāna-tan-mahotsava-rasa-makarandam aham apy āpātum āgatāsmi tat
tvayaiva pariveṣyatām |
lalitā sānandam -- bhadraṃ sarvair avadhāya śrūyatām | ṛtu-pativasanta-samaye
paurṇamāsyāṃ viśākhā-nakṣatre bhagavato hiraṇyagarbhasya gagana-vāṇyā
vṛndāvana-vāsino bhagavataḥ śrī-gopīśvarasya svapna-kṛta-nideśena ca
mānasa-suradhunī-kālindyādi-sarid-varobhiḥ
sāvitrī-saṃjñaikānaṃśā-prabhṛti-devībhiś ca samaṃ
muralī-mahatī-jharjharī-muraja-dundubhi-prabhṛti-vādya-śabda-kolāhalenākṛṣ
ṭeṣu kinnarī-gandharvī-kuleṣu sānandaṃ gāyatsu | apsaro-vidyādharī-vargeṣu
nṛtyatsu śacyādi-surāṅganā-nicayeṣu jaya-jaya-śabda-pūrvakaṃ
pārijātādi-kusuma-vṛṣṭiṃ kurvatsu viśākhādi-sahacarī-samudayeṣu
parimilita-paṭa-vāsa-surāga-bandhana-nava-ghanasāra-kṣoda-mañjula-mṛgamada
-sulalita-kuṅkuma-paṭīra-drava-vividha-surabhi-kusuma-kulāni
sulalita-gāna-puraḥsaram itas tato vikiratsu bhūsura-ramaṇī-vṛndeṣu
śubhāśīḥ-śatāni vitaratsu ca
sakhī-vṛnda-samarpyamāṇa-śobhana-kuṅkumāguru-karpūra-candana-vividha-su
rabhi-kusumādi-suvāsita-jala-paripūrita-kāñcanāṣṭottara-śata-ghaṭaiḥ
suvarṇa-vedikā-nihita-padmarāga-maṇi-pīṭhopari sanniviṣṭāṃ priya-sakhīṃ
gāndarvāṃ bhagavatī paurṇamāsī sānandam abhiṣicya
vividha-sulakṣaṇa-mahāratna-sañcayodaka-sahasra-dhārābhir
jaya-jaya-śabda-pūrvakaṃ ratnābhiṣekaṃ cakāra |
body.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s>, with respectful joy: 'O friend <s>Lalitā</s>! I too have come to drink the nectar-essence of that great festival flowing from the lotus of your mouth. So let you yourself serve it.' <s>Lalitā</s>, with delight: 'Good! Let all pay attention and listen. In the spring season of the lord of seasons, on the full-moon day, under the <s>Viśākhā</s> constellation, by the celestial voice of the blessed <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, and by the command given in a dream by the blessed <s>Śrī Gopīśvara</s> dwelling in <s>Vṛndāvana</s> — together with the celestial rivers <s>Mānasa-Gaṅgā</s>, <s>Kālindī</s>, and other excellent rivers; together with the goddesses <s>Sāvitrī</s>, <s>Ekānaṃśā</s>, and others; with the tumultuous sounds of flute, great flute, kettledrum, <s>mṛdaṅga</s>, <s>dundubhi</s>, and other instruments drawing the families of <s>Kinnarīs</s> and <s>Gandharvīs</s> who sang with delight; with groups of <s>Apsarases</s> and <s>Vidyādharīs</s> dancing; with the host of divine women led by <s>Śacī</s> showering <s>Pārijāta</s> and other flowers with cries of "Victory! Victory!"; with the groups of companion-friends scattering here and there, accompanied by beautiful singing, various fragrant flowers, fresh camphor dust, beautiful musk, lovely saffron, and sandalwood paste; with groups of <s>brāhmaṇa</s> women bestowing hundreds of auspicious blessings — the venerable <s>Paurṇamāsī</s>, with delight, consecrated our dear friend <s>Gāndharvā</s>, who was seated upon a ruby throne placed upon a golden platform, with one hundred and eight golden vessels filled with water perfumed with excellent saffron, <s>aguru</s>, camphor, sandalwood, and various fragrant flowers offered by the circle of friends; and performed the jewel-consecration with thousands of streams of water infused with various auspicious great gems, with cries of "Victory! Victory!"'

body.text: vṛndā sa-harṣam -- tatas tataḥ ?
body.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s>, with joy: 'Then what? Then what?'

body.text:
lalitā tato mayaiva sucīna-vasanena śanaiḥ śanair aṅgāny āmṛjya surakta-dukūlaṃ
paridhāpya ketakī-kusuma-suvāsita-jalada-nīlottarīya-vasanenāvaguṇṭhya sukham
anyatara-kanaka-0pīṭhe niveśya
nānāvidha-kusuma-nava-guñjā-puñja-sumadhura-muktādi-maṇi-nikarai
nindita-śikhi-piñcha-kalāpa-kānti-sukeśa-pāśaṃ
sudīrgha-prāntocchalat-kusuma-gucchaṃ veṇītvenāvirbhāvya
sva-sva-sevā-karma-karmaṭha-parijana-gaṇa-dīyamāna-vividhālepa-bhūṣaṇa-mā
lyādibhir yathā-sthānaṃ yathā-śobhaṃ nikāmam alaṅkṛtety ardhokte
tat-smaraṇānanda-janita-kampa-pulaka-svara-bhaṅga-parimilita-divya-moham

children.text: āsādayantī sā lalitā viśākhayā sasambhramaṃ pṛṣṭhe samālambya karṇe rādhe
children.translated_text: was hurriedly supported from behind by <s>Viśākhā</s>, who whispered in her ear: '<s>Rādhe</s>!'

children.text: kṛṣṇa rādhe kṛṣṇeti kīrtanāmṛtena sandhukṣitā kṣaṇaṃ maunena dhairyam
children.translated_text: '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>! <s>Rādhe</s>! <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>!' — revived by the nectar of this chanting, she held composure in silence for a moment
and began to narrate again.

body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s>: 'Then, by me myself, gently wiping her limbs with fine cloth, dressing her in a deeply red silk garment, covering her with a jasmine-scented rain-cloud-dark upper garment, seating her comfortably upon a golden seat, making her hair — which put to shame the splendor of a peacock's tail-feather cluster — appear as a long braid adorned with various flowers, fresh <s>guñjā</s> berry clusters, sweet pearls and other gems, with flower bunches protruding at its spreading ends, adorning her lavishly in each proper place with various ointments, ornaments, garlands and the like provided by the attentive retinue of servants devoted to their respective duties...' — while saying 'adorned,' that <s>Lalitā</s>, overcome by a divine swoon mingled with trembling, horripilation, and voice-breaking, all born from the bliss of that memory —

body.text:
tadānīm eva mūrcchitāṃ lalitām ālakṣya -- hā
mat-prāṇa-pradīpa-rājinīrājita-carite priya-sakhi lalite! hata-bhāgyāhaṃ tvayā
nirāśā kṛtāsmi | hā bhagavan! bhakta-vatsala! bhāskara-deva! rakṣa rakṣa | hā
santatam
āpulinda-sakala-gokula-janāvanārtha-kalita-nirvikalpa-mahā-saṅkalpa-gokula-sud
hānidhe jhaṭiti nija-sudhāmaya-karābhimarṣaṇena
mad-vidha-jīvita-kokila-kula-jīvātu-lalitā-nāmādbhuta-pīyūṣa-rasāla-vallīṃ
jīvitām ācārya kilaitat-paṇenaiva saṃkrīya dāsī krityatām iyaṃ tapasvinī rādhiketi
vilapya sāśru-dhāraṃ vegena tām āliṅgitum āgacchantī rādhikā
rasamaya-sāttvika-mahā-stambha-santati-sahacaryā suṣṭhu pariṣvajya rakṣitāsīt |
body.translated_text: At that very moment, seeing <s>Lalitā</s> fainted — 'Alas! O dear friend <s>Lalitā</s>, whose life-story is illumined by the queenly row of my life-lamps! Ill-fated am I — you have left me bereft of hope! Alas, O Lord! O lover of devotees! O <s>Bhāskara-deva</s> (Sun-god)! Save her, save her! Alas! O treasury of nectar of <s>Gokula</s>, who has perpetually undertaken the unwavering great vow for the protection of all the people of <s>Gokula</s>, even the <s>Pulindas</s> and others! Quickly, by the touch of your own nectar-filled hand, the wondrous ambrosia-mango-vine named <s>Lalitā</s>, who is the elixir of life for the cuckoo-flock of lives such as mine — let her be revived! O master! By this very price, let me be purchased and made a maidservant — I, the wretched <s>Rādhikā</s>!' — thus lamenting, with a stream of tears, rushing forward to embrace her, <s>Rādhikā</s>, accompanied by a continuous succession of great ecstatic paralysis (<s>sāttvika-stambha</s>) born of <s>rasa</s>, was held in a tight embrace and protected.

body.text:
ity avakalanāt trāsena sāntaḥkampaṃ raṅgaṇavallī-tulasībhyāṃ tat-savidham
upalabdhaṃ tato raṅnaṇavallyā vāma-bhujayā tat-pṛṣṭham avaṣṭabhya
dakṣiṇa-kareṇa mṛdu mṛdu mṛjyamānā hā nātha rakṣa rakṣa iti sāśru-pravāhaṃ
sa-gadgada-bhāṣitena tulasyā tu nava-mṛdula-tamāla-pallava-kula-vyajanenātijavena
bījyamānā bāhyam upālabhya susthām iva lalitām ālokayantī sānandā babhūva |
body.translated_text: From perceiving this, <s>Raṅgaṇavallī</s> and <s>Tulasī</s>, trembling inwardly with fright, reached her side. Then <s>Raṅgaṇavallī</s>, supporting her back with her left arm and gently, gently wiping her with her right hand, cried 'O Lord, save, save!' with a stream of tears and choked speech. <s>Tulasī</s>, fanning her rapidly with a cluster of fresh, soft <s>tamāla</s> sprouts, looked outward and, seeing <s>Lalitā</s> appearing well again, became joyful.

body.text:
lalitā -- huṃ ? tāṃ tadā
tadānandocchalita-sāttvika-bhāvālaṅkāra-bhūṣita-sabhya-gaṇaiḥ saha bhagavatī
vicitra-ratna-siṃhāsanopari samupaveśya
ekānaṃśā-sodara-kāmākhyā-śyāmala-devatā-hṛdyasthāsakād
āhṛta-datta-mṛgamadena vṛndāvana-rājya-mahā-rājñītvena
śaṅkha-ghaṇṭā-dundubhi-kolāhala-śabda-pūrvakaṃ jaya-jaya-śabdena tilakaṃ
cakāra |
body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s> — 'Hmm?' Then, together with the members of the assembly adorned with <s>sāttvika-bhāva</s> (ecstatic emotional) ornaments arising from the joy of that moment, <s>Bhagavatī</s> (<s>Rādhā</s>) was seated upon a wonderful jeweled throne, and with musk brought from the heart-abode of <s>Kāmākhyā</s>, the dark deity (<s>Śyāmala-devatā</s>) who is the sister of <s>Ekānaṃśā</s>, she was anointed with the <s>tilaka</s> of sovereignty as the great queen of the kingdom of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, preceded by the clamor of conch, bell, and drum and the cry of 'Victory! Victory!'

body.text:
tata etac-chravaṇena sarvāsām ānanda-hāsa-kolāhale jāte
tac-chravaṇānanda-samutthita-sāttvikādy-anubhāvān yatnenāvṛtya kiñcid vihasya
mayoktaṃ -- lalite! etat kathaṃ mayā na jñāyate etena kiṃ vo rājyam āyātam ?
pratyuta etad uṭṭaṅkanāt sva-mukhenaiva bhavatībhir yuṣmat-sahitam idaṃ rājyaṃ
mamaiveti nirṇītam |
body.translated_text: Then, when joyous laughter and uproar arose among all upon hearing this, I, carefully concealing the ecstatic and other involuntary responses arising from the joy of hearing it, laughed a little and said — '<s>Lalitā</s>! How is this not known to me? What kingdom has come to you by this? On the contrary, by this very proclamation, you yourselves have determined through your own mouths that this kingdom, together with you all, is mine alone.'

body.text: nāndīmukhī -- katham iva ?
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s> — 'How so?'

body.text:
tato'ham -- yato vṛndāvana-purandarasya mamaiva rājñītvena mad-iṅgitenaiva
bhagavaty-abhiṣikteyam ||
body.translated_text: Then I said — 'Because, as I am the lord of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, <s>Bhagavatī</s> anointed her to queenship at my very behest.'

body.text:
viśākhā vihasya -- asaṅgata-bhāṣin! purandarasya mahiṣi devy eva bhavati | sā
khalu śacīti prasiddhā svarge vasati | iyaṃ tu mama sakhī bhūmi-vihāriṇī
subhagābhimanyor jāyā mānuṣī |
body.translated_text: <s>Viśākhā</s>, laughing — 'O speaker of nonsense! The consort of <s>Purandara</s> (Indra) is indeed a goddess. She is well-known as <s>Śacī</s> and dwells in heaven. But this friend of mine is an earthly-dwelling mortal, the wife of the fortunate <s>Abhimanyu</s>.'

body.text:
mayoktaṃ -- tarkācārya-śiromaṇiṃ-manye viśākhe! tvaṃ suṣṭhu jaḍāsi yad bāraṃ
bāram adhītam api pratyakṣa-khaṇḍaṃ tvayā vismṛtam eva |
body.translated_text: I said — 'O <s>Viśākhe</s>! I consider you the crest-jewel of logicians! You are truly dull, for though studied again and again, you have forgotten the very chapter on <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception).'

body.text: viśākhā -- kiṃ tad vismṛtam ?
body.translated_text: <s>Viśākhā</s> — 'What have I forgotten?'

body.text:
mayoktaṃ -- śrūyatām | yadi bhavat-sahacarī mat-preyasī na syāt tarhi
mad-vakṣaḥ-sthāsakāhṛta-mṛgamadena kathaṃ bhagavatī tāṃ tilakinīṃ cakāra ?
kathaṃ vā mat-kaṇṭha-mālā-hāra-vaijayantībhyāṃ tat-kaṇṭham alañcakāra ?
body.translated_text: I said — 'Listen! If your companion were not my beloved, then how did <s>Bhagavatī</s> anoint her with the <s>tilaka</s> using musk taken from the treasury of my chest? And how did she adorn her throat with the garland-necklace and <s>Vaijayantī</s> from my neck?'

body.text:
lalitā -- bhoḥ śaśa-śṛṅga-dhanurdharālīka-purandara!
pravara-subhaga-lekhāvali-kalita-padāravindāyāḥ
gandharva-vidyādhara-gaṇa-gīyamāna-mahā-vaibhavāyāḥ ātmabhuvāpi
saṃstūyamāna-caritāyāḥ vividha-kāma-sampatti-dāyinyāḥ
nandy-ādīśvara-gṛhiṇyāḥ kāmāripur-vāsinyāḥ vindhya-vāstavyaikānaṃśāgrajāyāḥ
kāmākhyā-nāma-śyāmala-devatāyāḥ mahāprasāda-mṛgamada-mālābhir eva sā
kila bhagavatyā vibhūṣitā | tava kas tatra sambandhaḥ ?
body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s> — 'O wielder of the bow of hare-horns, O false <s>Purandara</s>! She was adorned by the great grace — the musk garlands — of the dark deity named <s>Kāmākhyā</s>: she whose lotus feet are adorned with rows of excellent auspicious marks, whose great glory is sung by hosts of <s>Gandharvas</s> and <s>Vidyādharas</s>, whose exploits are praised even by the Self-born (<s>Brahmā</s>), who bestows various desired riches, who is the consort of <s>Nandy-ādi-Īśvara</s>, who resides in <s>Kāmāri-pura</s>, who is the elder sister of <s>Ekānaṃśā</s> dwelling in the <s>Vindhya</s>. What is your connection there?'

body.text: tuṅgavidyā -- sakhi lalite! sādhu sambodhitaṃ yad ayam alīka-purandara eva |
body.translated_text: <s>Tuṅgavidyā</s> — 'Friend <s>Lalitā</s>! Well addressed — for this one is indeed the false <s>Purandara</s>.'

body.text: viśākhā -- katham iva ?
body.translated_text: <s>Viśākhā</s> — 'How so?'

body.text:
tuṅgavidyā -- śrūyatāṃ asmin māthura-pradeśe yācaka-dvija-kalāvadādibhir eva
pañcaviṃśati-kaparrdikā-mātra-labdhaye deva! mahārājety-alīka-sambodhanaiḥ
kṣudrataraika-grāmādhyakṣo'pi yathā praphullito bhavati tathaiva
śakrāśanāśana-durgata-bhaṇḍa-bhaṭṭādi-vargaiḥ
palaika-parimita-navanīta-mātram āptuṃ vṛndāvana-purandareti
kṛtāsambhavālīka-sambodhana-pūrvaka-stavābhāsenaiva nisargāgambhīra eṣa
kṛṣībalo bāḍham ātmanaḥ purnadaratā-mananena
nija-jālmato'marāvatī-purandaratvam eva prakaṭīcakāra |
body.translated_text: <s>Tuṅgavidyā</s> — 'Listen — in this <s>Mathurā</s> region, just as a petty village headman becomes puffed up by the false addresses "O Lord! O Great King!" from begging Brahmins and skilled artisans seeking a mere twenty-five cowrie shells, similarly this farmer (<s>kṛṣībala</s>), who is inherently shallow, has been addressed with impossible false praise as "Lord of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>" by the likes of <s>Śakrāśana</s> (he who eats <s>Indra</s>'s food), the poor merchant <s>Bhaṇḍa-bhaṭṭa</s>, and others — and thereby, through contemplating his own <s>Purandara</s>-hood, he has only manifested his own wretchedness as the supposed <s>Purandara</s>-hood of <s>Amarāvatī</s>'s <s>Indra</s>.'

body.text:
tatas tuṅgavidyā narma-smitam apavārya -- bhoḥ
pāvana-sarovara-jambāla-jāta-jāmbunada-jāta-sutāra-muktāphalādi-vividha-ratn
a-vrāta-viracita-mahā-siṃhāsanopari suṣṭhu niviṣṭasya
saurabha-bharonmādīkṛtāruṇa-bhramara-kulocchalita-jhaṅkāra-rava-nikareṇānu
gamyamāna-nirmala-gagana-sumanaḥ-prapañcāvirbhāvita-vara-mukuṭa-bandhāti
bandhūrottamāṅgasya sānandaṃ śirasi subalena
dhṛta-pariṇata-kamaṭha-kaṭhora-pṛṣṭha-supakṣa-kṛta-prakaṭa-surabhi-sudh-ka
ṇābhivarṣi-pravarāṭapatrasya
masṛṇatarakaratalodbhuta-tanurūha-prakara-racita-cāmara-dvayenojjvala-caturābh
yām ubhaya-pārśvayor ānandenābhivījyamānasya,
atisupratiṣṭhita-bandhyā-garbha-jāta-mahā-mahā-sat-puruṣa-vargaiḥ
padma-gandhābhidhādivalīvardha-sañcayānāṃ sumadhura-payaḥ-pravāheṇa
vṛndāṭavī-mahendratve'bhiṣiktasya,
pariṇata-saśottuṅga-śṛṅga-vinirmita-mañjula-kārmukālaṅkṛta-vāma-kara-muṣṭ
ikasyāsya, tad avadhi yaśaḥ-pratāpa-prakāśa-laharī brahmāṇḍa-bhare yādṛśī
prasarantī vartate | tām anubhavantībhir bhavatībhir api sākṣān mahendratvaṃ yan
na manyate, tad bhavatīnām anayo'yaṃ mahān eveti mayi prabhāsate |
body.translated_text: Then <s>Tuṅgavidyā</s>, suppressing a playful smile — 'O friends! He who is well-seated upon a great throne fashioned from various gems — pearls, gold, and other precious things — born from the mud of the sacred purifying lake; whose supreme crown-binding consists of heavenly flowers manifested in the spotless sky, accompanied by the buzzing swarm-sounds of reddish bees maddened by fragrance; upon whose head <s>Subala</s> joyfully holds a superb parasol made from the hard back-shell of a mature tortoise, raining down drops of sweet ambrosia; who is brilliantly fanned on both sides by two clever ones with a pair of fly-whisks fashioned from the mass of fine hairs sprouting from the smoothest palms; who was consecrated as the great <s>Indra</s> of <s>Vṛndā</s>'s forest with the sweet milk-streams of herds of cows named <s>Padma-gandhā</s> and the like, by throngs of supremely well-established, great, great virtuous men born from the wombs of barren women — the wave of his fame, glory, and radiance spreads throughout the universe as it does! And you who experience it directly do not consider him the great <s>Indra</s> — that, I declare, is indeed your great misfortune!'

body.text:
iti niśamya sa-smitaṃ nayana-kūṇanena sa-smita-lajjita-man-mukham ālokya
parasparaṃ cālokayantīṣu tāsu citrā vihasya - bhoḥ katham asau pariahasyate
bhavatībhyām ? satyam evāyaṃ devendraḥ |
body.translated_text: Hearing this, with smiling squinted eyes, as they all looked at my embarrassed smiling face and at one another, <s>Citrā</s>, laughing — 'O friends! How can he be mocked by you? Truly, this one is the Lord of the gods (<s>Devendra</s>)!'

body.text: tuṅgavidyā - citre! iti cet sa katham atrāgataḥ ?
body.translated_text: <s>Tuṅgavidyā</s> — '<s>Citrā</s>! If so, how did he come here?'

body.text:
citrā - śrūyatām | para-ramaṇīto'yam iti sarvataḥ samadhigamya krodhinyā devā
padāghātena nirbhartstas tāṃ parama-sukhada-tan-nija-bhavanaṃ ca nirvedataḥ
parityajya vanam idam āgatya parama-mañjula-navīna-gopatvam ivāsādya
puraścaraṇa-vidhānenaiva vṛndāvaneśvaryāḥ karṣako bhūtvā sukhena samayaṃ
gamayann asti | tad enaṃ hāsya-rasa-viṣayālambanam avidhāya
bāṭika-rūpa-prāghuṇe' smin sneha eva nikāmaṃ vidhīyatām |
body.translated_text: <s>Citrā</s> — 'Listen! This one, being a lover of other men's wives — having been found out by all, the angry goddess (<s>Śacī</s>) expelled him with a kick. Abandoning her and that supremely delightful heavenly abode out of disgust, he came to this forest, assumed the charming guise of a fresh young cowherd, and by performing the ritual of <s>puraścaraṇa</s> (preliminary worship) to the goddess of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, became her farmer-servant and passes his time happily. Therefore, do not make him an object of comic ridicule, but rather bestow abundant affection upon this stranger-guest in the guise of a gardener.'

body.text:
tac chrutvā sarvāsu smera-mukhīṣu nāndīmukhī vihasya - sakhi citre! vraja eva
nitya-vihāriṇi vrajendra-nandane yat kiñcit tvayedaṃ vyāhṛtam | tasya
śabdārthottha-gūḍhābhiprāyeṇa bhavitavyam iti lakṣyate | tatas tasya
vivecana-pūrvaka-kathanenāsmān baḍham ānandaya |
body.translated_text: Hearing that, as all had smiling faces, <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>, laughing — 'Friend <s>Citrā</s>! Regarding the son of <s>Vrajendra</s> (the lord of <s>Vraja</s>), who sports eternally in <s>Vraja</s> itself, whatever you have spoken here — there must be a hidden meaning arising from the connotations of those words, it appears. So explain it to us analytically and thoroughly delight us.'

body.text:
tataḥ smitvā muni-vratam ālambitavatyāṃ citrāyāṃ vṛndā sānandam āha -
nāndīmukhi! asyāḥ parama-vidagdhāyā gūḍhābhiprāyaḥ sphuṭaṃ mayaiva
nirvarṇyamānaḥ suṣṭhu samākarṇyatām |
body.translated_text: Then, as <s>Citrā</s>, smiling, adopted a vow of silence, <s>Vṛndā</s> joyfully said — '<s>Nāndīmukhī</s>! I shall clearly expound the hidden meaning of this supremely clever one — listen well.'

body.text: nāndīmukhīn - katham asya devendratvam ? tat prakaṭaya |
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s> — 'How is he the Lord of the gods (<s>Devendra</s>)? Make it clear.'

body.text:
vṛndā - dīvyanti krīḍantīti devāḥ - vicitra-vividha-manohara-keli-vilāsa-śālinaḥ |
tathā dīvyanti viśeṣeṇa dyotante iti devāḥ |
paramojjvala-tejas-taraṅga-hṛdyādbhuta-saundaryāmṛta-pravāha-śālinas teṣāṃ
teṣām apīndro mahā-parivṛḍha iti devendras tebhyo'pi paramotkarṣeṇa suṣṭhu
virājamāna ity arthaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> — 'Those who sport and play are <s>devas</s> — those who possess wondrous, varied, and enchanting amorous arts. Also, those who shine extraordinarily are <s>devas</s> — those who possess the flow of supremely radiant, dazzling, wondrously beautiful nectar of beauty. And the <s>Indra</s> (chief) of even those — the supreme sovereign — is <s>Devendra</s>. The meaning is: he who outshines even all of them with supreme excellence.'

body.text:
nāndīmukhī sa-smitaṃ - samīcīno'yam artho vivṛtaḥ kintu para-ramaṇī-rata ity
asya ko'rthaḥ ?
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>, smiling — 'This meaning is well explained. But what is the meaning of "lover of other men's wives" (<s>para-ramaṇī-rata</s>)?'

body.text:
vṛndā - parā anyā tathā parā vipakṣā, tathā parā paramotkṛṣṭā, parā cāsau
ramaṇī ceti para-ramaṇī śrī-rādhikā tasyāṃ rataḥ paramāśaktas tām eva
paramānurāgeṇa ramayann ity arthaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s>: '<s>Parā</s> means "another," also "an opponent," and also "supremely exalted." <s>Parā</s> meaning "supreme" combined with <s>ramaṇī</s> ("beloved woman") gives <s>para-ramaṇī</s>, that is, <s>Śrī Rādhikā</s>. <s>Rataḥ</s> means "supremely attached to her," that is, he who delights her with supreme passionate love — such is the meaning.'

body.text: campakalatā smitvā - vṛnde! devy api nirūpyatām |
body.translated_text: <s>Campakalatā</s>, smiling: '<s>Vṛndā</s>! Let <s>devī</s> also be analyzed.'

body.text:
vṛndā - nādevo devam arcayed iti caṇḍikā-paricaryāparatvāt asya devasya bhāryeti
vā | kiṃ vā amaṅgale maṅgala-śabdavad iyaṃ devī |
body.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s>: '"A non-god should not worship a god" — since she is devoted to the service of <s>Caṇḍikā</s>, she is the wife of this god. Or else, like the word <s>maṅgala</s> (auspicious) applied to something inauspicious, this one is a <s>devī</s> (goddess).'

body.text: nāndīmukhī - seyaṃ kā ?
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>: 'Who is this one?'

body.text: viśākhā - etādṛśī candāvaly eva bhaviṣyati |
body.translated_text: <s>Viśākhā</s>: 'Such a one can only be <s>Candāvalī</s>.'

body.text:
vṛndā smitvā maunam ālambate | sarvāḥ smitaṃ kurvanti | nāndīmukhī
padāghāteneti dhārṣṭyātiśayena tasyā anuttamatā sphuṭaiva kintu
parama-sukhada-tan-nija-bhavanaṃ vā katarat ?
body.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> smiled and remained silent. All smiled. <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>: '"By a stamp of the foot" — by the excess of boldness, her being the lowest is obvious enough. But which is her own dwelling that gives supreme happiness?'

body.text:
vṛndā - niviḍatva-puṣpavattva-bhṛṅga-guñjitvādi-rāhitvāt param asukhadam | kiṃ
vā parama-sukhaṃ dārayatīti parama-sukhadaṃ yat tasyā devyā nija-bhavanaṃ
sakhīsthalī-nikaṭa-vartinaṃ tad apahāya |
body.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s>: 'Since it lacks the qualities of denseness, floweriness, buzzing of bees, and so forth, it gives supreme unhappiness. Or else, <s>parama-sukhada</s> means "that which breaks (<s>dārayati</s>) supreme happiness" — that is the dwelling of that <s>devī</s>, situated near the rival's ground, which he abandons.'

body.text:
nāndīmukhī - aho! śabdānāṃ gūḍhārtha-vijñāyās tava vyākhyā-kauśalaṃ tad
asmādṛśībhir duravagāho navīna-gopatvādi-padānāṃ gūḍho'rthaḥ kṛpayā
prakāśyatām |
vṛndā -
veṇu-viṣāṇa-laguḍa-niryoga-pāśa-giri-dhātu-citra-nava-śikhaṇḍa-guñjāhārāraṇy
a-śṛṅgāra-dhāritvaṃ mañjula-navīna-gopatvaṃ tatrāpi navīna-śabdena tasya
prathamato nitya-nūtanatā ca dhvanitā | puraścaraṇa-saṃvidhāneneti puraḥ
saṃmukhe bhṛṅga-raṇita-kusuma-kalita-bakula-rāja-tale caraṇaṃ
proddāma-madonmatta-gajendravad-vividha-vilāsa-samullāsitam itas tato bhramaṇaṃ
tat-puraḥ-saraṃ yat saṃvidhānaṃ
līlā-kamala-cumbana-kaṅkelli-nava-pallavavad-aṃśena
nistula=nistala-dāḍimī-phala-kara-vinyāsa-kāñcan-yūthikā-samāliṅgana-pūrvaka
-smita-nava-karpūra-saṃmilita-cañcala-nayana-kamalāñcalāvalokana-paramonmād
aka-madhura-mādhvīka-pāyanam | tena
malli-bakula-campaka-mādhavī-kanaka-yūthikādi-kusuma-cayana-vilāsa-mādhur
ī-bharam anubhavantyāḥ śrī-vṛndāvana-rājadhānī-vilāsinyāḥ karṣaka ākarṣako
bhūtvā tena tām unmādya nija-nikaṭam ākṛṣyety arthaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>: 'Wonderful! Your skill in expounding the hidden meanings of words! The hidden meaning of terms like <s>navīna-gopa</s> ("new cowherd") is difficult for the likes of us to grasp — please kindly reveal it.' <s>Vṛndā</s>: 'The bearing of flute, horn, staff, yoke, rope, mountain-minerals, colorful new peacock-feather, <s>guñjā</s>-berry necklace, and forest adornments — that is the charming new-cowherd-hood. Moreover, by the word <s>navīna</s> ("new"), his eternally ever-new nature from the very first is suggested. "By the arrangement of <s>puraścaraṇa</s>" means: with the frontal approach — like a wildly intoxicated great elephant, his roaming here and there, enlivened with various playful delights, under the <s>bakula</s> tree adorned with blossoming flowers resounding with bees, preceding [her path] — that arrangement means: the drinking of supremely maddening, sweet honey-wine through the glancing of restless lotus-petal eyes combined with the smile of fresh camphor, preceded by the embrace of the golden jasmine, the placing of hands upon the incomparable seedless pomegranate fruit, with a portion like the new sprout of the <s>kaṅkelli</s> tree kissed by a playful lotus. By that, becoming the <s>karṣaka</s> ("farmer" or "attractor") of the queen of the capital of <s>Śrī Vṛndāvana</s>, who experiences the fullness of sweetness of the amorous sport of gathering flowers of <s>mallī</s>, <s>bakula</s>, <s>campaka</s>, <s>mādhavī</s>, <s>kanaka-yūthikā</s>, and so forth — the meaning is: having maddened her by that, he draws her near to himself.'

body.text:
sukhena ślāghya-madhura-madhura-rasāsvādana-janita-paramānanda-sandohena
samayaṃ sahaja-sarvadojjṛmbhamāṇa-vasanta-kālaṃ nirantaraṃ
nirupama-vilāsa-mādhurībhiḥ saubhāgya-lakṣmī-bharaṃ gamayan prāpayann asti
tayā sahānavaratam anirvacanīya-madhura-khelā-vilāsa-tat-paraḥ san sadā virājata
eveti |
body.translated_text: 'With the supreme flood of bliss born of the tasting of that praiseworthy, sweet, sweet <s>rasa</s>, spending the time — the spring season that naturally always manifests — ceaselessly with incomparable sweetness of amorous play, bringing and attaining the fullness of the splendor of good fortune, ever absorbed in inexpressibly sweet playful sport together with her, he shines eternally.'

body.text:
tato'haṃ sāntar-ānandaṃ -viśākhā-ghātini vṛnde mama vṛndāvanodyāna-pālikāpi
tvaṃ katham etāsu militāsi ?
body.translated_text: Then I, with inner joy: 'O <s>Vṛndā</s>, slayer of <s>Viśākhā</s>! Even you, the guardian of my <s>Vṛndāvana</s> garden — how have you joined among these women?'

body.text:
madhumaṅgalaḥ - priya-vayasya! iyam udyāna-pālī
sa-lavaṇa-takra-ślathita-bhakta-bhakṣaṇāya tad-udyāna-pālanaṃ parityajya
sāmpratam āsāṃ gṛha-pālī vṛttāsti | tat kathaṃ na bukkiṣyate ?
body.translated_text: <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>: 'Dear friend! This garden-keeper, in order to eat rice softened with salty buttermilk, has abandoned the care of that garden and now serves as a house-keeper for these women. So how would she not bark [like a guard dog]?'

body.text:
vṛndā - aye bhūsurābhāsa! kuṭabaṭo!
nija-sahacara-prathama-mudira-vacana-jaladhārā-varṣeṇa praphulla-varṣābhūs tvaṃ
santata-śravaṇa-kaṭu-śabdaṃ kurvan sarvān udvejayann asi |
body.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s>: 'Oh you sham <s>brāhmaṇa</s>! You impostor! Made to bloom like the rainy season by the rain-shower of words from your friend, the foremost rain-cloud, you constantly make harsh sounds grating to the ears and distress everyone.'

body.text:
mallī-bhṛṅgyau - devi lalite! svāminyā yad anya-patreṇa likhitam asti | tat kiṃ
vismṛtaṃ bhavatyā ?
body.translated_text: <s>Mallī</s> and <s>Bhṛṅgī</s>: 'O lady <s>Lalitā</s>! What was written in the letter from our mistress's other source — has your ladyship forgotten it?'

body.text: lalitā - kiṃ tat smāryatām |
body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s>: 'What was that? Remind me.'

body.text:
mallī-bhṛṅgyau - samucita-kara-dāne yaḥ kuyuktim uttolya virodham ācarati so'tra
baddhvā śīghraṃ praheya iti |
body.translated_text: <s>Mallī</s> and <s>Bhṛṅgī</s>: '"Whoever, when a proper tax-payment is due, stirs up a false pretext and commits obstruction — let him be seized and bound and promptly sent away."'

body.text:
lalitā - āṃ | tat-kara-dāna-virodhī madhumaṅgala eva | tad enaṃ latā-pāśena
dṛḍhaṃ nibadhya komalāyāḥ priya-sakhyāḥ savidham ānītvaiva
jaṭilābhimanyu-pārśve yuvābhyām eva satvaraṃ samarpyatām | yathā sa
yāva-grāma-siṃho'bhimanyur eva tāḍana-pūrvakaṃ sva-karaṃ gṛhṇāti |
body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s>: 'Ah yes! The one who obstructs the tax-payment is none other than <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>. So bind him tightly with a creeper-rope, bring him before the dear friend of the tender one (<s>Komalā</s>), and you two deliver him promptly to <s>Jaṭilā</s> and <s>Abhimanyu</s>'s side. Let that lion of <s>Yāva</s>-village, <s>Abhimanyu</s> himself, take his hand after giving him a beating.'

body.text:
madhumaṅgalaḥ antaḥ-sa-bhayam iva - vayasya! kiñcin nigūḍhaṃ kāryaṃ mama gṛhe
vidyate | tat sampādyāgacchann asmi |
body.translated_text: <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>, as if inwardly fearful: 'Friend! There is some secret business at my house. I am going to attend to it and will return.'

body.text: tato'haṃ - dhig brāhmaṇa! katham abalā-vāg-āḍambareṇa mad-agrato'pi bibheṣi ?
body.translated_text: Then I: 'Shame on you, <s>brāhmaṇa</s>! How can you be frightened even before me by the bluster of women?'

body.text:
madhumaṅgalaḥ - mahāśūra! ghaṭṭī-pālasya tava govardhane dāna-vartanyāṃ
bahuśaḥ śauryaṃ anubhūtam asti | yat tasmin dine etābhir eva
vṛndāvana-kara-nimittaṃ gāndharvā-nideśena nijottarīya-paṭāñcalena baddhā
nīyamānam api māṃ vīkṣamāṇa eva vilakṣas tvam āsīḥ | aham eva
nija-bhūsuratvaṃ vivṛtya bhāgyena kathañcid urvārito'smi |
body.translated_text: <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>: 'O great hero! Your valor, O toll-keeper, has been amply experienced many times on the toll-road at <s>Govardhana</s>! On that day, when by the order of <s>Gāndharvā</s> (<s>Rādhā</s>), these very women bound me with the border of their own upper garments on account of the <s>Vṛndāvana</s> tax, even as I was being led away, you merely watched, embarrassed. It was I myself who, by revealing my <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-hood, was somehow fortunately released!'

body.text:
ity uktvā bhītim anukṛtya palāyantam iva taṃ kare gṛhītvā parāvartya mayoktaṃ -
 lalite! tādṛśyāḥ komalābalāyā api katham ahaṃ karaṃ dāsyāmi ? pratyuta balāt
kāmam ādāsya eva |
body.translated_text: Having said this, as he feigned fear and pretended to flee, I seized his hand, turned him back, and said: '<s>Lalitā</s>! How could I possibly give the hand of such a tender young woman [to <s>Abhimanyu</s>]? Rather, I shall forcibly take it myself!'

body.text: iti niśamya netra-bhāgena mām īṣad avalokayantī rādhā susmitā āsīt |
body.translated_text: Hearing this, <s>Rādhā</s>, glancing at me slightly from the corner of her eye, wore a gentle smile.

body.text: nāndīmukhī - citre! bāṭikā-prāghuṇa ity asya kas tāvad abhiprāyaḥ ?
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>: '<s>Citrā</s>! What is the meaning of <s>bāṭikā-prāghuṇa</s> ("garden-guest")?'

body.text:
lalitā - nāndīmukhi! taj jānaty api kathaṃ pṛcchasi ? yat
sarva-kālīna-nija-vāsa-grāma-mahāvanam apahāya vatsara-ṣaṭ-saptaka-mātram
atrāgato'sti |
body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s>: '<s>Nāndīmukhī</s>! Though you know it, why do you ask? He has come here for a mere six or seven years, abandoning the great forest of his own eternal dwelling-village.'

body.text: nāndīmukhī - priya-janma-bhūmes tyāgena kiṃ tāvat kāraṇam ?
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>: 'What was the reason for leaving his beloved birthplace?'

body.text:
rādhā auccaiḥ - tat-sthānasyāsvācchandyāt janatādhikyena tad-grāme nagara iva
jāte
abalā-vadha-bhāṇḍa-sphoṭana-nava-nīta-haraṇādi-vividha-visadṛśa-vyavasāyābh
yāsena janita-bahu-vidha-vikarmābhilāṣasyāsiddhatvāt nirjane'smin mahati ghane
vṛndāvane kulābalā-kulānāṃ geha-deha adhara-daśana-vasanāni
svācchandyenāpahartum adhika-lālasaiva |
body.translated_text: <s>Rādhā</s>, aloud: 'Due to the lack of freedom in that place, when that village became like a city owing to the great number of people, his various improper occupational habits — such as killing women, breaking pots, stealing fresh butter, and other such unseemly enterprises — generated manifold unlawful desires that could not be fulfilled there. So he is all the more eager to steal at his whim the homes, bodies, lips, teeth, and garments of the families of noble women in this vast, dense, solitary <s>Vṛndāvana</s>.'

body.text:
ity evaṃ lalitayā sphuṭaṃ vyāhṛte sa-smitaṃ sākūtam āha - lalite! sāmpratam asya
tādṛśa-vyavasāyo na dṛśyate |
body.translated_text: When <s>Lalitā</s> had spoken this openly, she (<s>Rādhā</s>) said with a smile and a pointed look: '<s>Lalitā</s>! At present, no such enterprise of his is to be seen.'

body.text:
rādhā punar anuccaiḥ - satyam eva kathyate | yad ayaṃ samprati sva-dharma-tyāgena
visadṛśa-saṃskāreṇa ca janitānyādṛśa-buddhi-kṛta-cauryādi-duṣkṛtaṃ lalitācāryayā
pūrvam api vihita-niṣkṛtena nirvāsya, nirveda-kṛta-vivekena tāsām eva kṛṣi-vṛttam
eva nija-dharmam ācarya prakāmaṃ śasyāny utpādya tābhyaḥ pradāya tat svāṃśam
api svayam ādāya tāḥ svātmānam apy ānandayan mahāśucir iva virājate | ity eva
sphuṭaṃ viśākhāpi sa-smitaṃ bhāṣitavatī |
body.translated_text: <s>Rādhā</s> again, softly: 'It is truly said that this one, who had committed misdeeds of theft and the like through a distorted mentality generated by abandoning his own <s>dharma</s> and by improper training, was formerly banished by the teacher <s>Lalitā</s> with a prescribed expiation. Then, through the discernment born of disillusionment, adopting as his own <s>dharma</s> the very farming occupation of those women, producing abundant crops and giving them to those women while also taking his own share, delighting both them and himself, he shines forth as if supremely purified.' Thus <s>Viśākhā</s> too spoke with a smile, openly.

body.text:
tatas tan niśamya sarveṣu hāsa-kolāhala-mahotsavam āviṣkurvatsu sa-kapaṭāsūyaṃ
mayoktam - sakhe subala! dhūrtābhir imābhir narma-bhaṅgī-miṣeṇa mama
vṛndāvana-rājyādhikāritaiva dūrīkriyamāṇāstīti samadhigataṃ bhavatā |
subalaḥ - na kevalam adhikāritaiva dūrīkṛtā kintu karṣako'pi kṛto'si |
body.translated_text: Then, hearing that, while everyone was manifesting a great festival of uproarious laughter, I said with feigned jealousy: 'Friend <s>Subala</s>! It has been ascertained by you that these crafty women, under the pretext of playful jesting, are stripping away my very sovereignty over <s>Vṛndāvana</s>!' <s>Subala</s>: 'Not only has your sovereignty been stripped away, but you have even been made into a farmer!'

body.text:
vṛndā - subala! tvaṃ bahu-śruto vicakṣaṇas tathānayor api parama-snigdhaḥ | tat
kathaṃ nāndīmukhyā sahānayorḥ parama-snigdhayor api rājya-hetor
vivadamānayor ucita-nyāyāvalokanena virodhaṃ na davayasi ?
body.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s>: '<s>Subala</s>! You are learned and discerning, and also most tenderly affectionate to both of them. Why then do you not quell this dispute between these two supremely affectionate ones who are quarreling over sovereignty, by applying proper justice together with <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>?'

body.text:
tato bhadraṃ bhadram iti mayā lalitayā cokte subalaḥ prāha - vayasya! prathamaṃ
tāvat katham āsām etad rājyaṃ tal lalitaiva kathayatu | paścād bhavān api kathaṃ
vā bhavad-rājyaṃ taj jñāpayatu |
body.translated_text: Then, when I and <s>Lalitā</s> both said 'Very well, very well!' <s>Subala</s> said: 'Friend! First of all, let <s>Lalitā</s> herself explain how this sovereignty belongs to these women. Then let your lordship also explain how it is your sovereignty.'

body.text:
tato'haṃ - subala! yāsāṃ vraja-deva-kanyānām ajñānenāpi saṅgam ācarya
jāta-vyalīko'haṃ prāyaścittena śuddho'bhavaṃ sa kathaṃ tābhiḥ samam api punar
vākovākaṃ vistarayāmi ?
body.translated_text: Then I: '<s>Subala</s>! Having wrongfully associated even unknowingly with those girls of the <s>Vraja</s>-gods, I became guilty and was purified by expiation — how then could I again engage in dispute with them?'

body.text:
vṛndā - mahāśuddha! bhavad-vāg-gandha-mātreṇāpi samudita-kaluṣa-sañcayā etā
api śrī-vṛndāvana-cakravartinyā nūnam aśeṣa-vidhinā
śyāmala-viṣama-śara-sarovara-mahā-tīrthe punaḥ punaḥ snapanena śuddīkṛtā eva
sva-nikaṭam āpitāḥ santi tac cīrṇa-niṣkṛtayor ubhayoḥ saṃvāde doṣo nāsti | tal
lalite! bhavaty eva kathayatu |
body.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s>: 'O supremely pure one! Even by the mere scent of your words, these ones, in whom a mass of impurity had arisen, have surely been purified by <s>Śrī Vṛndāvana-cakravartinī</s> through every prescribed rite — by bathing them again and again in the great <s>tīrtha</s> of the dark and formidable <s>Śara-sarovara</s> — and thus brought near to her. Therefore, since both have completed their penance, there is no fault in their conversing. So, <s>Lalitā</s>! Let your good self speak.'

body.text:
lalitā - prathamaṃ tāvad asmin vṛndāvana-rājye'syālīka-vādino dhūrtasyādhipatyaṃ
tāvad dūre'stu sambandha-leśo'pi nāsti |
body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s>: 'First of all, in this kingdom of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, let alone sovereignty, this false-speaking rogue has not even the slightest connection to it!'

body.text: nāndīmukhī - katham iva ?
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>: 'How so?'

body.text: lalitā - sva-paitṛka-rājye bṛhad-vana eva kula-kramāgata-santata-vāsitvāt |
body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s>: 'Because his ancestral kingdom is <s>Bṛhadvana</s> alone, where his family has resided continuously by hereditary succession.'

body.text: nāndīmukhī - kim atra pramāṇam ?
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>: 'What is the evidence for this?'

body.text: lalitā - bhāgavatādi-purāṇa-vaktṛ-vyāsādi-munīndra-vacanāny eva |
body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s>: 'The very words of the foremost sages such as <s>Vyāsa</s> and others, who are the speakers of the <s>Bhāgavata</s> and other <s>Purāṇas</s>.'

body.text:
subalaḥ - lalite! madhyasthena mayā yathārtham eva vaktavyam | tvan-mukham
ālokya mithyā vaktuṃ na śakyate | tad asya bṛhad-vana-rājyatvenaiva bhavatyā
vṛndāvana-rājyādhipatyaṃ kim āyāti ? kintu tatra cet mahā-pramāṇam asti, tad
vada |
body.translated_text: <s>Subala</s>: '<s>Lalitā</s>! As a neutral party, I must speak only the truth. Looking at your face, I cannot speak falsely. But how does his kingdom being <s>Bṛhadvana</s> give your good self sovereignty over the kingdom of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>? However, if there is great evidence for that, then state it.'

body.text:
lalitā - pratyakṣaṃ parokṣam api bahutara-purāṇa-vacana-kulam asti | tatrāpi
pratyakṣa-parokṣayoḥ pratyakṣam eva balīya ity anusāreṇa pratyakṣam eva
grāhyam |
body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s>: 'There is direct evidence and also indirect evidence in the form of numerous <s>Purāṇic</s> statements. Moreover, following the principle that between direct and indirect evidence, direct evidence is stronger, only the direct evidence should be accepted.'

body.text: nāndīmukhī - kiṃ tat pratyakṣaṃ pramāṇam ?
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>: 'What is that direct evidence?'

body.text: lalitā - mayā kiṃ tad vaktavyam ? yuṣmākam anubhūtam eva tat |
body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s>: 'Why should I state it? You yourselves have experienced it!'

body.text: nāndīmukhī - na smaryate | tat prakāśaya |
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>: 'I do not remember. So please reveal it.'

body.text:
lalitā - brahma-gṛhiṇī-sāvitrī-prabhṛti-devy-ādibhir
dundubhi-vāditrādi-kolāhala-pūrvakaṃ kṛto'tra mahā-siṃhāsane you ratnābhiṣekaḥ
sa ca trilokī-vāsiṣu kasya vā paramānanda-pradāyako na saṃvṛtto'sti |
body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s>: 'The jeweled coronation (<s>ratnābhiṣeka</s>) that was performed here upon the great throne by goddesses led by <s>Brahma</s>'s consort <s>Sāvitrī</s> and others, accompanied by the tumult of kettledrums and other instruments — to whom among the inhabitants of the three worlds did that not become a source of supreme bliss?'

body.text:
tataḥ subalaḥ - lalite! etat tu tāvad anyathātvena nirūpya priya-vayasyo yuṣmān apy
ātmasāt kartuṃ virājamāno vartate |
body.translated_text: Then <s>Subala</s>: '<s>Lalitā</s>! But this matter — by explaining it differently, my dear friend is poised to claim even all of you as his own.'

body.text:
lalitā - subala! etac ced bhavad-dvipada-gopa-priya-vayasyaḥ satyam eva vakti tarhi
vṛndāvana-rājye æbhiṣiktāyā mahā-siṃhāsana-sthāyā ity ādi tathaitasyāś
caraṇānujīvino mamety ādi vyāhṛtya svāmy asau sāmpratam api kathaṃ tac
caraṇa-paricaraṇa-mātraika-lābhāya tan-mantra-rājam ādātum
āgraheṇādhyavasyann astīty ādi sarvaṃ kiṃ bhavādṛgbhir vismṛtam ?
body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s>: '<s>Subala</s>! If your two-legged cowherd dear friend truly speaks the truth about this, then — having himself declared "she who was coronated in the kingdom of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, who is seated upon the great throne" and so forth, and "I am a servant living at her feet" and so forth — how is it that he now still persists with eagerness to receive the <s>mantra-rāja</s> for the sole gain of serving those very feet? Has all this been forgotten by the likes of you?'

body.text:
nāndīmukhī smitvā - lalite! asya vilāsino rāja-putrasya madana-modaka-bhojino
mahā-kāmukasya yat pralapitaṃ tat kim atra pramāṇaṃ syāt ? anyac ced gāḍhaṃ
pramāṇaṃ syād darśaya |
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>, smiling: '<s>Lalitā</s>! Whatever was prattled by this amorous prince, this eater of <s>madana-modaka</s> sweets, this great lover — how can that be evidence here? If there is other firm evidence, show it.'

body.text:
vṛndā - yad yat pramāṇam iyaṃ darśayati, tat tad evāsyonmādino rāja-putrasya
pakṣam āśritya yuvābhyāṃ khaṇḍyate | ato'nyat sarvatra prasiddham api pramāṇaṃ
lalitātikopena noṭṭaṅkayati |
body.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s>: 'Whatever evidence she presents, each and every one is refuted by you two by taking the side of this lovesick prince. Therefore, <s>Lalitā</s>, in her great anger, will not even stamp out the evidence that is famous everywhere else.'

body.text: nāndīmukhī - vṛnde! tat tvayaiva tāvat kathyatām |
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>: '<s>Vṛndā</s>! Then let you yourself state it.'

body.text:
vṛndā - premnā nijāsādhāraṇa-sārūpya-dāna-pūrvakam iyaṃ vṛndāṭavī
priya-sakhyā sva-priya-sakhītve nityaṃ nirūpitāstīti |
body.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s>: 'Out of love, by first bestowing her own unique likeness upon it, this <s>Vṛndā</s> forest has been forever established by her dear friend (<s>Rādhā</s>) in the role of her own dear companion.'

body.text: nāndīmukhī - kīdṛśaṃ svārūpyaṃ tat kathyatām |
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>: 'What is the nature of that likeness? Please describe it.'

body.text: vṛndā - śrūyatām -
body.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s>: 'Listen —'

children.translated_text: The radiance of her body — the moving <s>campaka</s>-creeper garlands, fragrant and luminous,
and the rows of golden <s>yūthī</s> jasmine that conquer the lightning-vine;
these bestowed their own supreme likeness upon the cowherd village (<s>Vraja</s>),
and of her face too — the multitude of most beautiful, rising lotuses. ||1||
Of her eyes — the assemblage of fresh, slightly rolling <s>kuvalaya</s> blue lotuses,
and likewise her playful movements — the deer maddened by sideways-glancing, coming and going;
the cluster of shining <s>bimbī</s> fruits, the mass of lovely full-bloomed <s>bandhūka</s> flowers too —
these are the good fortune of her pair of lips, dripping with nectar. ||2||
Of her arms — the gracefully swaying creepers and the flocks of parrots,
of her nose — the sesame blossoms, friends in radiance;
of her smile — the opening cluster of <s>kumuda</s> night-lotuses; of her beautiful teeth —
the <s>kunda</s> jasmine buds, whose fragrance intoxicates the bees, blinding them. ||3||
Of her eyebrows — the measured row of excellent bees, wandering in curved motions,
of her forehead — the supremely lovely splendor of gleaming, beautiful <s>baka</s> (crane) flowers;
of her braid — that array of peacock-crests, rising with intoxicated pride,
of her ears — the arrangement of <s>muñja</s> grass, stealing the luster of <s>Madana</s>'s bowstring. ||4||

children.text: alaṃ bilvaṃ tālaṃ karakam udayac cāru-kucayoḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>bilva</s> fruits, the <s>tāla</s> palm fruits, and the <s>karaka</s> fruits suffice for her beautiful pair of breasts,
of her radiant chest — the multitudes of golden thrones;
of these her hips, resounding with the ringing of fresh bells —
clearly, the vast and formidable great mountains adorned with the sound of bamboo flutes. ||5||
Of her beautiful pair of thighs, capable of the battle of <s>Smara</s> (love) — the juicy
plantain-trunk pillars that inaugurate splendor; of her feet — the clusters of land-lotuses;
of her gait, the teacher of walking lessons to elephants always rising in frenzy —
the graceful, playful, rising cleverness of the rows of swan-flocks. ||6||
Sufficient for a hundredfold are the rows of shining <s>jambū</s> fruits and <s>āmalaka</s> fruits,
in spring, the sweet calls made by young cuckoos — these belong to her beautiful speech;
of the sequence of her dance of glancing from the corners of her eyes on her serene, beautiful face —
the flock of <s>khañjana</s> wagtail birds dancing upon the blossoming lotus. ||7||
Of the flowing tears of love, the water-stream fallen from the collyrium of her eyes —
the <s>Yamunā</s> river and the <s>Gaṅgā</s> water of the heart, ever pure in consciousness;
and of her profuse perspiration — the various multitudes of lakes and ponds,
and of her great passion — the clusters of <s>guñjā</s> berries, beautiful in their rich color. ||8||
Of her bodily splendors that constantly generate excessive torment in the noses of co-wives,
and that at every moment create delight in the noses of her circle of friends,
of her bodily fragrances that pervade all the land of <s>Vraja</s> —
abundantly, the saffron of <s>Kāśmīra</s>, the interiors of <s>Vraja</s> lotuses, and excellent radiance. ||9||
Of Mount <s>Sumeru</s>'s splendors — the pride-subduing, haughty droplet-
sprays; of the beauty of lightning fashioned into worship — her bodily luster;
the radiant tracts of land, studded with gold, the multitudes of dwellings,
the interiors of caves and bowers, the mountain ranges and rocks here and there. ||10||
The lakes belong to her beautiful navel; the line of soft hair glistening above it —
the dark row of serpents, alas, of the enemy of <s>Vaka</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), who bears trembling;
of her generosity and other virtues — the wish-fulfilling trees, jewel-studded,
and of her <s>romāñca</s> (horripilation) — the mass of thick, tawny <s>kiñjalka</s> filaments of the <s>priyaka</s> tree. ||11||

children.text: pare ye muktāḥ syuḥ sthira-cara-padārthā vraja-bhuvaḥ
children.translated_text: All the remaining stationary and moving entities of the land of <s>Vraja</s>

children.text: sadā stavyā bhavyais trijagati nikāmaṃ jana-kulaiḥ |
children.translated_text: are ever to be praised by the worthy, pious people in the three worlds;
they belong to the multitude of the exquisite beauty of her noble limbs and sub-limbs — she who is beyond

children.text: rati-śrī-varṇyāyāḥ pariṣadi yathā yuktam api te ||12||
children.translated_text: the description of <s>Umā</s>, <s>Rati</s>, and <s>Śrī</s> — as befitting in the assembly, they are yours. ||12||
Even before the supreme sky overflowing with the self-delight of the Lord of <s>Ramā</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>),
the ever-blazing, expansive, joy-giving trees and creepers stand alone;
of <s>Śrī Rādhā</s>, whose majestic fame rises like the moon throughout the entire universe —
therefore, this forest is manifestly her dear companion. ||13||

body.text: tato'haṃ sāṭopam avadam -
body.translated_text: Then I said with haughtiness:

children.translated_text: In the sovereign kingdom of <s>Vrajendra</s>, by the rite of victorious appointment as crown-prince,
anointed, surrounded by the most intimate friends and others, motionless with affection,

children.text: nijām etāṃ rakṣāmy aṭavim iha gocāra-miṣataḥ
children.translated_text: I protect this forest of my own, here under the pretext of cow-grazing —

children.text: kathaṃ svārūpyeṇaiva tu bhavatu vaḥ sāmpratam iyam ||14||
children.translated_text: how then, merely by this likeness, can it now be yours? ||14||

body.text: tac chrutvā vṛndā -
body.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Vṛndā</s>:

children.text: sakhitvaṃ yo yasya vrajati nija-sārūpyam athavā
children.translated_text: One who goes to another as a friend gives one's own likeness, or else —

children.text: na cet tasya syān no bhavati param anyasya hi tadā |
children.translated_text: if that were not the case for that one, then it certainly does not exist for another either;

children.text: kathaṃ no gṛhṇāsi druta-gatir idaṃ hanta kathayan
children.translated_text: why then do you not grasp this, O swift one? Alas, I shall explain:

children.text: svayaṃ gatvā lakṣmīṃ tad inasamarūpaṃ gaṇam api ||15||
children.translated_text: having yourself gone to <s>Lakṣmī</s>, consider also that host of beings who share her form. ||15||

body.text:
tan niśamya sāṭṭa-hāsaṃ madhumaṅgalaḥ - bho asatya-vādini vṛnde!
kurcikā-lobhena nija-devītvam utsṛjya vandinī bhūtvā,
mithyā-stava-mātreṇaivāsmad-vṛndāṭavīṃ nija-sakhyāṃ sañcārayituṃ kathaṃ
śakṣyasi ?
body.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> said with a scornful laugh: 'O false-speaking <s>Vṛndā</s>! Out of greed for a comb, having abandoned your own status as goddess, you have become a panegyrist — how will you be able to transfer our <s>Vṛndā</s> forest into the friendship of your mistress by mere false praise alone?'

body.text:
nāndīmukhī - lalite! vijña-prācīna-munīśvara-vacanaṃ vinā ko'pi nirasto na
bhaviṣyati tasmāt purāṇa-vacanam eva darśaya |
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>: '<s>Lalitā</s>! Without the words of a learned ancient sage, no one will be refuted. Therefore, show <s>Purāṇic</s> evidence.'

body.text:
lalitā - asya pakṣam āśritya tādṛgbhir evaṃ cet kathyate tadā tatra gatvā
bhagavatyāḥ sakāśād bahūni purāṇa-vacanāni śrūyantām |
body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s>: 'If it is said thus by the likes of you, who have taken his side, then go there and hear the many <s>Purāṇic</s> statements from the venerable goddess (<s>Paurṇamāsī</s>) herself.'

body.text: subalaḥ - bhavatya eva paṭhantu |
body.translated_text: <s>Subala</s>: 'Let your good selves recite them.'

body.text:
lalitā - vallava-jātīnāṃ tatrāpi strīṇām asmākaṃ purāṇa-vacana-pāṭhe'dhikāra eva
nāsti |
body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s>: 'Those of the cowherd caste, and moreover women among them — we have no authority whatsoever to recite <s>Purāṇa</s> verses.'

body.text: subalaḥ - vṛndeyaṃ devī | tad iyam eva śrāvayatu |
body.translated_text: <s>Subala</s>: 'This <s>Vṛndā</s> is a goddess. So let her alone recite them.'

body.text:
vṛndā smṛtim abhinīya - atra subahūni vacanāni santi | tāni kati pāṭhyāni kintu
anyeṣu deśeṣu anyāḥ pṛthak pṛthag devīr adhikariṇīr uktvā rādhā vṛndāvane
vane iti sarvopamardakaṃ purāṇa-vacanaṃ bhagavatyāḥ sakāśāt kena vā na śrutam
asti |
