body.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s>, assuming the manner of one recalling scripture: 'There are very many such verses here. How many of them should be recited? However, setting aside those that speak of other goddesses as sovereign in other regions — who has not heard from the mouth of the Blessed Goddess herself the all-superseding <s>Purāṇa</s> verse: "<s>Rādhā</s> in <s>Vṛndāvana</s>'s forest"?'

body.text:
tatas tāsāṃ jayābhimānena praphullatām ālokya madhumaṅgalaḥ sāṭopam āha -
nāndīmukhi! sarva-purāṇa-śirasi mahopaniṣadi gopāla-tāpanyāṃ vṛndāvanasya
kṛṣṇa-vanatvena prathita-khyātyā vṛndāvana-rāja-dhānī-purandaratvena
priya-vayasyaṃ brahma-bhavādayo'pi nirantaraṃ gāyantaḥ santīti ke vā na jānanti
? tataḥ śrutyā smṛtir bādhyate ity asmākam evedaṃ rājyaṃ susiddham | tat sakhe
subala! vidāvayām ūritaḥ para-rājya-kāṅkṣiṇīḥ |
body.translated_text: Then, seeing them bloom with the pride of victory, <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> said grandly: '<s>Nāndīmukhī</s>! In the <s>Gopāla-tāpanī</s>, the great <s>Upaniṣad</s> that crowns all the <s>Purāṇas</s> — who does not know that <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, and the other gods ceaselessly sing of my dear friend as the sovereign lord of the capital city of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, which is celebrated as "<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s forest"? Therefore, since <s>Śruti</s> (revealed scripture) overrides <s>Smṛti</s> (traditional scripture), this kingdom is well-established as ours alone. So, friend <s>Subala</s>, let us drive out these covetous women who hanker after another's kingdom!'

body.text:
tataḥ sakhe tvam eva me priyaṅkaraḥ priya-vayasya iti sānandaṃ madhumaṅgalam
āliṅgati mayi kiñcid vailakṣyam iva rādhādhiṣṭhita-nikuñjam ālokya
lalitādi-mukham ālokayantyāṃ nāndīmukhyāṃ rādhā smitvā anuccaiḥ - aho
kṛṣṇeti śabda-śravaṇa-mātrata evānena mahā-dūra-darśinā tad-artham
abuddhvaiva para-rājye'smin sva-tātam arpayatā kiṃśuka-kusuma-sādṛśyena
durvidha-bodhasya rolambasya śuka-tuṇḍa-pāna-smaraṇaṃ suṣṭhu samānītāḥ
smaḥ |
body.translated_text: Then, as I joyfully embraced <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> [saying] 'Friend, you alone are my benefactor, dearest companion!' — while <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>, feeling somewhat embarrassed, looked toward the bower presided over by <s>Rādhā</s> and then at the faces of <s>Lalitā</s> and the others — <s>Rādhā</s>, smiling, [said] softly: 'Ah, merely upon hearing the word "<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>," this great far-sighted one, without even understanding its meaning, while surrendering his own father to another's kingdom — has most aptly reminded us of the parrot-beak drinking of <s>Rolamba</s>, that dullard who resembles a <s>kiṃśuka</s> (Flame-of-the-Forest) flower!'

body.text:
tatas tasminn eva varṇa-vinyāse solluṇṭhaṃ lalitayāpi prakāśite sati
kṛṣṇa-vana-śabdasyārthāntaraṃ nūnam eṣā ghaṭayiṣyatīti tad-abhiprāyaṃ manasi
manāk vicārayati mayi nāndīmukhī sacamatkāraṃ māṃ prāha - jayākāṅkṣin!
ekaṃ vijñāpayitum icchāmi yadi tubhyaṃ rocate |
body.translated_text: Then, when <s>Lalitā</s> too proclaimed that very analysis of letters with a mischievous air — as I considered slightly in my mind her intent, [thinking] 'surely she will construct an alternative meaning of the word <s>kṛṣṇa-vana</s>' — <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>, with wonder, said to me: 'O you who desire victory! I wish to make one representation, if it pleases you.'

body.text: tato'haṃ - kāmaṃ kathyatām |
body.translated_text: Then I [said]: 'By all means, speak.'

body.text:
nāndīmukhī - śyāma-vana-samāsam ācarya tvayā saha tat-samāsenaiva nyāyam
ācarya tvāṃ parājitya svarājyam ādātuṃ laliteyam abhilaṣati |
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>: 'By applying the compound "<s>śyāma-vana</s>" (dark forest), this <s>Lalitā</s> desires to defeat you through reasoning by that very compound, and thus seize sovereignty for herself.'

body.text:
tato'haṃ - vividha-kusuma-candana-varṇikādibhiḥ śṛṅgāra-racanācāryeyam | tad eva
jānāti yad anayā tad-vana-puṣpair muhuḥ śṛṅgārito'smi | tad vyākaraṇasya keyam
?
body.translated_text: Then I [said]: 'She is an expert in the art of adornment with various flowers, sandal-paste, face-painting, and such. That alone she knows — for she has repeatedly adorned me with the flowers of that very forest. But what does she know of grammar?'

body.text:
vṛndā smitvā - vyākaraṇa-vijñaṃ-manya! tvatto'pi mat-priya-sakhī lalitā
tad-vyākaraṇasya prathitācāryā |
lalitā - pāmari vṛnde! apehi apehi |
body.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s>, smiling: 'O you who fancy yourself learned in grammar! My dear friend <s>Lalitā</s> is a more renowned master of that very grammar than even you!' <s>Lalitā</s>: 'Wicked <s>Vṛndā</s>! Away, away with you!'

body.text: vṛndā - tvat-pakṣam āśritya vivadamānāṃ māṃ kim ity ākṣipasi ?
body.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s>: 'Why do you reproach me, when I am arguing on your side?'

body.text:
lalitā - bhoḥ samāsācārya-śārdūla! kathaṃ svepsitāpara-samāsena vibhīṣikāṃ
pradarśya mat-priya-sakhyāḥ khelāspada-kṛṣṇa-vanam idam ādātuṃ
vṛthaivādhyavasyasi | yato'tra nityaṃ vaiśvānaravaj
jājjvalyamāna-bahuvrīhi-karmadhārayādy-avadhāraṇataḥ svayam eva dūrād
evāpasariṣyasi | [samāsābhijña kṛṣṇa-vana-śabdasya narma-cchalena
tat-puruṣa-samāsaṃ viracayya para-rājyaṃ grahītuṃ katham abhilaṣasi | yad atra
karmadhāraya-bahuvrīhi-samāsayor evāvakāśaḥ |]
body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s>: 'O tiger among compound-masters! How do you vainly persist in trying to seize this <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>-forest, the playground of my dear friend, by brandishing the specter of a compound favorable to yourself? For here, by the determination of <s>bahuvrīhi</s>, <s>karmadhāraya</s>, and other [compounds] that blaze eternally like <s>Vaiśvānara</s> (the universal fire), you yourself will retreat far away! [O knower of compounds! How can you desire to seize another's kingdom by constructing a <s>tatpuruṣa</s> compound of the word <s>kṛṣṇa-vana</s> under the pretext of wordplay? For here only <s>karmadhāraya</s> and <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compounds have scope.]'

body.text:
tato mayoktaṃ - caturaṃmanye! prakaṭe'tra tat-puruṣa-samāse kathaṃ
karamadhārayādi-yojanā sambhavati | bhavatu bhavatu durjana iti nyāyena tad eva
tāvat kathaya śrotavyam |
body.translated_text: Then I said: 'O you who think yourself clever! When the <s>tatpuruṣa</s> compound is evident here, how can a <s>karmadhāraya</s> or other construction be possible? Very well, very well — as the maxim goes, "let the rascal speak" — so tell us that much at least; it shall be worth hearing.'

body.text:
rādhā anuccaiḥ - vanasyāsya ghanatā-prācaryeṇa kṛṣṇaṃ śyāmaṃ ca tad-vanaṃ ceti
karmadhārayaḥ sphuta eva |
body.translated_text: <s>Rādhā</s>, softly: 'Because of the predominant darkness of this forest, it is dark (<s>kṛṣṇa</s>), and it is a forest (<s>vana</s>) — thus the <s>karmadhāraya</s> (appositional compound) is plainly evident.'

body.text:
ity evaṃ lalitayāpi sphuṭaṃ bhāṣite campakalatā sa-ślāgham āha - lalite! sādhu
sādhu satyaṃ satyaṃ yataḥ karmāṇi
ariṣṭa-keśyādi-vadha-kāliya-damana-govardhanoddharaṇa-nitya-rāsādi-līlā
dhārayati niṣpādayati prakāśayati vā ity asya vanasya karmadhārayatvaṃ sphuṭam
eva prasiddham |
body.translated_text: When <s>Lalitā</s> too spoke this clearly, <s>Campakalatā</s> said admiringly: '<s>Lalitā</s>! Well said, well said! True, true! For this forest bears (<s>dhārayati</s>), accomplishes (<s>niṣpādayati</s>), and manifests (<s>prakāśayati</s>) deeds (<s>karmāṇi</s>) — namely the pastimes of slaying <s>Ariṣṭa</s> and <s>Keśī</s>, subduing <s>Kāliya</s>, lifting <s>Govardhana</s>, the eternal <s>rāsa</s>-dance, and others — thus the <s>karmadhāraya</s> nature of this forest is plainly well-established!'

body.text:
punar lalitā rādhānucca-bhāṣitam evānuvadati - kṛṣṇāni kvacid kvacid atiśyāmāni
vanāni yatra tat kṛṣṇa-vanam iti vṛndāvanasya viśeṣaṇatvena bahuvrīhir api |
body.translated_text: Again, <s>Lalitā</s> repeats what <s>Rādhā</s> spoke softly: 'In places where the groves are dark (<s>kṛṣṇa</s>) — exceedingly dark — that is <s>Kṛṣṇa-vana</s>; thus, as a qualifier of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> (possessive compound) also [applies].'

body.text:
vṛndā -- satyaṃ satyaṃ kālindī-tīra-rāsa-sthalyām andhakāri-baṭa-vanaṃ, tathā
govardhanopaśalya-para-rāsa-sthalyām andhakāri-niviḍa-vanaṃ sarvānanda-karaṃ
suprasiddham eva |
body.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s>: 'True, true! The dark banyan grove at the <s>rāsa</s>-ground on the bank of the <s>Kālindī</s>, and likewise the dense, dark forest at the supreme <s>rāsa</s>-ground at the foot of <s>Govardhana</s> — [these are] the delight of all, supremely well-known!'

body.text:
indulekhā - lalite! satyaṃ satyaṃ bahavo brīhayo dhānyādi-śasyāni kiṃ vā
kedārikā-jātatvān muktā eva brīhayaḥ | bahavo brīhayo yasmin nityasya vanasya
bahuvrīhatvaṃ sphuṭam eva |
body.translated_text: <s>Indulekhā</s>: '<s>Lalitā</s>! True, true! Many <s>brīhi</s> (rice-plants) — meaning grains and other crops — or rather, since they grow in <s>kedārikā</s> (paddy-fields), they are verily unhusked rice (<s>brīhi</s>). "That in which there are many <s>brīhi</s>" — thus the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> nature of this eternal forest is plainly evident!'

body.text:
tataḥ sa-garva-garbhitaṃ hasantīṣu tāsu mayoktaṃ -
nānā-kuṭa-kalpanā-nagarī-cakravartini lalite! mukham atra tat-puruṣa-samāsaṃ
kalpita-karmadhāraya-bahuvrīhibhyāṃ kathaṃ davayituṃ śakyase |
body.translated_text: Then, as they laughed with concealed pride, I said: 'O <s>Lalitā</s>, empress of the city of manifold deceptive inventions! How can you devour the principal <s>tatpuruṣa</s> compound here with your fabricated <s>karmadhāraya</s> and <s>bahuvrīhi</s>?'

body.text:
lalitā - mahā-paṇḍita! tat-puruṣas tatpuruṣa iti bāraṃ bāraṃ jalpasi | tatpuruṣas
tāvad aneka-vidho bhavati | tatra katamo'yaṃ sa iti suṣṭhu nirṇīya kathyatām |
body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s>: 'O great scholar! You babble "<s>tatpuruṣa</s>, <s>tatpuruṣa</s>" again and again! A <s>tatpuruṣa</s> is of many kinds. So determine well which one of those this is, and then speak!'

body.text:
mayoktaṃ - jaḍa-buddhike! kṛṣṇasya vanaṃ kṛṣṇa-vanam iti ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas
trijagati suprasiddha eva |
body.translated_text: I said: 'O dull-witted one! "The forest of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>" — <s>Kṛṣṇa-vana</s> — this is a <s>ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa</s> (genitive <s>tatpuruṣa</s>), supremely well-known in all three worlds!'

body.text:
rādhā - kṛṣṇasya vanam iti cet tarhi sakhīsthalī-baṭa-śreṇir eva puruṣa-śārdūlasya
tava vanam | yataḥ ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣo'pi nityaṃ tatraiva vartate |
body.translated_text: <s>Rādhā</s>: 'If it is "the forest of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>," then that row of banyan trees at <s>Sakhīsthalī</s> is the forest of you, O tiger among men! For the <s>ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa</s> (the sixth one's husband) always resides right there.'

body.text:
atra ṣaṣṭhī-samāsasya sambhāvanāpi na vidyate ity evaṃ vihasya lalitayāpy ukte
nāndīmukhī - lalite! eṣa te vāg-vinyāso garbhita-sandarbha iti lakṣyate tat
prakāśya kathyatām |
body.translated_text: When <s>Lalitā</s> too said with laughter, 'There is not even the possibility of a <s>ṣaṣṭhī</s> (sixth-case) compound here!' — <s>Nāndīmukhī</s> [said]: '<s>Lalitā</s>! This verbal arrangement of yours appears to contain a hidden allusion. So make it clear and explain!'

body.text:
tato lalitā netrānta-nīlotpala-mālayā mām akurvatī smita-garbhitam āha -
nāndīmukhi! ṣaṣṭhī kācid ekā | tasyāḥ puruṣaḥ patir eva jano vā
ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: Then <s>Lalitā</s>, casting upon me a garland of sidelong blue-lotus glances, said with a concealed smile: '<s>Nāndīmukhī</s>! There is a certain <s>ṣaṣṭhī</s> ("sixth one"). Her <s>puruṣa</s> — that is, her husband or her man — is the <s>ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa</s> ("the man of the sixth").'

body.text: viśākhā sa-smitaṃ - lalite! tat-puruṣo jñāta eva | sā tāvat kā ?
body.translated_text: <s>Viśākhā</s>, with a smile: '<s>Lalitā</s>! The <s>puruṣa</s> (man) of that one is already known. But who then is she?'

body.text: lalitā - candrāvalī |
body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s>: '<s>Candrāvalī</s>.'

body.text: viśākhā - candrāvalī kathaṃ ṣaṣṭhī ?
body.translated_text: <s>Viśākhā</s>: 'How is <s>Candrāvalī</s> the <s>ṣaṣṭhī</s> ("the sixth")?'

body.text:
lalitā - devī-gaṇa-madhye prathamaḥ kaṃsa-gopo govardhana-mallo
mahā-bhairavaḥ | dvitīyā tan-mātā bhāruṇḍā caṇḍī, tṛtīyā candrāvalī-mātā
mahī-karālā carcikā | caturthī śaivyā kālī | pañcamī padmā śaṅkhinī prasiddhā |
ṣaṣṭhī sakhīsthalī-baṭa-vāsinī candrāvalī ṣaṣṭhī | yato baṭa-vana-vāsitvāt
tasyāḥ ṣaṣṭhītvaṃ yuktam eva |
body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s>: 'Among the group of goddesses — the first is <s>Kaṃsa</s>-<s>Gopa</s>, the <s>Govardhana</s>-wrestler, the great <s>Bhairava</s>; the second is his mother <s>Bhāruṇḍā</s>, the fierce <s>Caṇḍī</s>; the third is <s>Candrāvalī</s>'s mother <s>Mahī-karālā</s>, the terrible <s>Carcikā</s>; the fourth is <s>Śaivyā</s>, the dark <s>Kālī</s>; the fifth is <s>Padmā</s>, the well-known <s>Śaṅkhinī</s>; and the sixth, dwelling at the banyan tree of <s>Sakhīsthalī</s>, is <s>Candrāvalī</s> — the <s>ṣaṣṭhī</s> ("the sixth"). Since she resides in the banyan grove, her identity as <s>ṣaṣṭhī</s> ("the sixth goddess") is perfectly fitting.'

body.text:
tataḥ sarveṣāṃ hāsa-kolāhala-vṛtte ahaṃ svagataṃ - aho buddher variṣṭhatā
vraja-bālānāṃ, yad aham api vacanāṭopa-vilāsair nirvacanīkṛto'smi | prakāśaṃ
sa-nirvedam ivāhaṃ - nāndīmukhi! asmad-datta-bhoga-rāga-masṛṇa-vasanādibhiḥ
saṃvardhitābhir
asmad-datta-muktā-maṇi-pravāla-kamala-rāga-marakata-vajrādi-khacita-vividha-
bhūṣaṇa-bhūṣitābhiḥ sāmpratam
abhinava-yauvana-mahādhana-garveṇojjhita-guru-laghu-gaṇanotkarābhir
asmat-kṛṣaka-gujjara-gajjarībhir apy etābhir
helollāsita-cañcala-nayana-prānta-nartana-pūrvakaṃ
sāhaṅkṛti-vacanāḍambara-vinyāsa-bhareṇa samasta-vraja-sāmrājya-sārvabhaumasya
paramoddaṇḍa-kumāro'ham api niravadhi-viḍambyamāno'pi kevalaṃ
bhagavatī-caraṇa-parijana-mukhya-nāndīmukhī-mukham ālokya
tathaika-grāma-vāsenāpakīrti-bhayena ca etat-kṛtaṃ pratīpa-vyavasitam api
etāvantaṃ kālaṃ duḥkhadatvenāpi na gaṇitavān asmi |
body.translated_text: Then, amid a tumult of laughter from everyone, I [thought] to myself: 'Ah, how supreme is the wit of the young women of <s>Vraja</s>, that even I have been rendered speechless by the splendor of their verbal play!' Aloud, as if with dejection, I [said]: '<s>Nāndīmukhī</s>! Nourished by the enjoyment-softened garments and other [gifts] bestowed by us, adorned with various ornaments studded with pearls, gems, coral, rubies, emeralds, diamonds, and other [jewels] given by us — and now, by the pride of their fresh youth and great beauty, having cast off the reckoning of heavy and light syllables — even by these cowherd and <s>Gujjar</s> women of ours, with the preliminary dance of their mischievously darting, playful, restless sidelong glances, and with the weight of their ostentatious verbal display full of pride — though I, the supremely mighty prince, the universal emperor of all <s>Vraja</s>, am being endlessly mocked — merely by looking upon the face of <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>, the chief attendant of the Blessed Goddess's feet, and out of fear of ill-repute from dwelling in the same village, I have not counted even this contrary disposition, though it causes me pain, for all this time.'

body.text:
sāmprataṃ mama doṣo na deyaḥ | adhunaiva nija-nija-vakṣasi
masṛṇa-mecaka-paṭa-pariveṣṭitam ativicitrita-kārtasvara-sampūṭa-yuga-puṭitam
aruṇa-dvitīyā-śaśadhara-mudrā-mudritaṃ sva-sva-parivṛḍher api kadāpy
anālokita-caraṃ durlabha-nava-tāruṇya-dhanaṃ mahā-tīvra-nakha-bhañais tathaiva
nirupama-daśana-cchada-padmarāga-mahā-ratnam api daśanoddhara-sāmantair api
luṇṭhayitvā etā vacana-dhana-daridrā vidadhāno'smi |
body.translated_text: 'Now the fault should not be attributed to me. Right this moment, upon each of their own chests — wrapped in smooth dark cloth, enclosed in pairs of most elaborately decorated golden caskets, sealed with the crescent-moon seal of the second-day moon, the rare treasure of new youth never glimpsed even by their own retinues — as well as the incomparable great ruby gem of their lip-petals — I shall plunder them with attacks of my nail-soldiers and even through their tooth-generals, and render these ones destitute of verbal wealth!'

body.text:
iti sāṭopaṃ sahasopasṛtya tāḥ sandidhīrṣau mayi
kuṭila-bhrū-nartana-valita-smita-śavalita-kaṭākṣeṇa mad-avalokana-pūrvakam itas
tato manāg apasarpantīṣu sarvāsu, sa-roṣam iva lalitā - aye śyāmala
rasa-pāna-nirata! apehi apehi | etāṃ te matta-tāra-bhaṭīṃ vrajeśvaryai varṇayituṃ
vayaṃ calitāḥ smaḥ |
body.translated_text: Thus declaring with pride, as I suddenly rushed toward them intent on seizing them, all of them — casting sidelong glances adorned with dancing curved eyebrows and dappled with smiles, looking at me — began slipping away slightly here and there. <s>Lalitā</s>, as if with anger: 'O dark one, absorbed in drinking <s>rasa</s>! Away! Away! We have set out to report this intoxicated star-commanding behavior of yours to the queen of <s>Vraja</s>.'

body.text: satyabhāmā sa-camatkāraṃ hasantī - vinodin! ekaṃ praṣṭum icchāmi |
body.translated_text: <s>Satyabhāmā</s>, laughing with wonder: 'O playful one! I wish to ask one thing.'

body.text: kṛṣṇaḥ - priye! vijñāpaya |
body.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>: 'Beloved! Ask.'

body.text: satyabhāmā - rādhā-svagata-lapitāvalir eva lalitādibhir api katham anvavādi ?
body.translated_text: <s>Satyabhāmā</s>: 'How did <s>Lalitā</s> and the others also echo <s>Rādhā</s>'s inner soliloquy?'

body.text:
kṛṣṇaḥ - priye! rādhāyāḥ kāya-vyūha-rūpā eva lalitādayas tat kathaṃ
nādhigamiṣyanti ?
body.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>: 'Beloved! <s>Lalitā</s> and the others are emanated forms (<s>kāya-vyūha</s>) of <s>Rādhā</s> herself — so how would they not comprehend?'

body.text:
satyabhāmā - subhaga! rādhāyā narmottara-varṇa-vinyāsaḥ kathaṃ vā
bhavan-mānasa-sañcārī babhūva ?
body.translated_text: <s>Satyabhāmā</s>: 'O handsome one! How did <s>Rādhā</s>'s witty arrangement of words in reply to the jest come to travel within your mind?'

body.text:
madhumaṅgala sa-gadgadaṃ - priyasakhi satye!
parimala-mañjarī-mañjula-mṛgamadāv iva paraspara-saṃpṛktau
gāndharvā-giridhāriṇau tat kathaṃ na sañcaratv iti |
body.translated_text: <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>, with a choked voice: 'Dear friend <s>Satyā</s>! Like fragrance and the lovely musk-flower — mutually intermingled — so are <s>Gāndharvā</s> and the Mountain-lifter. So how would they not move in each other's minds?'

body.text:
iti
tad-vacana-niśamana-madhura-payaḥ-pāna-parivardhita-gāndharvā-virahotkaṭa-
kaṭu-garalodbhaṭa-vikaṭa-jvālā-jāla-janitābhiḥ | punaḥ punaś
cālyamāna-hṛdaya-marma-nimagnārdha-bhagna-pratapta-lauha-tiryag-avaśalyojjṛ
mbhita-yātanā-bharato'pi mahā-tīvra-pīḍāvalībhir abhito'vanta-nirbhara-kātaro
yadā babhūva tadaiva tad-avadhānataḥ
sañcarad-apūrva-jāḍya-mohonmādādi-priya-sahacara-samudaya-sahita-sūddīptata
ma-stambha-kampādy-aṣṭa-sāttvika-priya-vayasyeṣu bāḍham ahaṃ pūrvakaṃ ahaṃ
pūrvaka-kṣelana-vidhinā narmocchalita-paraspara-vijayāya pragāḍha-prāgalbhyam
upalabhya yugapat tvaritam upary upari tam āliṅgituṃ sarvataḥ sarabhasam
ārabhamāneṣu - re re vidagdha-śiromaṇiṃ-manyāḥ! khelana-samayam uttamaṃ
labdhāḥ stha ity upālabhya śrīmat-premānirvacanīya-pariṇāma-viśeṣa-svarūpeṇa
niravadya-hṛdya-sauhṛdyācintya-mahima-mahauṣadha-rasāti-vaśīkṛta-sapriya-par
ijana-gaṇa-kṛṣṇaika-sarvasva-rūpeṇa
samastātarkya-mahā-mahā-prabhāva-bahuvidha-līlādi-śakty-apaṇa-cintā-ratnādi
-ratna-viñcholīka-maṅgalākareṇa
nirupama-vividha-vaidagdhya-cāturya-samayādi-vijñatva-sugandha-kusumotkarān
irbharārāmeṇa śrī-śrī-rasa-nāma-prāṇa-priyatama-narma-sakhena
sa-bhrū-bhaṅgaṃ nayana-ghūrṇana-līlayā vihita-pratiṣedhāt svayam api ca paścād
avadhāya | bho bhoḥ! anāyyam anāyyam iti rasajñāṃ daśanaiḥ saṃdaśya laghu laghu
sa-saṅkocaṃ sva-pṛṣṭena dūram apasaratsu teṣu - tato'sphuṭa-bahir-vikāra-nikaraḥ
sambhṛta-hṛt-kampātiśayaḥ sa śrī-śrīmān yādavendraḥ svagatam idaṃ vilalāpa -
hā mat-prāṇa-kapota-vāsa-baḍabhi-prema-sphuran-mādhurī-dhārāpāra-sarid-vare!
guṇa-kalā-narma-prahelīkhane! hā man-netra-cakora-poṣaka-vibdhu-jyotsnā-tate
rādhike! hā hā mad-duritena kena nidhivat prāptā karāt tvaṃ cyutā ?
body.translated_text: Then, from hearing those words — sweet as drinking milk — the fierce, acrid, blazing poison-net of the terrible anguish of separation from <s>Gāndharvā</s> that had been nourished within; again and again, the half-broken red-hot iron bolt plunging into the depths of his heart's marrow, stirring agonizing pain — when he was thoroughly overwhelmed on all sides with unrelenting distress from the supremely sharp pangs — at that very moment, from his state of attention, the unprecedented companions of torpor, bewilderment, and madness moved about, and together with the eight <s>sāttvika</s> (pure emotional) companions of fierce horripilation, trembling, and the rest, fully blazing — having perceived the excellent opportunity for mutual triumph through the prior game, they all simultaneously rushed upon him in haste from every side to embrace him. 'Hey, hey! You who fancy yourselves the crest-jewels of cleverness! You have found a fine time for sport!' — having thus reproached them, through the special transformation of the indescribable beauty of sacred <s>prema</s> (divine love), in the form of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> who is the sole all-in-all together with his dear attendant-group, subjugated by the supreme medicinal essence of the inconceivable glory of faultless, heart-touching friendship, the repository of wish-fulfilling gems of the manifold powers of sports and the like of various inconceivable great magnificence, the garden overflowing with fragrant flowers of unmatched cleverness, ingenuity, timeliness, and expertise — by his most dear intimate jesting-friend named <s>Śrī Śrī Rasa</s>, having prohibited them with a frown and the play of rolling eyes — and he himself too observing afterward — 'Ho! Ho! Improper! Improper!' — biting the connoisseur's tongue with his teeth — as they quickly withdrew backward with embarrassment, retreating far — then he, with his outward emotional symptoms obscured, with intensified trembling collected within his heart, that most blessed lord of the <s>Yādavas</s>, spoke this soliloquy to himself: 'Alas! O supreme river beyond the shore of the stream of brilliant sweetness of love, which is the submarine-fire-abode of my life-dove! O tablet of puzzles of virtues, arts, and jests! Alas! O bank of moonlight that nourishes the <s>cakora</s> bird of my eyes, O <s>Rādhike</s>! Alas! Alas! By what sin of mine were you, found like a treasure, lost from my hand?'

body.text:
tataḥ satyabhāmā - yādavendra! śrīman-mukhāravindād
gokula-vilāsa-mādhurī-makarandaṃ dhayantyā api mama pipāsā param ullālasīti |
tat-kṛpayā tad eva punaḥ pāyaya |
body.translated_text: Then <s>Satyabhāmā</s>: 'O lord of the <s>Yādavas</s>! Though I drink the nectar of <s>Gokula</s>'s playful sweetness from your blessed lotus-mouth, my thirst only surges more. So please, mercifully give me that again to drink.'

body.text: kṛṣṇaḥ - priye śrūyatām |
body.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>: 'Beloved, listen.'

body.text:
tato madhumaṅgalenoktaṃ - sakhi lalite! priya-sakhasyāham
alaṅghya-vākya-sacivo'smi | tad apūrvaṃ kam apy utkocaṃ mahyaṃ dehi | mayā
mauktika-mūlyena vaḥ sācivyaṃ vidhāsyate |
body.translated_text: 'Then <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> said: "Friend <s>Lalitā</s>! I am the minister whose word cannot be transgressed by my dear friend. So give me some unprecedented bribe. I shall conduct ministerial service for you in the matter of the pearl-price."'

body.text:
viśākhā - ārya! kim apy atra nāsti | sāyaṃ sa-krośanārthaṃ tubhyaṃ
varāṭikā-catuṣṭayam avaśyaṃ deyam | yadi pratītir na kriyate tvayā nāndīmukhī
pratibhūr gṛhyatām |
body.translated_text: <s>Viśākhā</s>: 'Sir! There is nothing here for that. In the evening, four cowrie-shells will certainly be given to you for crying over. If you have no trust, let <s>Nāndīmukhī</s> be taken as guarantor.'

body.text:
madhumaṅgalaḥ sa-krodhaṃ - avadya-bhāṣiṇi ābhīrike! tiṣṭha tiṣṭha | eṣo'haṃ
sadya eva tavaitat prāyaścittaṃ kārayann asi iti nigadya māṃ pratyuvāca -
priya-vayasya! bhavan-mṛdula-vacana-druta-ghṛta-dhārayā
saṃvardhita-garva-vaiśvānarābhir amūbhiḥ suṣṭhu bhavantam upālabhya mām api
baddhā netuṃ vyavasīyate |
body.translated_text: <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>, angrily: 'O speaker of improper words! O coward! Stay, stay! I am about to make you perform this very expiation right now!' Saying this, he addressed me: 'Dear friend! These women, whose fire of pride has been nourished by the stream of melted ghee of your soft words, are thoroughly reproaching you, and they have also resolved to bind me and lead me away.'

body.text:
tato'haṃ - sakhe! satyaṃ satyaṃ yathā vinā rājadhānī-jayena tad-deśāḥ suṣṭhu vaśā
na bhavanti | tathaitad yūtheśā parābhavam antareṇa tadīyāḥ katham amūr amūkā
na bhavantu | iti nigadya rādhā-sanāthaṃ kuñjaṃ paśyan sa-nirvedaṃ punar avadaṃ -
 kiṃ kartavyaṃ sā kilaitad bhayenaiva mat-sānnidhyaṃ nāsāditavatī iti niśamya
drutam udgrīvikāvalokanāt saṅkucantī rādhā kuñja-madhye niviṣṭaḥ babhūva |
body.translated_text: Then I: 'Friend! Truly, truly — just as without conquering the capital, the territories of that country cannot be properly subdued, so too without the defeat of this herd-leader, how can these subordinates of hers not remain defiant?' Saying this, looking at the bower graced by <s>Rādhā</s>'s presence, I spoke again with regret: 'What is to be done? For she reportedly has not approached my presence precisely out of this fear.' Hearing this, <s>Rādhā</s>, quickly shrinking from the eager upward gaze, entered the interior of the bower.

body.text: satyabhāmā - tatas tataḥ ?
body.translated_text: <s>Satyabhāmā</s>: 'Then what? Then what?'

body.text:
kṛṣṇaḥ - tato'haṃ - nāndīmukhi! lalitādīnāṃ tāruṇya-dhanād api tasyās
tāruṇya-dhanaṃ pracurataram amūlyam apīti jñāyatām |
body.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>: 'Then I said: "O <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>! Let it be known that even compared to the youth-treasure of <s>Lalitā</s> and the others, her youth-treasure is far more abundant and priceless."'

body.text: nāndīmukhī - katham iva ?
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>: 'How so?'

body.text:
mayoktaṃ - yata āsāṃ tāvat sampūṭa-dvaya-parimitaṃ tat tasyās tu
mahā-mataṅgaja-kumbhato'pi nistalatvenonnatatvena pariṇāhena ca pravīṇatare
hṛn-madhyasthe gokula-prasiddha-taskara-bhītyeva mṛgamada-paṅkādi-lepena
varṇāntaram āpite hiraṇmaya-kumbha-yugale paripūrṇaṃ tat |
body.translated_text: I said: 'Because theirs is limited to a pair of caskets, but hers — surpassing even the great elephant's frontal globes in smoothness, height, and girth — is fully contained in a pair of golden pots placed at the center of her heart, which have been painted a different color with musk-paste and the like out of the well-known fear of the famous thief of <s>Gokula</s>.'

body.text:
nāndīmukhī - mohana! atisuguptam etad dhanaṃ kadāpi bhavad-dṛṣṭa-caraṃ
vṛttam asti |
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>: 'O enchanter! Has this most closely guarded treasure ever come within your sight?'

body.text: tato'haṃ sa-smitaṃ - nāndīmukhi! vidyuc-camatkṛtim iva sakṛd īkṣitam asti |
body.translated_text: Then I, with a smile: 'O <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>! Like the flash of lightning — glimpsed just once.'

body.text: nāndīmukhī - kadā ?
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>: 'When?'

body.text:
mayoktaṃ - ekasminn avasare nija-sarovara-snānād uttīrya nija-madhurāṅgataś
cīnāṃśukena rahasi tayā niḥsāryamāṇe payasi sumanoharaṇāya daivāt
tatraivāgatena mayā manāg evāvalokitaṃ tat tataḥ sā sabhayam iva sahasaiva
śyāmala-śāṭikāñcalenāvṛtavatī | samprati mad-bhāgya-vaśād yadi kutrāpi
yauvana-dhana-garvitā sāsmad-rājyābhilāṣiṇī mac-cakṣuṣor aparokṣībhavet tadā
nakha-daśana-bhaṭa-sāmantān antareṇāpi chāyā-dvitīyena mayā
kara-kamala-yugenaiva tat-kumbha-dvayam āloḍya tāruṇya-dhanānya ātma-sātkṛtya
sādhvasa-labdha-kampa-pulakāyāṃ tasyāṃ yūtha-nāthāyāṃ nirvacanī-kṛtāyāṃ
tad-amātya-ghaṭeyaṃ mahā-vaikulyena sva-sva-tāruṇya-dhanaṃ gṛhītvā palāyitum
api suṣṭhu-sthānam api nāpsyati kiṃ vā tad-dhana-samarpaṇa-pūrvakaṃ
śuddha-bhāvena mām eva paricariṣyati | tad atikṣudrābhir ābhiḥ
sva-mahimonnāha-glāni-kāriṇā vākovākena kim ?
body.translated_text: I said: 'On one occasion, when she had risen from bathing in her own lake and was privately wringing the water from her body with a Chinese silk cloth, I, having come there by chance to steal flowers, caught a momentary glimpse. Thereupon she fearfully and suddenly covered herself with the edge of her dark garment. Now, if by the fortune of my fate, she — proud of her youth-treasure and desirous of my kingdom — were to appear before my eyes somewhere, then without even the soldier-generals of nails and teeth, with my pair of lotus-hands alone, accompanied only by my shadow, I would churn that pair of pots, make her youth-treasures my own, and with her — the herd-leader, rendered speechless, trembling and horripilating with trepidation — this retinue-assembly of her ministers, in great confusion, taking up their own youth-treasures, would not even find a proper place to flee. Or rather, having offered up their treasures beforehand, they would serve me alone with pure devotion. So what is the use of this word-sparring with these utterly petty ones, which only diminishes the glory of my own grandeur?'

body.text:
tataḥ kiñcit smitvā nāndīmukhīṃ prati rādhā anuccaiḥ prāha - ayi
capala-brahmacāriṇi! apehi apehi |
body.translated_text: Then, smiling slightly, <s>Rādhā</s> said softly to <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>: 'O fickle celibate! Away! Away!'

body.text:
viśākhā - aho uḍḍīya calitum aśakyasya bimbīmātraika-bhojino bubhukṣitasya
lolubha-śukasya manasi durlabha-madhura-drākṣā-bhakṣaṇam etat |
body.translated_text: <s>Viśākhā</s>: 'Ah! This is the dream of eating rare sweet grapes in the mind of a hungry, greedy parrot who can only eat <s>bimba</s>-fruits and is unable to fly away.'

body.text:
madhumaṅgalaḥ - priya-vayasya! mad-abhīṣṭa-pāritoṣikaṃ dehi dhruvam
adhunaiva bhavad-rājyābhilāṣiṇīṃ rādhāṃ tāṃ bhavat-kara-gatāṃ vidhāsye |
tato'ham - sāyaṃ miṣṭānna-bhojanaṃ dāsye |
body.translated_text: <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>: 'Dear friend! Give me my desired reward — I shall surely right now bring that <s>Rādhā</s>, the one who desires your kingdom, into your hands.' Then I: 'I shall give you sweet food in the evening.'

body.text:
madhumaṅgalaḥ - māthura-rāja-pārśve phutkṛtya tad-aśvārūḍhānāṃ śatam ānīya
pṛṣṭha-deśe carma-rajjvā kaphoṇi-dvaya-bandha-pūrvakaṃ kaśābhis tat-patir
abhimanyus tathā tāḍayitavyaḥ yathā sa eva tām ānīya dadāti |
body.translated_text: <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> — Having rushed to the side of the <s>Māthura</s> king, bringing a hundred of his mounted horsemen, with both elbows bound behind his back with a leather rope, that master <s>Abhimanyu</s> should be whipped in such a manner that he himself brings her and hands her over.

body.text: tataḥ sarve smayayanti sma |
body.translated_text: Then everyone smiled.

body.text: lalitā - viśākhe! kam api mahābhāgam uddiśya yat kiñcin nivedayāmi tat śṛṇu |
body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s> — <s>Viśākhe</s>! Addressing a certain most fortunate one, I wish to submit something — please listen.

body.text: viśākhā - kathyatām |
body.translated_text: <s>Viśākhā</s> — Speak.

body.text:
tataḥ kadamba-bhūruhāgram abhivīkṣya lalitā - bho vṛndāvana-cara-tapasvi-vara!
tvaṃ tāvat phalāhārī khyātas tat-sva-maryādhām ullaṅghya
bhavad-ayogya-parama-durlabha-sādhvī-hṛdayaṅgama-mahā-dhane lālasām
udvahan kathaṃ kaluṣito bhavann asi ?
body.translated_text: Then, gazing up at the top of a <s>kadamba</s> tree, <s>Lalitā</s> said — O best of wandering ascetics of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>! You are known as one who subsists on fruits. Then, transgressing your own code of conduct, how have you become sullied by harboring greed for the great treasure that captivates the hearts of chaste women — a treasure supremely rare and utterly unfit for you?

body.text:
viśākhā - lalite! bubhukṣito'yaṃ tapasvī phalam anālabhya etad ayogyam api kartuṃ
pravṛtto'sti | tad uttama-phalam asmai samuddiśyatām | tathāpi dharma-vṛddhir
bhaviṣyati |
body.translated_text: <s>Viśākhā</s> — <s>Lalite</s>! This ascetic is hungry and, not having obtained any fruit, has set about doing even this improper thing. Therefore, let an excellent fruit be pointed out to him. Even so, there will be an increase of <s>dharma</s> (merit).

body.text: lalitā smitam apavarya - viśākhe! kim asau mānasa-jāhnavīṃ na jānāti ?
body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s>, suppressing a smile — <s>Viśākhe</s>! Does he not know the <s>Mānasa-Jāhnavī</s> (the celestial Ganges of the mind)?

body.text: viśākhā - sarvatra bhramaṇa-śīlo'yam atiprasiddhāṃ tāṃ kathaṃ na jñāsyati ?
body.translated_text: <s>Viśākhā</s> — He is accustomed to wandering everywhere — how could he not know that most famous river?

body.text:
lalitā - tad vāyavya-tīre sarvataś-calā kācid apūrva-padmā sphuṭam ekā vallarī
vartate | tasyā madhya-bhāge parama-manoharaṃ ahrasvaṃ tumbī-phala-dvandvaṃ

children.translated_text: and at its tip there is an undiminished, non-bitter pair of <s>bimbī</s>-fruits. (199)

body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s> — On its northwest bank, there is clearly a certain extraordinary, ever-swaying lotus-creeper. In its middle portion hangs a supremely enchanting, not-small pair of gourd-fruits,

body.text:
viśākhā - gosvāmin! tvaritam eva tatra gatvā
tva-yogya-tad-anuttama-phalopabhogena sādhvī-dhana-lobham apahāya sva-dharmaṃ
pālayatā bhavatā parama-sukhinā bhūyatām |
body.translated_text: <s>Viśākhā</s> — O <s>Gosvāmin</s>! Go there swiftly, and by enjoying that unsurpassed fruit most suited to you, abandon your greed for the wealth of chaste women, protect your own <s>dharma</s>, and be supremely happy!

body.text:
tataḥ sarvāsu hasantīṣu mayoktaṃ - lalite! tapasya-sāvayācita-vṛttiḥ kara-pātrī
bhakṣaṇe niṣiddhaṃ tumbīphalaṃ nopabhuṅkte | kintu atraiva
nirbhara-nija-pradyota-bhareṇa yā dṛśyamānāpi na dṛśyate | tasyāḥ kāñcanavallyāḥ
kroḍe madhura-rasa-maya-śrī-phala-dvandvaṃ yad vidyotate tat svayam eva
saivāgatya praṇaya-pūrvakaṃ madhura-vacanenainaṃ nimantryāsya karo yadi
pariveśayati, tadā tad-upabhogena sukhī bhavann asau tathāśiṣayati yathā
tat-phalonnatir mahatī syāt |
body.translated_text: Then, while everyone was laughing, I said — <s>Lalite</s>! An ascetic who lives by the rule of unsolicited alms, who eats from the vessel of his hands, does not consume gourd-fruit, which is forbidden. But right here, there is one who, though visible by the full weight of her own radiance, is yet unseen. In the lap of that golden creeper, a pair of glorious fruits made of sweet <s>rasa</s> (essence) gleams. If she herself comes of her own accord and, with affection and sweet words, invites him and serves those into his hands, then by enjoying them he would become happy and would bless her such that the exaltation of those fruits would become immense.

body.text:
tatas tan niśamya rādhā anuccaiḥ - narma-lampaṭo'yaṃ dhūrtaḥ | śaṅke
vaidagdhyenātratyāṃ mad-avasthitim avadhārya mām eva kadarthayitum imāṃ
vacana-bhaṅgīṃ vitanoti | tad itaḥ kuñjāntaram āsādya sva-gopanam eva nūnam
ucitam |
body.translated_text: Then, hearing that, <s>Rādhā</s> said softly — This rogue is addicted to amorous jesting! I suspect that through his cleverness he has ascertained my presence here and is spinning this turn of phrase just to torment me. Therefore, it would indeed be proper to slip away to another bower-grove and hide myself.

body.text:
iti manasi bhāvayantyāṃ tasyāṃ punar mayoktaṃ - priya-sakhi lalite! ayaṃ
vṛndāvana-cārī mahā-vinodī kṣuṇṇa-yūtheśāṃ tvāṃ paṭṭa-rājñīṃ vidhāya tvayā
sahaika-siṃhāsa upaviśya viśākhā-prabhṛti-vṛndāvana-carīṇāṃ lāsya-vilāsam
ālokayitym abhilaṣati tad ājñāpyatām etā nṛtyantu |
body.translated_text: As she was thinking this in her mind, I spoke again — Dear friend <s>Lalite</s>! This wanderer of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, this great connoisseur of sport, wishes to install you — the presiding <s>yūtheśvarī</s> (group-leader) — as his chief queen, and sitting with you upon a single throne, desires to watch the graceful dancing of <s>Viśākhā</s> and the other ladies who roam <s>Vṛndāvana</s>. So command them — let them dance!

body.text:
lalitā sa-krodhaṃ - nāndīmukhi! asman-muktā-kedārikā-kara-parivartanena kim
asya vidūṣakasya narma-dhanam eva dāpayituṃ vayam atra vyāghoṭyānītāḥ smaḥ
? tad etāṃ narmādi-gati-kriyām apahāya yathāsau subalena saha yathārthaṃ lekham
ācarya kedārikā-karaṃ dadāti tathā vidhāyāsmān drutaṃ gṛhāya prasthāpaya |
body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s>, angrily — <s>Nāndīmukhi</s>! Have we been dragged here by the neck merely to hand over the tax-revenue of our pearl-field as comedy-money for this buffoon? Then, setting aside all this jesting and such antics, arrange it so that he, together with <s>Subala</s>, properly prepares a written assessment and pays the field-tax. Then take us home quickly!

body.text: nāndīmukhī - bhavatīnāṃ kiyān karaḥ saṃmataḥ syāt tat tāvat kathaya |
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s> — First tell me — what rate of tax would be agreeable to you all?

body.text:
lalitā - śyāmākādi-kṣetra-karato dhānyasyādhikaḥ karo lagati | tato'pi kārpāsasya |
tato'pi vāstu-bhūmeḥ pracurataraḥ | apūrvāmūlya-muktā-kedārasya tato'pi
parārdha-guṇaḥ | tad-alaukika-muktā-kedārikām imāṃ
dharma-śāstrokta-vṛndāvana-rājya-vihitālaukika-māna-daṇḍena parimāya lekhaṃ
vidhāya ca subala eva kathayatu |
body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s> — On grain fields such as <s>śyāmāka</s> (millet) and the like, a higher tax applies than on ordinary produce. Higher still on cotton. Even higher on homestead land. And on a pearl-field of incomparable value, higher still by an immeasurable factor! Therefore, let <s>Subala</s> himself measure this extraordinary pearl-field with the extraordinary measuring-rod prescribed by the <s>dharma-śāstra</s> for the kingdom of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, prepare the written record, and state the amount.

body.text: nāndīmukhī - kiyat pramāṇaṃ sa khalu māna-daṇḍaḥ ?
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s> — What exactly is the measure of that measuring-rod?

body.text:
lalitā - mayā kathyamānaḥ sa khalu kena pratīyatāṃ | tad etat kṣetra-pālikayā
sarva-śāstrābhijñayā vṛndayaiva sa nirūpayitavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s> — If I were to state it, who indeed would accept it from me? Therefore, let <s>Vṛndā</s> herself — the guardian of the fields, who is learned in all the <s>śāstras</s> — determine it.

body.text:
nāndīmukhī - bhadraṃ vṛnde! madhyasthayā tvayaiva muktā-māna-daṇḍaḥ kṛtvā
dīyatām |
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s> — Good! <s>Vṛnde</s>! Since you are the neutral party, you yourself should fashion the pearl-measuring-rod and present it.

body.text:
vṛndā devī -
vāstu-dhānyādi-kaṅkvādi-kārpāsa-mauktika-kṣamāḥ |
mīyante'ṅguṣṭham ārabhya kramād aṅguli-pañcakaiḥ || iti |
anyatra ca -
apūrva-muktā-kṣetrāṇām anarghya-karato budhaiḥ |
anāmikāṅguli-prāyo māna-daṇḍaḥ prakīrtitaḥ || iti |
body.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā Devī</s> — "Homestead land, grain fields, millet fields, cotton fields, and pearl fields are measured, starting from the thumb, progressively by sets of five fingers." And elsewhere — "For extraordinary pearl-fields, the wise have declared that the measuring-rod is principally the ring finger, on account of their incalculable tax-rate." Thus it is stated.

body.text:
nāndīmukhī - kṣura-pramātra-khānita-bhūmer
anāyāsenaivānargha-śasyotpādakatvāt kaniṣṭhaiva |
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s> — Since the land, dug to merely a razor's depth, effortlessly produces priceless crops, the little finger itself should be used!

body.text:
nāndīmukhī - lalite! yady api tad eva yuktaṃ bhavati tathāpi
vrajendra-kumāra-mukham ālokya bhagavatī-paricārikāṃ māṃ ca dṛṣṭvā
anāmikaiva sthāpyatām |
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s> — <s>Lalite</s>! Although that is indeed fitting, nevertheless, considering the face of the prince of <s>Vraja</s>, and seeing me, the attendant of the Goddess — let the ring finger be fixed as the standard.

body.text:
lalitā - vṛnde! tvaṃ tāval lekha-kriyāyāṃ māna-viṣaye ca nipuṇyāsi tat sarvābhiḥ
sambhūya gatvā nāndīmukhī-subala-saṃmati-pūrvakaṃ kedārikāṃ
parimīyāgamyatām |
nāndīmukhī - kṣuṇṇa-yūtheśvari! ekaṃ prārthayitum icchāmi |
body.translated_text:
<s>Lalitā</s> — <s>Vṛnde</s>! You are skilled in the preparation of written records and in matters of measurement. Therefore, let everyone go together, and with the approval of <s>Nāndīmukhī</s> and <s>Subala</s>, measure the pearl-field and return.
<s>Nāndīmukhī</s> — O presiding <s>yūtheśvarī</s>! I wish to make one request.

body.text: lalitā - kāmaṃ kathyatāṃ yogyaṃ cet kartavyam |
body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s> — By all means, speak — if it is reasonable, it shall be done.

body.text:
nāndīmukhī - ayaṃ tāvat sva-deśaṃ vihāyātrāgato navīna-prāghunaḥ tatrāpi
vṛndāvana-rājñīm āśrito'sti ihāpi bahv-āyāsenojjaṭa-bhūmiṃ kṛṣṭvā vaḥ
prakāma-dhana-lābhaṃ vardhayann asti | tasmān māne kṛte bhavatīnāṃ
bhoga-rāgādi-vyayena bahu-hānyā punaḥ kṛṣi-karaṇo vimanaska iva bhaviṣyati |
kṛte'pi māne karaṃ dātum api na śakyate | ato māna-karaṇaṃ vihāya nija-bhāgam
ādāya tat-samucitāṃśam api pradāyāsya prakāmam utsāhaṃ vivardhayantu
bhavatyaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s> — This man has left his own country and come here as a new tenant-farmer. Moreover, he has taken shelter of the queen of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>. And here too, with great effort, he has cleared the barren land, plowed it, and is increasing your abundant wealth. Therefore, once the measurement is done, between your expenses for enjoyment, cosmetics, and so forth, and the great loss thereby, the farmer will become disheartened. Even after measurement, he will not be able to pay the tax. So, setting aside the measurement altogether, let your ladyships take your own share and also grant him his appropriate portion, thus abundantly encouraging his enthusiasm!

body.text: vṛndā - kīdṛśaṃ sa bhāgaḥ ?
body.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> — What kind of share-arrangement is that?

body.text:
nāndīmukhī - tvayā kiṃ na jñāyate ? yad asya paramojjvala-kṣetrasya samāna eva
dvayor bhāgaḥ | tathāyaṃ para-grāmād āgatya kṛṣi-vṛttiṃ kurvann āste |
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s> — Do you not know? For this supremely splendid field, the share of both parties is equal. Moreover, he has come from another village and is carrying on the farming livelihood.

body.text:
raṅgaṇamālā anuccaiḥ - asau para-grāma-vāsī bhaumiko na syāt | sāmprataṃ
etasmin vane vāsam ācarya śrī-vṛndāvaneśākṛṣim ācarann asti | tad asya ṣaṣṭho
bhāga eva prāptavyo bhavati | kathaṃ samānaṃ labhatām ?
body.translated_text: <s>Raṅgaṇamālā</s>, softly — He is a resident of another village, so he would not be a native landholder. At present, having taken up residence in this forest, he is farming under the authority of <s>Śrī Vṛndāvaneśa</s> (the Lord of Vṛndāvana). Therefore, only a sixth share is due to him. How should he receive an equal share?

body.text:
viśākhā - ayi mugdhe! bhāga-nirṇaya-cālanayā kim asmākaṃ yato māna-pūrvakaṃ
sarvadā kara-dānaṃ kartum eva mahā-rājñīnām ājñā-lekhaḥ samāgato'sti tat
katham asmābhiḥ svātantryeṇaivaṃ kartuṃ śakyate ?
body.translated_text: <s>Viśākhā</s> — O naive one! What is the use of this maneuvering over share-determination? Since a decree from the great queen has already arrived ordering that tax must always be paid after proper measurement, how can we act independently in this manner?

body.text:
tato lalitā-viśākhayor mukham avalokya sva-karṇāvataṃsaṃ nāndīmukhyai
netra-kūṇanena vṛndā darśitavatī | tato'lpaṃ smitvā nāndīmukhī kiñcid upasṛtya
vṛndayā saha utkoca-dāna-kathan-mudrābhinayena tayor īṣad iṅgitam
evādhigamya mad-antikam āgatya sānucca-bhāṣaṃ - mohana! vṛndāvana-rājñyāḥ
sarvādhyakṣa-sacive khalu lalitā-viśākhe | tad anayoḥ paramottamam utkocaṃ kam
api dehi | tadaiva tavābhimatam eva drutaṃ sampādayitavyam etābhyām |
body.translated_text: Then, glancing at the faces of <s>Lalitā</s> and <s>Viśākhā</s>, <s>Vṛndā</s> showed her own ear-ornament to <s>Nāndīmukhī</s> with a wink. Then, smiling slightly, <s>Nāndīmukhī</s> approached a little and, through a pantomime gesture suggesting the giving of a bribe with <s>Vṛndā</s>, having grasped just a slight hint from those two, came to my side and said in a semi-audible voice — O <s>Mohana</s>! <s>Lalitā</s> and <s>Viśākhā</s> are indeed the chief ministers overseeing all affairs of the queen of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>. Therefore, give them some supremely excellent bribe! Only then will these two swiftly arrange exactly what you desire.

body.text:
tadāhaṃ sānandaṃ - sakhi nāndīmukhi! yathā anyā na jānanti tathā ime eva
nirjana-kuñje mat-samīpam ānīyetāṃ yathā etad abhīṣṭam utkocaṃ dattvā
prīṇayāmi |
body.translated_text: Then I said joyfully — Friend <s>Nāndīmukhi</s>! In such a way that the others do not find out, bring just these two to me in a secluded bower, so that I may give them the desired bribe and please them!

body.text:
nāndīmukhī - sundara! etāḥ khalv anayor abhinnā eva tad asaṅkocaṃ prakaṭam
atraiva dehi |
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s> — Handsome one! These others are in fact inseparable from those two. So give it openly, right here, without hesitation!

body.text:
tato'haṃ - svābhimatārtha-lābhena vinā pūrvam eva kathaṃ dātavyam | yadi mayy
apratītiḥ syāt tarhi tvayy eva sthāpayāmi |
body.translated_text: Then I said — How can one give in advance, without first obtaining the object one desires? If there is distrust toward me, then I shall place it in your keeping.

body.text: nāndīmukhī sa-śiraś-cālanaṃ - nahi nahi |
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>, shaking her head — No, no!

body.text:
tato'haṃ - āṃ brahmacāriṇyās tu viṣaya-sparśe kālūṣyam iti cet tadā
mat-pratīti-pātryāṃ sādhvī-pravarāyāṃ raṅgaṇamālikāyām eva tad arpayāmi |
body.translated_text: Then I said — Ah, if the concern is that contact with worldly objects would be defiling for a <s>brahmacāriṇī</s>, then I shall entrust it to <s>Raṅgaṇamālikā</s>, the foremost among chaste women, who is a worthy vessel of my trust.

body.text:
nāndīmukhī - rasika-śekhara! prathamaṃ tāvat śrāvaya kiṃ vā kiyad vā
dātavyam | tena tāvataiva vānayoḥ santoṣo bhaven na veti nirdhārayāmaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s> — 'O crown of connoisseurs (<s>rasika-śekhara</s>)! First just tell us what and how much is to be given. Then we shall determine whether those two will be satisfied with just that amount or not.'

body.text:
tadā mayoktaṃ - bhavatu | śrūyatām | vṛndāvana-rājasya mama vana-pālanam
apahāya dhana-lobhena mad-rājñīṃ rādhikām anusṛteyaṃ vṛndā | tat prathamam
utkoca-dānena kāyasthām enām ātmano vaśāṃ vidadhāmi |
body.translated_text: Then I said — 'Very well. Listen! This <s>Vṛndā</s>, abandoning the forest-keeping of my <s>Vṛndāvana</s> kingdom, has followed my queen <s>Rādhikā</s> out of greed for wealth. So first, by giving a bribe, I shall bring this female scribe (<s>kāyasthā</s>) under my control.'

body.text: nāndīmukhī - bhadram etat |
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s> — 'This is good.'

body.text:
tato'haṃ - carama-śarvaryāṃ paramākalpa-kalpanācāryayā gāḍhānurāga-vihvalayā
gāndharvyā yena mad-vakṣo-gaganam ākalpitaṃ tenaiva
niravadyārdha-candra-padaka-rājena sva-hastenaināṃ bhūṣayāmi | tataḥ kaustubhād
apy adhika-dedīpyamānenātula-tat-sahodara-mac-cumbaka-maṇinā yad
gāndharvayā praguṇa-paraspara-praṇayoddhura-keli-kautukena bakula-rāja-tale
parivartitaṃ apūrva-rasa-samudra-saṃloḍanāt
samudbhūta-ghanībhūta-tat-sārāṃśa-rūpaṃ man-maṇito'py anarghyaṃ
sva-cumbaka-mahā-ratnaṃ tat-tad-advaita-dayitam api lalitāyai dāsyāmi |
yathāsphuṭam asau tena sva-karṇābhyarṇam alaṃkaromi |
body.translated_text: Then I said — 'On the last night, by <s>Gāndharvā</s> (<s>Rādhā</s>), who was overcome with deep passion and was a master-adorner of supreme artistry, my chest-firmament was adorned — with that very peerless crescent-moon medallion-king, I shall adorn this one with my own hand. Then, with a kiss-jewel of mine — more brilliantly radiant than even the <s>Kaustubha</s> gem, its matchless twin born from her — which <s>Gāndharvā</s>, in the sportive curiosity of their mutually expert and passionately elated love, rolled beneath the <s>bakula</s> tree-king; which arose from the churning of an unprecedented ocean of <s>rasa</s> and is the solidified quintessence thereof; which is more priceless even than my own gem — that very kiss-jewel, though the inseparable beloved of its twin, I shall give to <s>Lalitā</s>. And I shall openly adorn her ear with it.'

body.text:
tataḥ punaḥ punar viśākhā-vadanam īṣad avalokyāhaṃ sa-smitam avadam -
anukṣaṇa-paramānurāga-bhareṇa sva-karābhyāṃ suṣṭhu viracayya
sva-kuṇḍa-kuḍaṅgāṅgane etat priya-sakhī gāndharvā suvaidagdhyena yī̀aṃ
mahyam arpitavatī | tayaiva vicitrāṅka-mālayā mad-dhṛdayākāśa-viśākhāṃ
viśākhām apy alaṅkṛtya paritoṣayāmi |
body.translated_text: Then, glancing again and again at <s>Viśākhā</s>'s face, I said with a smile — 'With supreme affection, moment by moment, skillfully fashioned by her own hands upon the courtyard of her own <s>kuṇḍa</s>, this precious thing my dear friend <s>Gāndharvā</s> gave to me with great artistry. With that very wondrous series of designs, I shall adorn <s>Viśākhā</s> — the <s>Viśākhā</s> (branching star) of my heart's firmament — and satisfy her.'

body.text:
tac chrutvā - alīka-rājendra! tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti vyāharantī rādhā manasaiva
līlā-kamalena tāṃ tāḍayati sma |
body.translated_text: Hearing that — 'O false king of kings! Stop, stop!' — saying this, <s>Rādhā</s> mentally struck him with a playful lotus.

body.text: lalitā - padmādhara-rasāhiphenāśana-pramatta! apehi apehi!
body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s> — 'O one intoxicated by the serpent-froth-nectar of lotus-lips! Begone, begone!'

body.text:
viśākhā - ārya vidūṣaka-pravara madhumaṅgala! bhavad-vayasyaḥ kiṃ bhavato'pi
guruḥ kiṃ vā tasya bhavān gurur ity avagantuṃ sarvāḥ samabhilaṣanti |
body.translated_text: <s>Viśākhā</s> — 'O noble premier jester <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>! All of us wish to know — is your friend your <s>guru</s>, or are you his <s>guru</s>?'

body.text:
lalitā - viśākhe! śrūyatām | kapaṭa-nāṭakasya yaḥ kusumaśara-nāmā naṭas tasya
suprasiddho yaḥ śuci-nāmā vidūṣakas tenāyaṃ dhūrtaḥ śiṣyatvena
kṛpayānugṛhīto'sti | madhumaṅgalas tu
bhinna-sampradāyi-bhojana-lampaṭa-nāmno vidūṣakācāryasya prathīyān śiṣyaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s> — '<s>Viśākhe</s>! Listen — the famous jester named <s>Śuci</s> (Pure), who belongs to the actor named <s>Kusumaśara</s> (<s>Kāmadeva</s>, the flower-arrowed one) of the drama of deceit, has graciously accepted this rogue as his disciple. <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>, however, is the eminent disciple of the jester-teacher named <s>Bhinna-sampradāyi-bhojana-lampaṭa</s> (the Glutton of Heterodox Cuisine).'

body.text: viśākhā - lalite! tad enaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ miṣṭānnaṃ bhojayitum icchāmi |
body.translated_text: <s>Viśākhā</s> — '<s>Lalitā</s>! I wish to feed this <s>brāhmaṇa</s> some sweet food.'

body.text:
lalitā - viśākhe! asau karma-sūcakaḥ paramānucāno mahā-brāhmaṇaḥ | tat katham
asmākaṃ brāhmaṇetara-gopa-jātīnāṃ rāddham annam aśnātu |
body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s> — '<s>Viśākhe</s>! That one is a <s>karma-sūcaka</s> (indicator of ritual acts) — a supremely learned great <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. So how can he eat food cooked by us who are of non-<s>brāhmaṇa</s> cowherd castes?'

body.text:
viśākhā - paramottama-dvijābhyāṃ mallī-bhṛṅgābhyāṃ sva-hastenānnaṃ saṃskṛtya
paramādareṇa yathāsau bhojyate tathaiva sampādanīyam |
body.translated_text: <s>Viśākhā</s> — 'Let the two supreme excellent twice-borns (<s>dvijas</s>), <s>Mallī</s> and <s>Bhṛṅgī</s>, cook the food with their own hands and let it be arranged that he is served with the highest respect.'

body.text:
tatas tac chrutvā krodhena kampamāna iva madhumaṅgalaḥ prāha - aye
avadyavādini garvitābhīrike! etad
duḥśravaṇa-narmotkaṭa-kaṭu-lavaṇa-digdha-dagdhārdha-paryuṣita-vāg-godhūm
a-roṭikāḥ saṃbhojya mama madhura-karṇāv eva suṣṭhu kaṭūkṛtau, kiṃ punar
mukha-vivaram | tad vidūṣaka-gopa-vadhūnāṃ yuṣmākaṃ chāyā-nikaṭa-bhūmim
api kadāpi na spṛśāmi | kintu prātar evāsmaj-jāti-yājñika-vadhū-vargam
upasarpiṣyāmi | tatas tena paramādareṇa mac-caraṇa-kṣālana-pūrvakaṃ
kauśeya-dukūle paridhāpya
sakarpūra-vāsitopalāpānaka-madhura-paramānna-sasaindhavārdraka-limpāka-nā
nā-vidha-vyañjana-veṣṭita-saghṛta-sugandhi-śālyanna-phānita-śaṣkulī-kuṇḍalik
ā-laḍḍuka-ghanāvartita-dugdha-rasālā-saśarkara-baddha-dadhi-vividha-baṭakotta
ma-marīcādibhis tathāhaṃ bhojayiṣye | yathā vartmani succhāya-taru-mūleṣu
svapan sva-gṛham āgatya saṅgavāvadhi svapann eva tiṣṭhāmi |
body.translated_text: Then, hearing that, <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>, trembling as if with rage, said — 'O speaker of shameful words! O proud <s>Abhīrikā</s> (cowherd-girl)! Having feasted me on these unbearable, harshly jesting, sharp, salty, smeared, burnt, half-stale verbal wheat-cakes, you have made even my sweet ears most bitter — let alone the opening of my mouth! Therefore I shall never touch even the shadow-ground near you jester-cowherd-wives. But in the very morning I shall approach the womenfolk of the <s>yājñika</s>-<s>brāhmaṇas</s> of my own caste. Then, with the highest respect, after first washing my feet and wrapping me in silken garments, I shall feast upon camphor-scented sugar-water drink, sweet rice-pudding (<s>paramānna</s>), salty ginger pickle, various side-dishes, ghee-laden fragrant rice, treacle cakes (<s>śaṣkulī</s>), spirals (<s>kuṇḍalikā</s>), <s>laḍḍus</s>, thickened milk, mango cream (<s>rasālā</s>), sweetened curd, various fritters (<s>baṭaka</s>), finest pepper and other spices — in such a manner that I shall sleep at the shady tree-roots along the road, and arriving home continue sleeping until the <s>saṅgava</s> hour (mid-morning).'

body.text:
tatas tac-chravaṇena hāsa-kolāhale vṛtte mayoktaṃ - nāndīmukhi! kṣudra-gāminair
eva sva-sva-grāma-sīmārthaṃ madhyastham ālambya nyāyaḥ kriyate | rājānas tu
rājyaṃ sva-dordaṇḍa-balenaiva labhante | tad etad-rājya-hetor nyāyena kim ? mayā
sahaitāḥ samaram ācarantu | tatra yasya jayo bhavet tasyaiva rājyaṃ sphuṭaṃ
setsyati |
body.translated_text: Then, when laughter and uproar arose from hearing that, I said — '<s>Nāndīmukhī</s>! Only the petty-minded seek an arbitrator from within their own village boundaries for justice. Kings, however, obtain their kingdoms by the strength of their own arms alone. So what need is there of legal proceedings for this kingdom? Let them wage war against me. Whoever wins, the kingdom shall clearly be theirs.'

body.text:
ity uktvā tad-artham iva sāṭopaṃ kiñcid upasarpati mayi tāsu ca itas tataḥ
sa-bhaya-sahelanam apasarpantīṣu nāndīmukhī - vīra! sampraty asmat-samakṣam
etāsām ujjvala-kula-vilasita-ballava-vadhūnāṃ dharṣaṇam etad bhavataḥ param
asāmpratam eva |
body.translated_text: Saying this, as I advanced with martial swagger as if for that very purpose, and as they scattered here and there with fearful playfulness, <s>Nāndīmukhī</s> — 'O hero! At present, in our very presence, this assault upon these illustrious, radiant cowherd-wives of noble clan is most unseemly of you.'

body.text:
ity avadhārayann ārād eva tiṣṭheti mām ābhāṣya lalitāṃ praty uvāca - lalite |
sāmpratam asya vana-vīrasya nirjana-vane'smin pragalbhatā-mahatī bhavatīnāṃ tu
śirīṣa-kusuma-mṛdulāni śarīrāṇi, tad deśa-kāla-balādikaṃ vīkṣya vivādaṃ tyaja |
body.translated_text: Thus determining, telling me 'Stay far away!', she addressed <s>Lalitā</s> — '<s>Lalitā</s>! At present, the boldness of this forest-hero is great indeed in this desolate forest. But your bodies are soft as <s>śirīṣa</s> (silk-cotton) blossoms. Therefore, considering the balance of place, time, and strength, abandon this quarrel.'

body.text:
tac chrutvā candramukhī - bho mugdhāḥ! nāndīmukhī satyaṃ kathayati | tac
chṛṇudhvam | vayam abalāḥ komalāṅgyaḥ | ayaṃ tu nirjana-vana-puruṣo'ticapalaḥ |
yasyā darśanād evāyaṃ sādhvasena vihvalo bhavati | sāpy asmac-cakravartinī
nāntika-vartinī | sudurmukhābhimanyu-prabhṛti-vāhinī-patayo'pi sampraty
etad-vṛttānabhijñā dūre vartante | tad-bhayānaka-deśe'sminn ātma-madhye dvandve
patite sarvataḥ sarve luṇṭāka-duṣṭa-gamakāḥ samutthāya samasta-mauktikāni
viluṇṭhya neṣyanti | tadāsmākam eva mahatī hānir bhaviṣyati | asya tu ṣaṣṭhāṃśa
eva tato'lpa-hāniḥ | tad yadi sarvābhyo rocate tarhi vayaṃ saumyā iva bhavatyaḥ
samprati rājya-vārtām apahāya samucitād apy adhika-mūlyena mauktikāny ādāya
asya cillātakasya sparśa-mātreṇaiva janiṣyamāṇa-duṣkīrti-bharād ātmānam api
saṃrakṣya sva-gṛham āsādayāmaḥ | paścād etad-vṛttānta-śravaṇād eva
vṛndāvana-mahārājñī tan-muktā-pradānena drutam eva guru-prabhṛtīn santoṣya
mahārāgeṇātivegena svayam atrāgatya dūrata eva kaṭakāṭopam avaṣṭabhya svayaṃ
samaram akurvāṇā cañcala-nayanāñcala-pravaṇayā
nīta-tīkṣṇādhāra-viṣama-śarāstra-saṃvardhita-bhrūkuṭi-dhanurdhara-sumukha-
kañja-bhīṣaṇābhimanyu-prabhṛti-vāhinī-pati-dvāraiva tathā vigraha-bhaṅgīm
āṭopayiṣyati | yathāyaṃ vana-madhya eva vīraṃmanyas tvaritam eva sādhvasena
kampamānaḥ san
bṛṃhita-hāheti-kamala-rāga-maṇi-prakara-khacita-cāru-cāṭu-cintā-rana-nikara-ra
cita-mañjula-mālāṃ nija-kaṇṭhād uttāryopaḍhaukitīkṛtya tac-caraṇa-parisaraṃ
śaraṇam upagacchann etat-samudita-gadgada-gadita-khara-dyuti-lavena
tat-kāla-druta-citta-navanītayā tayā kāruṇyena prasādī-kṛtenaiva
tad-yāvakāruṇa-maṇi-draveṇābhinava-śikhaṇḍāvataṃsaṃ śoṇam iva racayann
etad-rājyaṃ tad-utpanna-nikhila-mauktikādikam api samarpya svayam api tām
evānucariṣyati |
body.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Candramukhī</s> — 'O naive ones! <s>Nāndīmukhī</s> speaks the truth. Listen! We are weak, soft-limbed women. This one, however, is an extremely fickle man of the desolate forest. She at whose very sight he becomes overwhelmed with dread — she, our empress, is not nearby. Even the army-chiefs like <s>Durmukhābhimanyu</s> and others are presently far away, unaware of these events. In this frightful place, if a duel breaks out in our midst, from all sides the robbers and wicked highwaymen will rise up and plunder all the pearls and carry them away. Then we ourselves shall suffer the greatest loss, while his would be only a sixth — hence small. Therefore, if it pleases you all, let us — as gentle ladies — setting aside this talk of kingdoms, take the pearls at even more than the appropriate price, and also preserving ourselves from the mass of ill-repute that would arise from even the touch of this scoundrel, let us reach our homes. Afterward, upon merely hearing the account of these events, the great queen of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, having quickly satisfied the elders and others by giving them those pearls, will herself come here with great passion and utmost speed. From a distance, taking up a martial stance, without herself engaging in battle — with her restless sidelong glance, with her fierce sharp lower-lip arrow-weapon, with her bow-like furrowed brow, with her awe-inspiring lotus-face — through the army-chiefs like <s>Abhimanyu</s> alone, she will contrive such a form of war that this forest-hero, fancying himself brave, will quickly tremble with dread right here in the forest, and removing from his own neck his ruby-gem-studded, beautiful, flattery-filled, wondrously crafted lovely garland — with cries of "Alas! Alas!" — will humbly offer it and take refuge at her feet. And then, with his heart-butter instantly melted by the gleam of her harsh-bright tears, she, compassionately pacified, with the flow of crimson lac-jewel-liquid from her reddened feet, will fashion upon him a fresh peacock-feather crest-ornament tinged scarlet. And he will surrender this kingdom and all the pearls it has produced and follow her himself.'

body.text:
tac-chravaṇena sānandollāsa-sasmitaṃ rādhā-kuñjaṃ tiryag avalokayati mayi
nāndīmukhī smitvā - gokula-pravīra! tvad-anurūpa-viṣama-śara-samara-pravīṇayā
vṛndāvana-cakravartinyā samam eva bhavat-samara-paripāṭī paraṃ śobhate | etāḥ
punar atīva komalās tad-abhyarṇam antareṇa tvayā saha tādṛśa-vigraha-vilāsaṃ
katham ācarantu tad alīka-virodhaṃ parityajya sāmpratam anyāsām api mauktikam
amūlyaṃ nirṇīyatāṃ paścād bhagavaty eva rājya-nyāyaṃ vicārayiṣyati |
body.translated_text: Hearing that, as I was joyfully, delightedly, and smilingly gazing sideways toward <s>Rādhā</s>'s bower, <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>, smiling — 'O hero of <s>Gokula</s>! A battle with the empress of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, who is skilled in the fierce-arrow combat suited to you, would indeed be most fitting. But these others are exceedingly delicate; so without her nearby, how can they engage in such warlike sport with you? Therefore, abandoning this pretense of hostility, let the pearls of the rest also be priced at once. Afterward, <s>Bhagavatī</s> herself shall adjudicate the matter of the kingdom.'

body.text:
tatas tāsāṃ sākūta-vacanam avadhāryaiva garvita-gopyo jitā jitā iti vadan sva-mukhe
vāma-muṣṭiṃ bherīkṛtya vādayan madhumaṅgalaḥ sānandaṃ bhāṇḍavam ātanoti |
body.translated_text: Then, having understood the insinuating words of those [<s>gopīs</s>], <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>, saying triumphantly 'Conquered! Conquered!' — making his left fist into a drum and beating it against his mouth — joyfully performed a comic dance.

body.text:
vṛndā - bho naṭa-pravara madhumaṅgala! asmac-cakravartinyām atrāyātāyām api
tad-āhlādanārtham ātma-priya-sakhasya hāheti-ḍhakkā-vādyena śikṣā-vaiśiṣṭyena
ṣaṭ-pado bhavan uḍḍīyoḍḍīya bhramarikām ādadānaḥ sphuṭam ito raṅgād asmād
adhikam uddaṇḍaḥ tāṇḍavayann anena dvipada-gopena sārdhaṃ sugahanaṃ
nandīśvara-goṣṭham āpsyasi | tadānīṃ tad-avalokanād vayam api
cakṣuḥ-sāphalyam utsphārayiṣyāmaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> [said]: 'O best of actors, <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>! Even though our empress has arrived here, you — a six-legged [bee] — in order to delight your dear friend, [making] the drum-sound "hāhā," displaying your special skill, buzzing and buzzing about, performing a wilder <s>tāṇḍava</s> dance from this stage than [what is seen] here, together with this two-legged cowherd, you will surely reach the dense assembly-hall of <s>Nandīśvara</s>. At that time, by beholding that, we too shall make our eyes fruitful.'

body.text:
tato'haṃ vihasya - nāndīmukhi! seyaṃ candramukhī sāmañjasya-ratā lalitādivad
dvandva-pātinī na bhavati | ato vinā mūlyenāpy asyai santuṣṭena mayā mauktikāni
deyāni | kintv iyaṃ mantra-vidāṃ mūrdhanyā tataḥ śvaḥ paraśvo vā parama-śuciḥ
satī rahaḥ sthānam āgatya snānādinā parama-śucaye
kāntadarpābhidhācārya-nirukta-mantra-paṭalaṃ mahyam upadiśatu | yatheha
vṛndāvane gopenaiva mayā surādhikā-śrī-drutam eva labhyate |
body.translated_text: Then I, laughing, [said]: '<s>Nāndīmukhī</s>! This <s>Candramukhī</s> is devoted to fairness and does not play favorites in pairs like <s>Lalitā</s> and the others. Therefore, even without payment, I, being satisfied, should give her pearls. But since she is foremost among those versed in <s>mantras</s>, let her — being supremely pure tomorrow or the day after — come to a secluded place and, after bathing and so forth, teach me the chapter of <s>mantras</s> expounded by the teacher named <s>Kāntadarpa</s> ("Beloved's Pride"), so that I, a mere cowherd, may quickly attain in this <s>Vṛndāvana</s> a glory surpassing even the gods.'

body.text:
tataś candramukhī kuṭilaṃ mām avalokayanty āha - aho mām api hitopadeśinīṃ
kṛtānabhijñas tvaṃ kadarthayitum udyato'si ? nāhaṃ tava mantrābhijñā
tan-mantra-caturā kāñcana-latair ācāryā kriyatāṃ bhavatā |
body.translated_text: Then <s>Candramukhī</s>, looking at me sideways, said: 'Oh! Are you, pretending not to know, ready to insult me too, who am giving you good advice? I am not versed in <s>mantras</s> for you — [if you want] a teacher skilled in those <s>mantras</s>, let <s>Kāñcana-latā</s> ("Golden Vine") be made your teacher!'

body.text:
tato'haṃ - kāñcanalate! bhavad-vaidagdhyāvalokanena man-mano-bhramaras tvayi
prakāmam anurajyann atīvotkaṇṭhate tat-parama-sundaratārādhikā
bhavad-upakaṇṭha-vartinī mañjulataraikāvalir ekā sasmitam ālokayantīnām āsāṃ
samakṣam eva paramotkaṇṭhite mad-urasi sneha-bhareṇa svayam eva tvayā yady
adhīyate tarhi mūlyam antareṇāpi bhavad-abhīṣṭa-mauktikāny avaśyaṃ
vitariṣyāmi | api ca mat-pariṣvaṅga-lalita-ratna-hāra-trayeṇa
bhavat-kaṇṭha-madhya-nābhi-pradeśānalaṃ prasādhayiṣyāmīti tām anusarati mayi
sā māṃ tiryag-avalokayantī huṃ kurvatī kiñcic apasasāra | rādhā ca sasmitaṃ
kurvatī ātmani śaṅkām ādhāya sambhramam avāpa |
body.translated_text: Then I [said]: 'O <s>Kāñcana-latā</s>! Beholding your cleverness, the bee of my mind, deeply attracted to you, is filled with intense longing. O supremely beautiful one, near you there abides a most charming single necklace, which smiles as it gazes — before the eyes of these [ladies] who look on smilingly — if it is placed by you yourself, out of the weight of affection, upon my supremely longing breast, without any price, I shall certainly bestow the pearls you desire. Moreover, with three lovely gem-necklaces from my embrace, I shall adorn the regions of your throat, middle, and navel.' As I followed her saying this, she, looking at me sideways, said 'hum!' with displeasure and slightly drew back. And <s>Rādhā</s>, making a slight smile, placed suspicion upon herself and became agitated.

body.text:
tato viśākhā tarjany-aṅguṣṭha-choṭikayā nāndīmukhīm abhimukhīkṛtya
netra-kūṇanena raṅgaṇamālikā-tulasike darśitavatī |
body.translated_text: Then <s>Viśākhā</s>, snapping her thumb and forefinger, facing <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>, indicated <s>Raṅgaṇamālikā</s> and <s>Tulasikā</s> with a wink of the eye.

body.text:
nāndīmukhī vihasya - mohana! ime rādhikā-priya-caraṇa-tat-pare tad-atīva-priye
raṅgaṇamālikā-tulasike tāṃ vinā-kṣaṇam api kutrāpy avasthātuṃ na śaknuvatas tad
anayor muktā-mūlyaṃ nirṇīya tūrṇam ete tad-antike prasthāpaya |
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>, laughing [said]: 'O enchanting one! These <s>Raṅgaṇamālikā</s> and <s>Tulasikā</s>, devoted to the beloved feet of <s>Rādhikā</s>, most dear to her, are unable to remain anywhere even for a moment without her. Therefore, having fixed the pearl-price for these two, quickly send them to her side.'

body.text:
tato'haṃ sāntarānandaṃ vihasya - nāndīmukhi! tulasyā
adṛṣṭacara-cañcala-nayanāñcalāvaloka-lava-marikca-kṣoda-miśrita-susmita-nava-
ghanasāra-lava-parimilitāśruta-cara-nava-nava-bhāṣita-makaranda-pāyanena
vihvalīkṛtam iva māṃ sneha-vihvalā raṅgaṇamālikā mad-urasi
nija-kuca-kuṭmalābhyām avaṣṭabhya maj-jīvātu-rūpa-svādhara-pīyūṣa-pāyanena
drutaṃ sandhukṣayatv iti |
body.translated_text: Then I, laughing with inner delight, [said]: '<s>Nāndīmukhī</s>! By the drink of the nectar of ever-new speech — mixed with a pinch of tender smile [like] fresh camphor blended with crumbs of pepper from the fleeting sidelong glance of <s>Tulasī</s>'s playful, darting eyes — I am made to swoon, as it were. Let <s>Raṅgaṇamālikā</s>, overwhelmed with affection, pressing the buds of her breasts against my chest, quickly revive me with the nectar-drink of her own lower lip, which is the very elixir of my life!'

body.text: tataḥ sarvāsu hasantīṣv avanata-mukhyau te viśākhā-pṛṣṭha-lagne babhūvatuḥ |
body.translated_text: Then, as all [the <s>gopīs</s>] laughed, those two, with faces bowed down, clung to <s>Viśākhā</s>'s back.

body.text:
nāndīmukhī - muktāphala-vāṇijya-vilāsin! yūtheśayor api rādhā-viśākhayor
mauktika-mūlya-nirṇaye yan mano na dhatse | tatra kiṃ kāraṇam ?
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s> [said]: 'O merchant sporting in pearl-trade! You do not set your mind to fixing the pearl-price even for the two group-leaders, <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Viśākhā</s>. What is the reason?'

body.text:
tato'haṃ - sā yūtheśā mat-savidham āgatya cet svayaṃ nirṇayati | tadaiva
nirṇayanīyam | tad-agocare kena nirṇīyatām ?
body.translated_text: Then I [said]: 'If that group-leader herself comes near me and fixes [the price] of her own accord, then alone it should be fixed. Outside her presence, who can fix it?'

body.text:
nāndīmukhī - vīra! mūlyaṃ tāvat prakāśaya | yathā tac-chravaṇena
tan-mūlya-dravyāṇāṃ samāhṛtis tayā kriyate |
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s> [said]: 'O hero! At least declare the price, so that upon hearing it, she may gather the goods [worth] that price.'

body.text:
mayoktaṃ - rādhā-viśākhayor advaitād dvayor api mad-atīva-priyayor yat kiñcin
mūlyaṃ kathyate tac chrūyatām |
mat-pṛṣṭha-mañjulatara-tamāla-saṃvalita-masṛṇatara-
dakṣiṇa-savya-bhujā-svarṇa-latayor gāndharvikā-viśākhayor
lalita-natāṃsa-nihita-vilāsollasita-parimilita-supracaṇḍa-dor-daṇḍa-yugalasya
surabhi-kusuma-kula-parivāsita-vana-vihāra-mādhurīm anusṛtasya parasparam
aviṣama-nirupama-prema-kalāpāvalokana-kautukena mama gaṇḍa-raṅga-sthale
tan-madhura-vadana-sudhākara-pravīṇa-naṭa-pravarau yugapat pṛthag vā mṛdu
mṛdu tāṇḍavaṃ samullāsayantau mad-ānanda-kandaṃ kandalayatām |
body.translated_text: I said: 'Since <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Viśākhā</s> are non-different, both most dear to me, hear whatever price is stated for both: Let the two expert dancers — the sweet-faced, moonlike ones — while entwined on my back by the lovely, dark <s>tamāla</s>-smooth right and left golden-creeper-arms of the musician <s>Viśākhā</s>, with their gracefully bent shoulders bearing the touching, playfully-swaying, fierce paired arms — as I follow the sweetness of a forest excursion perfumed by clusters of fragrant flowers — with the curiosity of beholding each other's matchless and incomparable garlands of love, perform on the stage of my cheek, gently, gently, a <s>tāṇḍava</s> [dance] simultaneously or separately, and cause the sprout of my bliss to blossom!'

body.text:
kiṃ ca, rādhā-kuṇḍa-taṭī-kuḍuṅga-bhavanāṅgane
bhramad-bhramara-jhaṅkṛti-parimilita-surabhi-kusuma-vṛnda-syandamāna-makar
anda-mañjula-bakula-talāmala-kanaka-vedikāyāṃ
mañjula-malli-kusuma-dala-kula-kalpita-praśasta-sukumāra-talpopari svarṇa-
yūthikā-kusuma-kṛta-candropadhāne vāma-kaphoṇim avaṣṭabhya
saṅkucita-jānu-dvayaṃ sukhopaviṣṭasya man-mano-madhupāśrayavāsantyā
viśākhayā svarṇa-sampuṭa-sthita-kuṅkuma-rasaṃ kiñcit ślatham ivālokayantyā
sva-sakhya-praṇaya-madhūnmādena nistala-nija-vakṣoja-yugalād
ākṛṣṭa-dara-kaṭhinībhūta-surabhi-kuṅkuma-paṅka-milanād īṣad ghanīkṛtya tena
mṛdu mṛdu rūṣite mama pulakita-vakṣasi mat-prāṇa-pañjara-śārikā rādhikā
kadācit svasya kadācit viśākhāyāḥ kuca-sampuṭa-vikṛṣṭa-nava-mṛgamada-draveṇa
saromāñcaṃ campaka-kalikāgreṇa vallari-makarāṅkura-patrāṇi
praguṇākalpa-kalpanayā kalpayantī
nirbhara-parasparāsamānordhva-sauhārda-saurabhya-bhareṇa
camatkṛti-valita-mad-deha-mano-vākyāni paraṃ parivāsayatv iti |
body.translated_text: Furthermore: 'On the spotless golden platform beneath the lovely <s>bakula</s> tree, from which streams of nectar drip from clusters of fragrant flowers mingled with the humming of buzzing bees, in the courtyard of the bower-house on the bank of <s>Rādhā-kuṇḍa</s> — upon a beautiful, delicate couch fashioned from clusters of lovely <s>mallī</s>-flower petals, with a pillow made of golden <s>yūthikā</s> flowers — as I sit comfortably, leaning on my left elbow with knees drawn in, while <s>Viśākhā</s>, the bee-refuge <s>vāsantī</s> (spring-jasmine) of my mind, looking somewhat languorously at the <s>kuṅkuma</s>-paste in a golden casket, her love-intoxication stirred by affection for her dear friend, slightly thickens [the paste] drawn and somewhat hardened from the round surface of her own breasts with fragrant <s>kuṅkuma</s> mud, and gently, gently applies it on my thrilled chest — let <s>Rādhikā</s>, the <s>śārikā</s>-bird of the cage of my life, sometimes with the drops of fresh musk drawn from her own breast-casket, sometimes from <s>Viśākhā</s>'s, fashioning with a <s>campaka</s>-bud-tip the leaf-designs of creeper-<s>makara</s>-sprouts in ingenious ornamental patterns, with goosebumps [arising], thoroughly perfume my body, mind, and words with the weight of the uncontainable, mutual, unrivaled, exalted fragrance of love!'

body.text:
ato rādhā-viśākhe sa-snehaṃ yugapat supulaka-paraspara-cātu-rakṣika-vīkṣaṇena
lajjite babhūvatuḥ |
body.translated_text: At this, <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Viśākhā</s>, simultaneously, with horripilation, exchanging affectionate, playful, protective glances at each other, became bashful.

body.text:
viśākhā - lalite! lampaṭatā-nāṭye tal-lampaṭa-naṭābhyām
asambhava-manoratha-nāma-nāṭakasya vidhīyamānābhinaya-vīkṣaṇāya
nirjana-vana-raṅge'smin yathārtha-nāmnī nāndīmukhīyaṃ
mauktika-pradāna-nimittaka-vitathā-vāk-prastutyāsmān sabhāsadaḥ kartuṃ
saṃrakṣya prakāreṇa viḍambayitum udyuktāsti | tad atra raṅge yasyā raṅgo vidyate
sā kila kulavatī sādhvī sphuṭam asya catuḥṣaṣṭhī-kalā-vidagdhasya naṭasya
lāsyam atropaviśya paśyantī bhadreṇa kula-dvayam utkīrtayatu ahaṃ tu gṛhaṃ
gacchāmi |
body.translated_text: <s>Viśākhā</s> [said]: '<s>Lalitā</s>! In the drama of licentiousness, this aptly-named <s>Nāndīmukhī</s> — under the pretext of giving pearls, through the false praise of words — is prepared to make us into an audience in this solitary forest-stage for the performance of the play called "Impossible Fantasy" enacted by those two debauched actors, and is cunningly attempting to embarrass us. So in this arena, let whichever well-born, virtuous lady has a taste for such spectacle sit here watching the dance (<s>lāsya</s>) of this actor skilled in the sixty-four arts, and thereby glorify both [our] families. As for me — I am going home.'

body.text:
tato nāndīmukhī -sakhi viśākhe! asya narma-karmaṭha-śīlasya durlīlasya
vacana-vilāsa-mātreṇaiva kathaṃ nirvidya khidyase ? kṣaṇaṃ tiṣṭha | niḥsandeham
adhunaiva muktā dāpayiṣyanty asmi iti tām ābhāsya nivartya ca mat-savidham
āsādya māṃ prāha - durlīla gopa-yuvarāja! bhavad-visadṛśa-narmālāpa-śravaṇena
viśākhādayo mad-upari śaśvat khidyante | tat kṛpayā samprati
narma-karma-pañjikā-prapañcaṃ saṃrakṣya kraya-vikraya-pañjikām udghāṭya
draviṇādi-mūlyena muktāḥ pradāya dhruvam amūr
bhavat-snigdha-gāndharvā-camūs tvaritam anurañjaya |
body.translated_text: Then <s>Nāndīmukhī</s> [said]: 'Dear <s>Viśākhā</s>! Why are you wearied and displeased merely by the playful words of this one whose nature is that of a mischievous prankster? Wait a moment! I shall without doubt have him give the pearls right now.' Having addressed her thus and turned her back, coming near me, she said: 'O mischievous prince of cowherds! By hearing your jests so unlike yourself, <s>Viśākhā</s> and the others are constantly vexed with me. Therefore, kindly now, setting aside the register of pranks, open the register of buying and selling, and having given the pearls for the price in money and the like, quickly delight these musicians — your affectionate troupe.'

body.text:
tato'haṃ - nāndīmukhi! yadyapi rādhā mayi kāṭhinyam eva santatam ātanoti,
tathāpi sahaja-snigdhasya mama manas tu tan-nāma-mātra-śravaṇād eva nāṅgam
eva samastaṃ drutam anusandhatte tadānu tat-sahacarīṣu kāṭhinyena kim ? tato
dina-dvayābhyantare yāvan nirṇīta-mūlyam upasthāpayanti | tāvad eva
tat-suvarṇālaṅkāraṇādi-raupyādi-rasādi-priya-gavādikaṃ dhanaṃ mayi sthāpyatayā
mayi saṃrakṣya etad-anurūpa-kiyan-mauktikāni gṛhṇantu |
body.translated_text: Then I [said]: '<s>Nāndīmukhī</s>! Although <s>Rādhā</s> constantly extends only hardness toward me, nevertheless, since my heart, being naturally tender, at the mere hearing of her name instantly melts in every limb — what need then of hardness toward her companions? So within two days, as long as they present the assessed price, let them keep with me all that wealth — gold ornaments, silver, mercury, and beloved cows and the like — and take the corresponding pearls.'

body.text:
ity ābhāṣya punaḥ kṣaṇaṃ maunena vimṛśyāha - nāndīmukhi!
santata-dayita-gocāraṇa-līlayā vane vane bhramatā mayaitat sarvaṃ kutra
rakṣitavyam | pratīti-pātram api ko'pi na dṛśyate | rakṣite ca para-ramaṇī-dravye
lajjāpakīrtito mahad bhayaṃ labhyate | tat satyam ucyate prastuta-mūlyaṃ vinā etat
kim api na sampadyata eva |
body.translated_text: Having said this, I paused a moment in silence and reflected, then said: '<s>Nāndīmukhī</s>! Constantly roaming from forest to forest in the pastime of tending my beloved's cows — where am I to safeguard all this? There is not a single trustworthy person to be seen. And if one guards the property of another's woman, great fear of shame and infamy is incurred. So truly it is said: without the price being duly presented, nothing at all can be accomplished.'

body.text: nāndīmukhī - mohana! etad apūrva-mūlyaṃ kutrāpi na dṛṣṭaṃ na vā śrutam asti |
body.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>: 'O enchanting one! Such an unprecedented price has never been seen or heard of anywhere!'

body.text:
tato'haṃ - vidagdhe nāndīmukhi! īdṛśam etad bhūmi-jātāpūrva-mauktikaṃ tvayā
brahmāṇḍe kutrāpi dṛṣṭacaraṃ śrutacaraṃ vā asti ? tad-apūrva-padārthasya
mūlyam apy apūrvam | tatrāpi na vayaṃ muktā-vyāpāriṇaḥ kintu kevalaṃ
bhagavatī-pādānām ādeśena bhavad-āgraheṇa cātra pravartitāḥ smaḥ | tasmāc ced
icchā syāt tarhi mitho nirdhārita-mūlyaṃ prastutaṃ dattvā parama-caturā etā
mauktikāni gṛhṇantu | no ced gṛhaṃ gacchantu | paśya madhyāhna-prāyo divaso
jātas tad vayam api godhana-sambhālanāya govardhanaṃ gacchāmaḥ |
body.translated_text: Then I: 'O witty <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>! Have you ever seen or heard of such an unprecedented earth-born pearl anywhere in the universe? An unprecedented object has an unprecedented price. Moreover, we are not pearl-merchants — we have been engaged in this purely by the command of the divine lady's feet and by your insistence. Therefore, if you wish, let these supremely clever women pay the duly agreed price and take the pearls. If not, let them go home. Look, the day has become nearly midday — so we too shall go to <s>Govardhana</s> to tend the cattle.'

body.text:
tato nāndīmukhī sanirvedam iva lalitāntikam upetya anuccaiḥ - sakhi lalite! sakhi
viśākhe! bhoḥ sarvāḥ priyasakhyaḥ!
body.translated_text: Then <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>, as if with dejection, approached <s>Lalitā</s> and said softly: 'Friend <s>Lalitā</s>! Friend <s>Viśākhā</s>! O all dear friends!'

body.text:
tataḥ adbhuta-tapasvini! tiṣṭha tiṣṭha iti nāndīmukhīm ākṣipya māṃ prati lalitā
smitvā - dhīra-lalita yuvarāja!
body.translated_text: Then, exclaiming 'O wondrous ascetic woman! Wait, wait!' and drawing <s>Nāndīmukhī</s> aside, <s>Lalitā</s> smiled toward me: 'O bold and playful crown prince!'

body.text:
tataḥ paramānanda-sandohena mayā vicitya vicitya paramottama-mauktika-saṅcayaiḥ
sva-hastena vicitra-śilpa-kalpanayā rādhāṅga-pratyaṅgābharaṇāni viracayya
suvarṇa-sampuṭe nidhāya tan-nāma-mudrayā cihnitīkṛtya
lalitā-viśākhādi-sakhī-maṇḍalīnāṃ ca bhūṣaṇāni tathaiva nirmāya pṛthak pṛthak
sampuṭe nyasya tat-tan-nāma-mudrayā cihnitīkṛtya tathaivāgrathitāny apy
uttama-mauktikāni bahūni ca nāndīmukhyā saha
madhumaṅgala-subala-tat-kālāgatojjvala-vasanta-kokilādi-hastena
rādhā-kuṇḍa-nikuñja-mandire prahitāni |
body.translated_text: Then, with a flood of supreme bliss, I carefully selected choice collections of the finest pearls and with my own hand, through the art of variegated craftsmanship, fashioned ornaments for each of <s>Rādhā</s>'s limbs and sub-limbs, placed them in a golden casket, and marked it with a seal bearing her name. Likewise, I made ornaments for the circle of friends — <s>Lalitā</s>, <s>Viśākhā</s>, and the others — placed each set separately in caskets marked with seals bearing their respective names, and also many excellent strung pearls. These were sent to <s>Rādhā</s>'s bower-temple at <s>Rādhā-kuṇḍa</s> by the hands of <s>Nāndīmukhī</s> together with <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>, <s>Subala</s>, and <s>Ujjvala</s>, <s>Vasanta</s>, <s>Kokila</s>, and others who had arrived at that time.

body.text:
rādhayā smita-lalita-lalitā-viśākhādi-sakhībhiḥ samaṃ smita-śavalita-harṣeṇādāya
sādara-madhura-pracuratara-pakvānna-tāmbūla-vīṭikābhir madhumaṅgalaṃ
praṇaya-rūpa-gandha-candanair vara-tāmbūlaiś ca subalādikaṃ ca santoṣya
tad-dhastena
