sva-hasta-sampādita-surabhi-sukumārāruṇa-kusuma-vicitrita-kāñcana-yūthikā-m
ālya-karpūra-vāsita-tāmbūlopaḍhaukanena nirbharam ānandito'haṃ
praṇayādhikyena tan-mālya-bhūṣitas tat-tāmbūlam upayuñjānaḥ sakhībhiḥ saha
gosambhālanāya govardhanam āgataḥ |
body.translated_text: When <s>Rādhā</s>, together with the smiling <s>Lalitā</s>, <s>Viśākhā</s>, and the other friends, accepted them with delight suffused with smiles, they gratified <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> with affectionate, sweet, and abundant cooked food and betel-nut rolls, and gratified <s>Subala</s> and the others with loving sandalwood paste, fragrant as love itself, and excellent betel. Through his hand, the offering sent to me of a garland of golden jasmine adorned with fragrant, soft, reddish flowers prepared by her own hand and camphor-scented betel — I was overflowing with bliss, and adorned with that garland out of exceeding love, partaking of that betel, I went with my friends to <s>Govardhana</s> to tend the cattle.

body.text:
tataś ca svarṇa-sampuṭaṃ samudhghāṭya lalitā tad-alaṅkaraṇena sānandam
ānanditāṃ rādhāṃ prasādhayāmāsa |
body.translated_text: Then, opening the golden casket, <s>Lalitā</s> joyfully adorned and beautified the delighted <s>Rādhā</s> with those ornaments.

body.text:
tad anu lalitā-viśākhādayaḥ sakhyo'pi parasparaṃ tat-tat-sampuṭābharaṇenātmānaṃ
bhūṣayāmāsuḥ | tatas tāḥ sva-sva-gṛhe gatvā
tat-pracuratarādbhuta-mauktika-pradānena sva-sva-patiṃ sva-sva-gurūṃś ca paraṃ
santoṣya punar gāndharvā-saras-tīra-gāndharvā-sthānīm avāpya mitho
man-madhura-madhura-narma-vārtā-vinodena sukhaṃ vijahruḥ |
body.translated_text: After that, the friends — <s>Lalitā</s>, <s>Viśākhā</s>, and the others — also adorned themselves with the ornaments from their respective caskets. Then, going each to their own homes, they supremely delighted their respective husbands and elders by giving them those abundant, wondrous pearls. Then, returning to the <s>Gāndharvā</s>-place on the shore of <s>Gāndharvā</s>'s lake, they sported happily in mutual entertainment with my sweet, sweet playful conversation.

body.text: satyā - gokula-vilāsārāma-matta-kokila! tatas tataḥ ?
body.translated_text: <s>Satyā</s> (<s>Satyabhāmā</s>): 'O intoxicated cuckoo of the pleasure-garden of <s>Gokula</s>'s pastimes! Then what? Then what?'

body.text:
kṛṣṇaḥ - priye! śrutaṃ śrotavyam | tad alaṃ tad-ati-vārtayeti bruvann eva
tan-madhura-rahasya-keli-vṛttāntodghāṭana-vaikulyātiśayenādhairyaṃ -
body.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>: 'Beloved! What was to be heard has been heard. Enough of this excessive narrative.' — Even while speaking thus, overwhelmed by the agitation of revealing those sweet, secret amorous affairs —

children.translated_text: 'The necklace resplendent with clusters of jewels set in beautiful gold upon my neck,
the pair of gold ear-ornaments sparkling on my ears,
the supreme fragrant saffron ointment glistening upon my body — when, oh when

children.text: hāhā yāsyati dṛk-pathaṃ mama punaḥ puṇyair agaṇyair iha ||
children.translated_text: alas, alas, will that come again before my eyes, through immeasurable merit, here?'

body.text: iti kṣaṇaṃ maunam ālambya punaḥ sautsukyaṃ -
body.translated_text: Thus, pausing a moment in silence, then again with eager longing —

children.translated_text: 'This row of <s>campaka</s> flowers upon my chest, this pair of lotus-eyes of mine,
this sprinkling from the palace-terrace, this splendor gracing my every limb,
this creeper-perch of the great bird of my life-breath, this beauty that I desire,

children.text: maj-jīvātur iyaṃ mayā punar aho hā hā kadā lapsyate ||
children.translated_text: this very elixir of my life — alas, alas, when shall I obtain her again?'

body.text:
iti vilapan sāśru-dhāras tal-līlā-smaraṇa-vihvalaṃ bhūmau nipatya sa-śabdaṃ
rudantaṃ madhumaṅgalam āliṅgya tad anu - prāṇa-vallabhe! tvam eva jīvātu-rūpā
rādhāsīti sa-kampaṃ sa-gadgadaṃ lapan tāṃ satyāṃ pariṣvajya muhur muhur
dīrgham uṣṇaṃ ca uccair niśasann āsīt |
body.translated_text: Thus lamenting, with streams of tears, falling to the ground overwhelmed by the remembrance of those pastimes, embracing <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> who was weeping aloud — then [saying]: 'O beloved of my life! You yourself are <s>Rādhā</s>, the very form of my life-elixir!' — trembling and stammering, murmuring thus, he embraced that <s>Satyā</s> (<s>Satyabhāmā</s>) and, sighing deeply, heavily, and loudly again and again, sat still.

body.text:
satyabhāmā ca - sambhrameṇa sāśru-romāñcā nija-śāṭikāñcalena taṃ vījayantī
tūṣṇīm āsīt |
body.translated_text: And <s>Satyabhāmā</s> — in agitation, with tears and goosebumps, fanning him with the border of her garment — sat in silence.

body.text:
ity akhila-vṛttāntaṃ paurṇamāsī-śiṣyā samañjasā-mukhād ākarṇya saromāñcaṃ
sakautukaṃ savyathaṃ lakṣmaṇā prāha - sakhi samañjase! tatas tataḥ ?
body.translated_text: Having heard this entire account from the mouth of <s>Samañjasā</s>, the pupil of <s>Paurṇamāsī</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇā</s>, with goosebumps, with wonder, and with anguish, said: 'Friend <s>Samañjasā</s>! Then what? Then what?'

body.text:
samañjasā -- tataḥ prathamam atisambhrameṇa kṣaṇaṃ tūṣṇīṃ sthitvā tad anu -
prāṇanātha! nikhila-vraja-janaika-jīvana! jaya jaya dhairyam avalambasva dhairyam
avalambasva | samāśvāsīhi samāśvāsīhīti vaiyagrya-viśaṅkaṭa-dhvaniṃ
bhāṣamāṇayā muhur muhur vijanena mṛdu mṛdu madhurāṅga-mārjanena
gokula-gamanārtha-prārthanādibhir eva nija-jīvita-nāthaṃ śanaiḥ śanaiḥ
sandhukṣitīkṛtya nijānanta-sukha-sudhā-sindhūn nijānanta-prāṇa-parasparām api
tṛṇavad dhruvam anapekṣya sadā
cikīrṣita-nija-paramābhīṣṭa-tat-sukhābhāsa-lava-leśayā
tac-caraṇa-paṅkajaika-gatyā satyayā tadānīm eva sakhī-dvārā
tatrānīta-śrīmad-uddhava-mantri-rāja-sannirūpite samāgāmini paraśvo'hani
madhura-dadhyannādi-bhojanānantaraṃ
guru-dina-sita-daśamī-dhaniṣṭhābha-śubha-yoga-sambhāvita-vividha-guṇābhirā
jitābhijin-nāma-san-muhūrta-vare sarvato nairvighnyena jhaṭiti
samasta-praśasta-śastotpādana-puraḥsara-gokula-pura-praveśa-sampādayitrīṃ
parama-maṅgala-kulojjvalita-yātrāṃ vidhāya savinaya-nirbandhena
pūjya-caraṇa-śrīmad-agraja-mahānubhāvaṃ gokula-gamanārtham atyutkaṇṭhitayam
api dvārakā-purābhibhāvanārtham abhisaṃrakṣya tatrabhavatī
śrī-bhagavatī-pāda-padmān puro nidhāya sārdham uddhava-rohiṇīśvarībhyāṃ
sakala-maṅgalāliṅgito madhumaṅgalālaṅkṛtaḥ śrī-śrīmad-vraja-nava-yuvarājas
tat-kṣaṇād eva drutam itaś calitvā śrīmatā nandīghoṣa-rathena
śrī-gokulopaśalyam āsādya
pramada-sambhṛta-cintābhilaṣita-nijābhilaṣita-nijābhīra-śṛṅgāra-nikareṇāti-bhr
ājamānaḥ san śrīmati nija-vraja-pure śubha-praveśam avaśyaṃ kariṣyatīti
sudṛḍhaṃ sarva-sammatyā nirṇītam astīti
tat-pariveśita-madhura-samācāra-sudhāsāram ānandāsāra-samplutā
śravaṇa-caṣakaiḥ samācamya
parama-saubhāgyavatī-śiromaṇi-mañjarī-satyabhāmāsamakakṣa-paṭṭa-mahiṣī
sakala-sallakṣaṇa-guṇa-lakṣojjvalita-lakṣmaṇā sautsukyaṃ sālalāpa -- sakhi
samañjase! etan-madhura-rasa-vārtāśravaṇād atīva utkaṇṭhitāhaṃ
śrī-yādavendreṇa sārdhaṃ goṣṭhendra-goṣṭham avāpya
rādhā-sakhya-puṣpa-saurabhyenātmānaṃ vāsayitum abhilaṣāmi |
body.translated_text: <s>Samañjasā</s>: 'Then, at first with great flurry, she stood silent for a moment; then — "O lord of my life! O sole life of all the people of <s>Vraja</s>! Victory! Victory! Hold firm! Hold firm! Be consoled! Be consoled!" — speaking with a voice choked with the harsh tones of agitation, again and again, gently wiping his sweet limbs in private, softly entreating him for the journey to <s>Gokula</s> — by such means, gradually reviving the lord of her own life — disregarding her own infinite ocean of blissful nectar and even her own infinite life-essence as nothing more than a blade of grass — by <s>Satyā</s>, who has the lotus feet of her beloved as her sole refuge, ever desirous of the slightest semblance of happiness of her supremely desired beloved's pleasure — through the friends, at that very moment, the royal minister <s>Śrīmad Uddhava</s> was brought there and a reunion was arranged for the day after tomorrow. On that day, following a meal of sweet curd-rice and the like, at the auspicious conjunction of the <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s> constellation with the bright tenth day, on a heavy day, at the supremely excellent <s>muhūrta</s> called <s>Abhijit</s> — possessed of various auspicious qualities — arranging an entirely unobstructed, most auspicious, brilliantly resplendent procession to secure the entry into <s>Gokula</s>-city, preceded by the production of all auspicious implements; and with respectful insistence, having safeguarded the revered elder brother of great majesty — though himself extremely eager for the journey to <s>Gokula</s> — for the protection of <s>Dvārakā</s>-city; placing the lotus feet of the venerable <s>Śrī Bhagavatī</s> before him; together with <s>Uddhava</s> and <s>Rohiṇīśvarī</s>; embraced by all auspiciousness; adorned by <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> — the most blessed new prince of <s>Vraja</s>, setting forth swiftly from here, by the blessed chariot of <s>Nandīghoṣa</s>, arriving at the outskirts of <s>Śrī Gokula</s>, resplendent with the array of his own cherished adornments obtained through joyously cherished longings — he shall certainly make an auspicious entry into his own town of <s>Vraja</s>. Thus it has been firmly determined with the unanimous consent of all.' Having drunk with the cups of her ears this nectar-essence of sweet news served by her, flooded with waves of bliss, <s>Lakṣmaṇā</s> — the supreme crest-jewel of most fortunate women, equal in rank to <s>Satyabhāmā</s> as a chief queen, radiant with a multitude of auspicious marks and excellent qualities — spoke with eagerness: 'O friend <s>Samañjasā</s>! From hearing this sweet <s>rasa</s>-narrative, I am supremely eager. Together with <s>Śrī Yādavendra</s>, I desire to reach the dwelling of the lord of <s>Goṣṭha</s> and pervade myself with the fragrance of friendship with <s>Rādhā</s>.'

body.text: samañjasā - sakhi tathaiva sarvathā bhavatu bhavatyā iti |
body.translated_text: <s>Samañjasā</s>: 'O friend! May it indeed be so for you in every way.'

children.text: ādadānas tṛṇaṃ dantair idaṃ yāce punaḥ punaḥ |
children.translated_text: Taking grass between my teeth, I pray this again and again:
May I be the dust of the blessed <s>Rūpa</s>'s lotus feet, birth after birth. (1)
By me, whose intellect was awakened by the nectar of his command, these stories of pearls (<s>Muktā-caritra</s>)

children.text: gucchaḥ puṣpa-bharair vyadhāyi ya iha śrī-rūpa-saṃśikṣayā |
children.translated_text: were fashioned into a bouquet laden with flower-clusters, here, under <s>Śrī Rūpa</s>'s tutelage.
May the bee-like gaze of the one whose sole life is mine, known as <s>Jīva</s>,

children.text: ghrāṇais taṃ paribhūṣitaṃ na tanutāṃ tat-keli-śīdhūtka-dhīḥ ||2||
children.translated_text: adorn it by smelling it — he whose mind overflows with the nectar of those pastimes. (2)
This wondrous bouquet woven from the profusion of flowers of the <s>Muktā-caritra</s> (Story of Pearls) —
may the group of <s>Śrīmad Rūpa</s>, out of affection for me, privately wear it as an ear-ornament. (3)
By the strength of whose companionship, by me
this tale of the finest pearls was composed —
with that <s>Kṛṣṇa-kavi-bhūpati</s> in <s>Vraja</s>,
may I have association birth after birth. (4)
